title: Windows: pending Bun.stdin.text() no longer keeps the event loop alive after module evaluation (regression in 1.4.0, worked in 1.3.11–1.3.14)
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (also reproduced on 1.4.0 and 1.4.1)

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64 (Windows 11 Pro)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`repro.ts`:

```ts
process.on("exit", (code) =>
  console.error("exit", code, "bun", Bun.version, process.platform)
);

async function main() {
  const text = await Bun.stdin.text();
  console.log("read:", JSON.stringify(text));
}

main();
```

```
printf 'hello\n' | bun run repro.ts
```

The same happens with a file redirect (`bun run repro.ts < in.txt`) and with a parent that spawns the script with `stdin: "pipe"` and writes to it two seconds later — the child exits before the data arrives.

### What is the expected behavior?

```
read: "hello\n"
exit 0 bun 1.4.2 win32
```

This is what Linux prints on 1.4.0, and what Windows prints on 1.3.11 through 1.3.14.

### What do you see instead?

```
exit 0 bun 1.4.2 win32
```

The process exits 0 without the `read:` line: the pending `Bun.stdin.text()` read does not keep the event loop alive once module evaluation has finished, so the promise never settles.

### Additional information

Bisect on Windows x64 (same script, `printf 'hello\n' | bun run repro.ts`, 3–5 runs each, fully deterministic):

| Bun                    | result               |
| ---------------------- | -------------------- |
| 1.3.9, 1.3.10          | exits before reading |
| 1.3.11, 1.3.13, 1.3.14 | reads correctly      |
| 1.4.0, 1.4.1, 1.4.2    | exits before reading |

The v1.3.11 release notes list "Fixed: `Bun.file().text()` and similar async read methods not keeping event loop alive", which matches the window in which it worked; 1.4.0 appears to have regressed that fix on Windows. Linux 1.4.0 is unaffected.

Two details that narrow it down:

- A top-level `await Bun.stdin.text()` works on every version. Only a read awaited after module evaluation has completed (a floating `main()`, a Commander action, a `.then()` chain) is affected.
- Adding any other ref'd handle — a `setInterval`, a `process.on("beforeExit")` listener, or reading through `process.stdin` async iteration instead — makes the read complete, so the data path is fine; only the keep-alive accounting is missing.

Real-world impact: a git credential helper written in Bun (`git` spawns it with the request on a pipe and waits for stdout) silently answers nothing, so every authenticated clone fails with `could not read Username`. That is how we found it: https://github.com/archgate/cli/pull/604

title: Event loop spins at 100% CPU in userspace, never re-enters kevent, rebuilding the HTTP Date header after a unix-socket peer vanishes (macOS ARM64, 1.3.14)
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14 (Homebrew `oven-sh/bun/bun`, `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/bun/1.3.14/bin/bun`)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 (macOS 15.7.5, Apple Silicon)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

No minimal reproduction yet. This is a long-running daemon that ran fine for 7 days and then spun forever after one specific network event. Fresh-process attempts to trigger the same event do not spin (details below), so it seems to need accumulated state.

The app is the `bridge/index.ts` daemon from https://github.com/AltanS/collie, run under launchd. It uses:

- `Bun.serve` on `127.0.0.1:8787`
- `Bun.connect({ unix })` for short-lived newline-JSON RPCs: 3 in parallel every 1.5 s, each with a 5 s `setTimeout` that calls `socket.end()`, or ends the socket in `.then()` of the connect promise if the timeout fired before `open`
- one long-lived `Bun.connect({ unix })` event stream that gets closed and re-dialed often (hundreds of times over the week, on subscription changes)
- a few `setInterval` timers, some `unref()`ed

Timeline:

1. Aug 17: process starts. Normal for 7 days.
2. Aug 24: the unix socket server it talks to stopped accepting connections while the long-lived stream socket was still open.
3. The next `Bun.connect` rejected with `Failed to connect`. The app logged that line. It is the last line it ever logged.
4. From that moment no JS ran again: the stream socket's `close` handler never fired (its peer is gone per `lsof`), all timers stopped, `Bun.serve` stopped answering (`curl` times out), and the main thread spun at 100% CPU for 13 days until I killed it with SIGKILL. SIGTERM had no effect because the `process.on("SIGTERM")` handler never ran.

Tried and could not reproduce in a fresh process on 1.3.14 (each run 12 to 30 s, CPU stayed at ~0.1%):

1. `Bun.connect({ unix })` to a missing path every 1.5 s
2. same, to a stale socket file with no listener
3. the full app against a fake unix server, server killed with SIGTERM and with SIGKILL mid-session
4. the full app with the socket file unlinked while the server stayed alive, so dials fail while the stream stays open (this reproduces the exact log ordering of the real incident: "poll failed" with no preceding stream-close line)

### What is the expected behavior?

A failed `Bun.connect` rejects its promise and the event loop goes back to waiting in `kevent`.

### What do you see instead?

Process state while hung (via `ps`, `top -l 3 -s 2`, `lsof`):

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| `%CPU` | 99 |
| user time | 12027 min (over ~13 days; sleep time excluded) |
| BSD syscalls | +7 per 2 s |
| Mach syscalls | +0 per 2 s |
| context switches | ~150 to 300 per s (preemption only) |
| RSS | 720 KB, 35 MB compressed |
| `127.0.0.1:8787` | still LISTEN in `lsof`, `curl -m 3` times out |
| worker threads | all idle in `__ulock_wait2` |

`sample 75828 3` (1 ms interval, 2205 samples): the main thread is never in `kevent64`. Every sample is inside the bun binary itself, no JIT frames, so no JS is on the stack. About 85% of samples are in one small function that calls `time()`, then `gmtime_r()` (which shows up as `gmtsub` and `notify_check_tz`), then `snprintf()` with `%s` and integer arguments. That matches uWebSockets `LoopData::updateDate()`, i.e. the loop is rebuilding the HTTP `Date:` header on every iteration and never blocking. The caller chain is a stable 11-frame stack from `start`, with the loop around frame `bun + 0x117ff70` calling `bun + 0xfcb5fc` calling `bun + 0x12c5adc`, which also touches `pthread_rwlock_rdlock/unlock` on each pass.

Main-thread call graph (libsystem_notify internals under `notify_check` collapsed):

<details>
<summary>sample excerpt</summary>

```
Call graph:
    2205 Thread_76134769   DispatchQueue_1: com.apple.main-thread  (serial)
    + 2205 start  (in dyld) + 6076  [0x19dcc6b98]
    +   2205 ???  (in bun)  load address 0x102908000 + 0x9bdd0c  [0x1032c5d0c]
    +     2205 ???  (in bun)  load address 0

Bun 1.4.1 bundler renames two identifiers to the same name, emitting illegal "var Check2 = Check2" that Bun's own runtime rejects
body:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.1 (also reproduced with the exact `oven/bun:1.4.1-alpine` image)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (Alpine, docker `oven/bun:1.4.1-alpine`)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Minimal repro repo: **https://github.com/vlrdimir/bun-1.4.1-var-shadow-repro**

`repro.js`:

```js
import { t } from "elysia";
const schema = t.Object({ name: t.String() });
console.log("bundle parsed and ran, schema:", typeof schema);
```

Bundle and run with bun 1.4.1:

```sh
bun install
bun build repro.js --outdir=dist --target=bun
bun dist/repro.js
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The bundle produced by `bun build` should be parseable and runnable — as it is with bun 1.4.0, which outputs `bundle parsed and ran, schema: object` for the same input.

### What do you see instead?

Bun 1.4.1's runtime rejects the bundle Bun 1.4.1's bundler just produced:

```
SyntaxError: Cannot declare a var variable that shadows a let/const/class variable: 'Check2'.

Bun v1.4.1 (Linux x64)
```

### Additional information

The 1.4.1 bundler renames **two distinct identifiers to the same name**. Source is `elysia@1.4.29` `dist/schema.mjs:283`, which legitimately aliases:

```js
let Check = function(value, validated = false) { ... };
// ...
var Check2 = Check, runCheckers = runCheckers2, mergeValues = mergeValues2;
```

Bun 1.4.1's bundle output collapses both `Check` and `Check2` into `Check2`, emitting an illegal same-scope `let`/`var` collision (and TDZ self-reference):

```js
let Check2 = function(value, validated = false) { ... };
// ...
var Check2 = Check2, runCheckers = runCheckers2, mergeValues = mergeValues2;
```

Bun 1.4.0 bundling the identical input renames correctly (`Check` -> `Check22`):

```js
var Check2 = Check22, runCheckers = runCheckers2, mergeValues = mergeValues2;
```

and that 1.4.0 output runs fine on **both** the 1.4.0 and 1.4.1 runtimes — so this looks like a regression in the 1.4.1 bundler's identifier renaming, not in the parser (the parser is right to reject it).

Real-world impact: any app bundling `elysia` (we're on elysia 1.4.29, zod 4.4.3, `--target=bun`) fails at startup after deploying a 1.4.1-built bundle. We hit this in production because our Dockerfiles use the floating `oven/bun:1.4` tag, which moved from 1.4.0 to 1.4.1 today; we've pinned back to 1.4.0 as a workaround.

Repro repo with bundle excerpts for both versions: https://github.com/vlrdimir/bun-1.4.1-var-shadow-repro

title: [Bug]: Missing minimumReleaseAge prompt when initializing Storybook with pnpm 12
body:
### Describe the bug

When the Storybook CLI is already cached from another project, `pnpm create storybook` starts in a project with `minimumReleaseAge` configured, but does not show the prompt to exclude Storybook packages or use an older release.

It generates configuration files and updates `package.json`, then dependency installation fails because of the waiting period, leaving the project partially initialized.

### Reproduction link

...

### Reproduction steps

1. Use pnpm 12.4.2.
2. In project A, without a custom minimum release age, run:
   ```bash
   pnpm create storybook@10.6.0
   ```
   This downloads and caches the CLI.
3. In project B, an existing React + Vite project, configure `minimumReleaseAge` to exceed the age of Storybook 10.6.0. Do not add Storybook exclusions.
4. Using the same environment while the CLI cache is still valid, run:
   ```bash
   pnpm create storybook@10.6.0
   ```
5. Complete the initialization prompts. No minimum-release-age prompt appears, and dependency installation fails.

Expected: show the waiting-period prompt before generating files or updating dependencies.

### System

```bash
npm: 12.0.0 - /home/.nvm/versions/node/v24.15.0/bin/npm
pnpm: 12.4.2 - /home/.nvm/versions/node/v24.15.0/bin/pnpm
```

title: [Bug]: pseudo-states - negated pseudo-class selectors (:not(:hover)) are permanently matched, hiding elements even during real interaction
body:
### Describe the bug

A common CSS pattern for "reveal on hover/focus" elements uses a negated pseudo-class to hide by default:

```
.parent:not(:hover):not(:focus-visible) .icon {
  visibility: hidden;
  pointer-events: none;
}
```
  This works correctly in every real browser and in production builds. With
  storybook-addon-pseudo-states registered, however, the element never becomes visible on a real 
  mouse hover inside Storybook.

  ### Environment

  - storybook-addon-pseudo-states: 10.5.7 (also reproduced on 10.5.5)
  - storybook: 10.6

### Reproduction link

Storybook.new is down and I can't create the env.

### Reproduction steps

  ### Reproduction

  1. Register storybook-addon-pseudo-states in main.js addons.
  2. Add a component with:
```
  .row:not(:hover) .action-icon {
    display: none;
  }
```
  3. Render it in a plain story.
  4. Hover .row with a real mouse.

*Expected:* .action-icon becomes visible (matches production behavior).
 *Actual:* .action-icon stays hidden. document.querySelector('.row').matches(':hover') returns true,
  but the computed display on .action-icon remains none.

### System

```bash
│  OS: macOS 26.6.2
│  CPU: (15) arm64 Apple M5 Pro
│  Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh
│  Binaries:
│  Node: 24.18.0
│  Yarn: 4.14.1
│  npm: 11.16.0
```

### Additional context

### AI Investigation 

#### Root cause

  The addon rewrites every stylesheet on every STORY_RENDERED/GLOBALS_UPDATED/etc. event,
  unconditionally, regardless of whether pseudo-forcing is actually active for the current story.
  Any selector containing a pseudo-class gets a class-based fallback appended so it can be forced
  without a real interaction. For the rule above, the rewritten CSS (from
  rewriteNotSelectors/rewriteRule) becomes roughly:

```
  .parent:not(:hover):not(:focus-visible) .icon,
  .parent:not(.pseudo-hover):not(.pseudo-focus-visible) .icon {
    visibility: hidden;
    pointer-events: none;
  }
```
  These two selectors are OR'd in the same rule. .pseudo-hover / .pseudo-focus-visible are classes
  that only exist when a state is explicitly forced — they are absent during normal, real 
  interaction. That means :not(.pseudo-hover):not(.pseudo-focus-visible) is always true whenever
  pseudo-forcing isn't active, so the second selector always matches and always applies visibility:
  hidden, permanently overriding the real :not(:hover) clause even while genuinely hovering.

  ### AI Suggested fix

  Only run the stylesheet rewrite/apply the transform when pseudo-forcing is actually active for
  the current story (toolbar global set, or parameters.pseudo present), rather than unconditionally
  on every render. Alternatively, when rewriting a :not(:pseudo-class) selector, scope the
  class-based fallback so it can only match while some pseudo state is currently being forced (e.g.
  under a root marker class), instead of making the negation trivially always-true whenever
  nothing is forced.

title: Canary PR body update fails when the pull request description has no CANARY_RELEASE markers
body:
This is about repository CI, not about a Storybook project, so the bug report template does not fit: there is no reproduction link to give and `npx storybook@latest info` says nothing useful here. Everything below is read from `next` and can be checked from the files.

## What is wrong

`publish-canary-pr-body.yml` patches the PR description through two marker pairs, `CANARY_RELEASE_HEADING` and `CANARY_RELEASE_SECTION`. `replaceMarker` in `.github/scripts/replace-pr-body-markers.ts` throws when a pair is missing:

```js
if (matches?.length !== 1) {
  throw new Error(`expected 1 ${marker} pair, found ${matches?.length ?? 0}`);
}
```

`applyCanaryPrBodyUpdate` calls it without a guard, and `main()` in `update-canary-pr-body-from-run.ts` does not catch. So for a pull request whose description does not carry those markers, the packages publish to pkg.pr.new normally and then the `Update Canary PR Body` job fails with `expected 1 CANARY_RELEASE_HEADING pair, found 0`. The install commands never reach the pull request, and the maintainer who asked for the canary sees a red job instead.

A description loses the markers whenever the author replaces the template rather than filling it in. That is not rare, and it is invisible until a canary is requested, because nothing else in CI reads those markers.

## The failure path loses more than the body

In `updateCanaryPrBodyFromRun` the order is: build the new body, patch the pull request, then comment. For `action: 'failed'` the throw happens in the first step, before this:

```js
if (decision.action === 'failed') {
  gh(['pr', 'comment', ...buildFailureComment(...)]);
}
```

So when a canary publish fails **and** the description has no markers, the comment that was meant to tell the actor about the failure is not posted either. The information that something broke is lost twice.

## What I have not verified

This is read from source, not observed. The mechanism is two days old: across the runs of `publish-canary-pr-body.yml` so far there are 99 `skipped` and 1 `success`, and no failure yet, so this path has not fired in practice. The current `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` does contain both marker pairs, so a description that keeps the template is fine. There is also no test for a body without markers in `update-canary-pr-body-from-run.test.ts`.

I noticed it because `ci:canary` was put on #36155, whose description does not carry the markers. That pull request is from a fork, so by the design in `publish-canary.yml` the label alone cannot publish it and a `workflow_dispatch` with the `pr` input is needed. If that dispatch is run against it as it stands, this is what will happen.

## Suggested fix

1. Treat a missing marker pair as a no-op in the canary path, with a log line, instead of an error. `replaceMarker` itself should stay strict, because `replace-pr-body-markers.ts` is a CLI where a missing marker really is a mistake; the tolerance belongs at the call site in `applyCanaryPrBodyUpdate`.
2. Post the failure comment before patching the body, so a body problem cannot swallow the failure notice.
3. Add a case to `update-canary-pr-body-from-run.test.ts` for a description without markers.

I can open the pull request for this if you want it. If you would rather the canary path required the markers and told the maintainer that the description is missing them, that also works and I am happy to write it that way instead.

title: [Bug]: CLI rejects every Node.js prerelease build
body:
### Describe the bug

The Storybook CLI can't tell prerelease Node builds from old ones, and it's blocking `storybook info` when it shouldn't.

The bug is in how the CLI checks your Node version. In [`code/core/src/bin/dispatcher.ts`](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/next/code/core/src/bin/dispatcher.ts), it takes `process.versions.node`, splits it on the dots, and converts each piece to a number:

```js
const [major, minor, patch] = process.versions.node.split('.').map(Number);
return satisfies(`${major}.${minor}.${patch}`, supportedRange);
```

Checked against Storybook's supported range (`>=20.19.0 <22.0.0 || >=22.12.0`), here's what that produces on various Node versions:

```
"18.20.4"                       => [18, 20, 4]    => false   (too old, correctly rejected)
"20.11.1"                       => [20, 11, 1]    => false   (below 20.19.0, correctly rejected)
"20.19.0"                       => [20, 19, 0]    => true    (correctly accepted)
"20.20.2"                       => [20, 20, 2]    => true    (correctly accepted)
"22.9.0"                        => [22, 9, 0]     => false   (below 22.12.0, correctly rejected)
"22.22.2"                       => [22, 22, 2]    => true    (correctly accepted)
"24.15.0"                       => [24, 15, 0]    => true    (correctly accepted)
"26.1.0"                        => [26, 1, 0]     => true    (correctly accepted)
"26.1.0-rc.0"                   => [26, 1, NaN]   => false   (misfire: should be true)
"24.15.0-nightly20260415abcdef" => [24, 15, NaN]  => false   (misfire: should be true)
"27.0.0-alpha.1"                => [27, 0, NaN]   => false   (misfire: should be true)
```

Any version with a tag after the patch number turns that number into `NaN`. The rebuilt version string becomes unparseable by semver, `satisfies()` returns false, and the CLI reports a perfectly supported Node version as too old.

Since this check runs before `run()` is even defined, it applies to every subcommand, including `storybook info`. On an affected machine, there's no way to run that command to generate the debug output this issue asks for.

### Reproduction link

https://github.com/Xevion/storybook-repro-version-parsing

### Reproduction steps

1. `git clone`
2. Build with Docker. The bug is demonstrateable with no components or code, so, the repository is just the Dockerfile.

```
docker build -t sb-node-prerelease .
docker run --rm sb-node-prerelease
```

Alternatively, you can test on Linux in just a few seconds by pasting these commands. 

```sh
curl -sSLO https://nodejs.org/download/rc/v26.1.0-rc.0/node-v26.1.0-rc.0-linux-x64.tar.xz
tar xf node-v26.1.0-rc.0-linux-x64.tar.xz
PATH="$PWD/node-v26.1.0-rc.0-linux-x64/bin:$PATH" npx -y storybook@latest info
# rm -rf ./node-v26.1.0-rc.0-linux-x64{/,.tar.xz}

title: Addon MCP: composed refs are silently dropped from MCP composition (trailing slash, invalid manifest, unreachable ref)
body:
## Problem Statement

When a user composes a hosted Storybook into their project via `refs`, the composed Storybook shows up in the Storybook UI but can be entirely invisible to the MCP docs tools (`docs-list`, `docs-show`, `docs-show-story`). There is no error, no log line, and no indication anywhere of why: the MCP server simply boots in single-source (local-only) mode. Agents then report that composed sources "are not in the MCP catalog", and users cannot tell whether the cause is their config, the ref's build, a version mismatch, or a network failure.

Several distinct root causes all funnel into this one silent outcome:

1. **URL normalization divergence.** The manager UI normalizes ref URLs (strips trailing slashes) before use, but the MCP addon reads the raw `refs` preset value. A ref URL with a trailing slash produces a double-slash manifest probe (`https://host//manifests/components.json`), which hosts like Chromatic's CDN 404. The ref is then classified as having no manifest and dropped. Reproduced empirically: the same URL works without the trailing slash and fails with it, while the UI works with both.
2. **Invalid manifest is indistinguishable from missing manifest.** A ref whose `components.json` response fails schema validation is classified identically to a 404 and silently dropped. This bucket itself hides two very different situations: a host with SPA fallback rewrites returning 200 with an HTML page for a manifest that does not exist, versus a real JSON manifest in a newer format than the local reader understands (e.g. an older reader composing a Storybook that publishes the v1 split/`$ref` manifest format).
3. **No diagnostics.** The "no manifest" classification is a bare skip with no logging, so all of the above — plus a transient network failure at dev-server boot — present identically as "composition just isn't there".

A related divergence: the MCP addon also ignores the `disable` flag on refs, so a ref disabled for the UI would still be composed into MCP.

## Solution

The MCP addon treats refs the same way the UI does, and says what it is doing:

- Ref URLs are normalized (trailing slash stripped) before any manifest probe or fetch, so a ref that works in the UI also works in MCP composition.
- Refs with `disable: true` are excluded from MCP composition, matching the UI.
- When a ref is skipped at boot, a warning names the ref and the precise reason:
  - **Manifest not found** — a 404/non-OK response, *or* a 200 response whose body is not JSON (SPA fallback pages land here, not in the mismatch bucket). Hint: enable `componentsManifest` on the ref's Storybook.
  - **Manifest failed validation** — a 200 response with valid JSON that fails the manifest schema. Hint: this usually means a version mismatch between the composed Storybook and the local addon; upgrade the older side.
  - **Ref unreachable** — a network error. Hint: the check runs at dev-server boot; restart once the ref is reachable.
- When a ref is accepted, the existing sources log line continues to confirm it.

## User Stories

1. As a Storybook user composing a hosted Storybook via `refs`, I want a ref URL with a trailing slash to work in MCP composition, so that the MCP tools see the same refs the UI shows.
2. As a Storybook user, I want MCP composition and UI composition to interpret my `refs` config identically, so that "it shows in the sidebar" implies "the MCP docs tools can see it" whenever the ref publishes manifests.
3. As a Storybook user with a ref marked `disable: true`, I want that ref excluded from MCP composition, so that disabling a ref means it is disabled everywhere.
4. As a Storybook user whose composed ref has no components manifest, I want a dev-server warning naming the ref and saying the manifest was not found (with a hint to enable the manifest feature on that Storybook), so that I know the fix is on the ref's side.
5. As a Storybook user whose ref is hosted with SPA fallback rewrites (a 200 HTML page where the manif

title: [Bug]: action events are logged twice — but only after navigating away from and back to a story — for any non-implicit `action()` invoked directly
body:
### Describe the bug

**The duplicate does not appear on a story's first render.** A fresh page load followed by a single interaction logs the action correctly, exactly once. The duplicate only appears starting with the *second* render of the same story — for example, after navigating to a different story and back, or after using the "Remount component" toolbar action. Once triggered, every subsequent interaction on that story instance logs the action twice, consistently (it does not escalate to 3x, 4x, etc. on further interactions) — until the story is freshly reloaded.

We are also **not** manually calling `action()` or manually configuring `argTypes.<name>.action` anywhere in our stories. In our case (using `@storybook/angular`), the entire chain that produces a non-implicit `action()` is automatic:

1. `@storybook/angular`'s built-in `argTypesEnhancer` inspects component metadata and, for every property it classifies as an `@Output`, automatically sets `argTypes.<name>.action = <name>` (`@storybook/angular`'s `dist/client/config.js`: `action = section === "outputs" ? { action: item.name } : {}`). No story-author input.
2. Storybook core's `addActionsFromArgTypes` argsEnhancer sees that `.action` and creates a real `action(name)` function on `args.<name>`. Also automatic.
3. `@storybook/angular`'s `argsToTemplate()` helper decides whether to render an Angular property binding or event binding purely by checking `typeof args[key] === 'function'`. Since `args.<name>` is now a function, it renders an event binding: `(name)="name($event)"`. Also automatic — the story only calls `argsToTemplate(args)` once, with no per-output configuration.

So an ordinary component output, with zero action-related code written by the story author, ends up bound to a Storybook-managed `action()` that Storybook itself wraps in a spy (see Root Cause below). We believe the root cause is generic to `storybook` core and not specific to `@storybook/angular`, but our confirmed reproduction below uses `@storybook/angular` since that's where we encountered it; we have not verified whether the "second render" trigger reproduces with other renderers or with a manually-configured `action()`.

When the duplicate is present, the two logged entries have **different payload shapes**:

1. An array-wrapped payload, e.g. `[event]` — logged via the global `onMockCall` listener that `logActionsWhenMockCalled` registers.
2. The correctly-shaped raw payload, e.g. `event` — logged via the action's own direct emission.

Both emissions happen synchronously, back-to-back, within the same call — this is not a timing race.

### Reproduction link

Blocked by firewall -- see below

### Reproduction steps

Using `@storybook/angular` (9.1.20), with a component library where an Angular `@Output` is auto-detected and turned into an action by the mechanism above (no explicit action config in the story):

```ts
// widget.stories.ts
export default {
  title: 'Example/Widget',
  component: WidgetComponent,
} as Meta<WidgetComponent>;

export const Interactive: StoryObj<WidgetComponent> = {
  render: (args) => ({
    props: args,
    template: `<my-widget ${argsToTemplate(args)}></my-widget>`,
  }),
};
```

Where `WidgetComponent` has a plain `@Output() change = new EventEmitter<any>();` with no story-level action configuration of any kind.

Steps:
1. Open the `Interactive` story fresh (hard reload).
2. Trigger the component's `change` output once (e.g. click a control that emits it).
3. Check the Actions panel: **exactly one** `change` entry is logged, with the correct raw payload. ✅ Correct so far.
4. Navigate to a different story, then navigate back to `Interactive`.
5. Trigger the `change` output again.
6. Check the Actions panel: **two** `change` entries are now logged for the single interaction — one array-wrapped, one raw. ❌ Bug.
7. Trigger the output again (without navigating away): still exactly two entries per interaction, consistently — it does not get worse with repeated i

title: [Bug]: a `getAbsolutePath`-wrapped addon resolves by directory, which bypasses its exports map
body:
### Describe the bug

`getAbsolutePath` converts a package **specifier** into a filesystem **directory**:

```ts
const getAbsolutePath = (packageName) =>
  dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.resolve(`${packageName}/package.json`)));
```

`resolveAddonName` then reaches an addon's entry points by joining onto whatever it was given:

```ts
// core/src/common/presets.ts:82
const presetFile  = safeResolveModule({ specifier: join(name, 'preset'),  parent: configDir });
const managerFile = safeResolveModule({ specifier: join(name, 'manager'), parent: configDir });
const previewFile = safeResolveModule({ specifier: join(name, 'preview'), parent: configDir });

if (managerFile || previewFile || presetFile) { ... }
```

Those two do not compose:

| `name` | `join(name, 'preset')` | resolved how |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@storybook/addon-designs` | `@storybook/addon-designs/preset` | through the package's `exports` map |
| `/abs/path/node_modules/@storybook/addon-designs` | `/abs/path/.../addon-designs/preset` | as a filesystem path, **`exports` bypassed** |

So the moment an addon is written as `getAbsolutePath(...)`, its exports map stops being consulted. If the package does not also happen to have a real `preset.js` file sitting at its root, all three lookups miss, the `if` falls through, and the addon is dropped:

```
▲  Could not resolve addon "/…/node_modules/@storybook/addon-designs", skipping. Is it installed?
```

It is installed, at exactly that path. `@storybook/addon-designs@11` ships an exports map and no root-level shims. Unwrapping that one entry back to the bare specifier takes the message count from 1 to 0.

The message is also wrong twice over: it prints a path we generated rather than the specifier the user wrote, and it asks whether a package that is installed is installed.

### Reproduction link

https://github.com/gravitee-io/gravitee-ui-particles

### Reproduction steps

Its committed `.storybook/main.ts` line 11 is the trigger:

```ts
addons: ['@storybook/addon-a11y', '@storybook/addon-designs', '@storybook/addon-docs'],
```

1. Clone it and run `storybook upgrade`, or `storybook automigrate wrap-require`.
2. The addons come back wrapped: `getAbsolutePath("@storybook/addon-designs")`.
3. Start Storybook. `Could not resolve addon "/…/node_modules/@storybook/addon-designs", skipping.` The addon does nothing from then on.
4. Change that one entry back to the bare `'@storybook/addon-designs'`. The message goes away and the addon works.

Nothing else in the config needs to change, which isolates it to the wrapping.

### System

```bash
Not from `npx storybook info`: mechanism verified against a local build of `next` @ fda4d712195.

  Affected: core/src/common/presets.ts (resolveAddonName), reached via any wrapped addon
  Not framework-specific.
```

### Additional context

**This is not only an automigration artifact. We document the pattern.** `docs/_snippets/storybook-main-pnpm-with-module-resolution.md` recommends it for pnpm and monorepos, with the addons array called out explicitly:

```js
addons: [
  //👇 Use getAbsolutePath when referencing Storybook's addons and frameworks
  getAbsolutePath('@storybook/addon-docs'),
],
```

So the population is anyone on pnpm or in a monorepo who followed our own guidance, plus everyone the `wrap-require` automigration has touched. It also reaches `storybook add`, which wraps through `setup-addon-in-config.ts`.

**Why we have never hit this ourselves.** Our own addons ship *both* an exports map and redundant root-level shim files:

```
addons/a11y:    preset.js  manager.js      exports: ['.', './manager', './package.json',
addons/docs:    preset.js  manager.js                './postinstall', './preset', './preview']
addons/vitest:  preset.js  manager.js
```

`<dir>/preset` therefore always lands on a shim for a first-party addon, and the bypass is invisible. Only a third-party addon shipping an exports map alone exposes it, which is simply what a modern package looks like. This

title: [Bug]: Vite builder: dev does not resolve tsconfig compilerOptions.paths while build does - every Vite framework, not just Angular
body:
### Describe the bug

## The asymmetry

Vite resolves `compilerOptions.paths` in `build` but not in `dev`, and Storybook never turns the dev-side switch on.

* `resolve.tsconfigPaths` defaults to `false` (`vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js`, `configDefaults`).
* In **dev**, both `vite:import-analysis` and the dependency scanner go through Vite's JS resolver, which only reads tsconfig when that flag is on.
* In **build**, Vite hands resolution to rolldown. `resolveRolldownOptions` does not pass `tsconfig`, so rolldown's native resolver falls back to its default: auto-detect the nearest `tsconfig.json` and apply its `paths`.

So a workspace builds green and then cannot serve a single module importing one of its own aliases. Users conclude the migration worked from a passing build and hit a wall in dev.

## Minimal proof, no Storybook and no Angular involved

One `tsconfig.json` with `"@lib/foo": ["src/lib/foo.ts"]`, default config, Vite 8.2.0:

```
### A) baseline build (resolve.tsconfigPaths default false)
✓ built in 18ms                        # dist contains RESOLVED_VIA_TSCONFIG_PATHS

### B) build with build.rolldownOptions.tsconfig=false
error during build:
Error: [vite]: Rolldown failed to resolve import "@lib/foo" from ".../src/main.ts".

### C) build with tsconfig.json renamed away
Error: [vite]: Rolldown failed to resolve import "@lib/foo" from ".../src/main.ts".
```

Same project, `vite dev`, same default config:

```
"message":"Failed to resolve import \"@lib/foo\" from \"src/main.ts\". Does the file exist?"
"plugin":"vite:import-analysis"
```

B and C isolate it: the build's resolution comes from rolldown's tsconfig auto-detection, and nothing feeds that to dev.

## Scope

`@storybook/angular-vite` now sets `resolve: { tsconfigPaths: config.resolve?.tsconfigPaths ?? true }` in its `viteFinal`, because it declares `vite: ">=8.0.0"` so the key always exists. Every other Vite framework has the same split today: `react-vite`, `vue3-vite`, `svelte-vite`, `html-vite`, `web-components-vite`, `preact-vite`. `vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs` already sets `tsconfigPaths: true` on Vite 8, so the Angular change matches existing in-repo precedent rather than inventing one.

The framework-agnostic home is `@storybook/builder-vite`. What blocks moving it there: builder-vite still resolves the repo-root `vite@7.3.6`, where `resolve.tsconfigPaths` does not exist, so it needs a version guard or a dependency bump first.

## Related infrastructure problem

In-monorepo sandboxes cannot exercise this at all. `@storybook/builder-vite` resolves the repo-root `vite@7.3.6` while `angular-vite` has a nested `vite@8.0.16`, so a sandbox linked to the repo runs its dev server on Vite 7 - a major the framework does not ship against. Worth its own fix; otherwise angular-vite e2e never runs on the Vite major it actually targets.

## Docs

Any guidance telling Vite users to recreate their tsconfig paths as `resolve.alias` entries in `viteFinal` is obsolete for Vite 8 projects once this lands. Not audited yet.

---

## Correction: the root cause above is only half right

An adversarial review caught this, and I reproduced it against the exact Vite copy the package resolves (`8.0.16` at `code/frameworks/angular-vite/node_modules/vite`).

**Build is not neutral to** `resolve.tsconfigPaths`**.** It consults `compilerOptions.paths` as a *fallback*, after normal resolution fails - which is why the probe above (a paths entry with no `node_modules` candidate) resolved at build time with the flag off. When a specifier resolves **both** ways, the flag flips precedence:

| `resolve.tsconfigPaths` | build resolves `lodash-es` to |
| -- | -- |
| unset | `node_modules` |
| `false` | `node_modules` |
| `true` | the tsconfig target (`local/lodash-es.ts`) |

So the statement "build resolves `compilerOptions.paths` whatever this is set to" is false in exactly the case that matters, and turning the flag on **changes production bundle contents**, not just dev behaviour. `buil

title: [Bug]: ACM - Components imported from built packages (.d.ts)
body:
### Describe the bug

When stories import a component through its built package rather than its source, ACM analyses the emitted .d.ts, where inputs and outputs survive only as plain fields plus the `ɵɵComponentDeclaration` generic - so ACM's decorator- and signal-based detection sees nothing and the props table empties out.

Compodoc does not have this problem: it scans sources by class name regardless of what the story imported.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a story importing a component from a package's built output, when the component is extracted, then its inputs and outputs are read from the ɵɵComponentDeclaration type parameters, including their public binding names.
- Given a component available in both source and built form, when it is extracted, then the source is preferred and the .d.ts path is the fallback, never the other way round.
- Given a .d.ts-sourced component, when its members are listed, then underscore-internal and framework-emitted members do not leak into the props table.

title: Sandbox: `@storybook/addon-mcp` ends up twice in the generated main.ts addons array
body:
### Describe the bug

A freshly generated sandbox (`yarn task sandbox --template react-vite/default-ts`) lists `@storybook/addon-mcp` twice in `.storybook/main.ts`:

```ts
addons: [
  "@chromatic-com/storybook",
  "@storybook/addon-vitest",
  "@storybook/addon-a11y",
  "@storybook/addon-docs",
  "@storybook/addon-mcp",
  "@storybook/addon-mcp",
],
```

Likely cause: `create-storybook` init already appends `@storybook/addon-mcp` (`code/lib/create-storybook/src/services/AddonService.ts`), and the sandbox task's extra-addons step appends it again without deduplicating against what init wrote.

### Impact

Cosmetic but visible to agent tooling: `npx storybook skills get setup` renders the addon twice in its Project Info table, and anything that assumes unique addon entries sees a duplicate. Also worth checking that user-facing `npx storybook add @storybook/addon-mcp` is a no-op when the addon is already registered, since the plugin skills instruct agents to install it when missing.

### Environment

- `next` @ 10.6.0-alpha.6, macOS
- Found while QA'ing Milestone 7 of #35526

title: Tools CLI: `--json` output is unparseable when logger warnings fire (warnings print to stdout)
body:
### Describe the bug

`npx storybook tools <toolset> <tool> --json` promises "the tool's structured result data as JSON instead of markdown", but node-logger warnings emitted during the run (e.g. the indexer's "Multiple story files share the component id …" warning) are written to **stdout**, ahead of the JSON payload. Any agent or script that pipes the output into `JSON.parse` fails:

```
JSON.parse fails: Unexpected token '│', "│\n▲  Multi"... is not valid JSON
```

### Reproduction

In a project whose config produces any logger warning (a fresh `react-vite/default-ts` sandbox does, via the duplicate-title template stories):

```sh
npx storybook tools docs show --id example-button --json 2>/dev/null | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c).on('end',()=>JSON.parse(d))"
```

The warning box appears in stdout even with stderr discarded, so the stream a `--json` consumer reads starts with the clack-styled warning instead of `{`.

### Expected

With `--json`, stdout should carry only the JSON document. Logger output should go to stderr (or be suppressed) for `--json` runs — same contract as most CLIs with a machine-readable mode.

### Environment

- storybook `10.6.0-alpha.6` (published), macOS
- Found while QA'ing Milestone 7 of #35526 (plugins delegating to `storybook tools`)

title: [Bug]:
body:
### Describe the bug

Howdy! We recently bumped our Storybook version to `10.5.5` and experienced a serious performance regression during HMR. I _think_ I've managed to pin down part (but not all!) of that slowdown to two causes. Take it with a grain of salt,  because this is my first time digging deep into the Storybook internals. But here's what I found:

## Problem 1: `ModuleGraphEngine` always rebuilds the complete reverse index on file updates

In this section of code:

https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/64f0b421ef68880b848e6cbeaf6cf4085a36ed68/code/core/src/shared/open-service/services/module-graph/engine/module-graph-engine.ts#L112-L131

`bumpedStoryFiles` contains the delta of changed Stories, by lookup from the reverse index. These should be the only Stories that need any changes, right? But `reverseIndexToStoriesByFile()` is then called:

https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/64f0b421ef68880b848e6cbeaf6cf4085a36ed68/code/core/src/shared/open-service/services/module-graph/types.ts#L100-L111)

And the logic in there is not aware of the changed file delta. It runs on the entire module graph. Now, there is already a guard for this over in `patch()`:

https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/64f0b421ef68880b848e6cbeaf6cf4085a36ed68/code/core/src/shared/open-service/services/module-graph/engine/dependency-graph/incremental-patcher.ts#L126-L134

But that is on a different code path. Nothing over in `mirrorUpdate()`/`reverseIndexToStoriesByFile()` has access to this signal. So a bunch of extra stuff gets repeatedly rebuilt.

## Problem 2: Unknown files force a full rebuild

This is a special case of problem 1. back to `patch()`:

https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/64f0b421ef68880b848e6cbeaf6cf4085a36ed68/code/core/src/shared/open-service/services/module-graph/engine/dependency-graph/incremental-patcher.ts#L121-L144

The logic here is correct! When `this.graph.get(path)` is `undefined` or there are no `affectedStories`, the patcher catches this correctly does no work. So far so good! But... as above, the rest of the code does not know about this. So _any_ file update, even one with no relation to any story, triggers that full rebuild.

## Reproing it

Unfortunately it's tough to repro the full impact unless you have a very large Storybook with a convulated module graph, and ours is not open source. For a size estimate, our Storybook has ~2.1K Stories files, ~8.3K individual Story exports, a ~20K module graph, and ~3.2M (Story, file) edges. At this size, the version bump was causing me to experience HMR delays up to 30 seconds, and other coworkers up to several minutes leading to disconnects.

I created a less dramatic repro for ya by asking creating a dummy Storybook with many files. (I used Claude for that purpose, hope that's OK vis-a-vis your AI policy?) On this repo, I measure a much more modest ~2s slowdown, which occurs whether or not the file I update is relevant to the module graph. I include reproduction instructions as well as the instrumentation I used to diagnose this in the first place.

## Fixing it

I am putting up a draft PR up over in #35809 where I explored a patch. I will readily admit I'm not an expert on the Storybook internals, so I won't be offended if you choose to close it and fix internally. But if it looks like a useful direction, I'm happy to polish it up for ya.

### Reproduction link

https://github.com/MercuryTechnologies/storybook-modulegraph-perf-repro

### Reproduction steps

Repro steps in the linked README.

### System

```bash
│  Storybook Environment Info:
│

│  System:
│  OS: macOS 26.5.2
│  CPU: (16) arm64 Apple M4 Max
│  Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh
│  Binaries:
│  Node: 22.22.0 -
│  /Users/vivshaw/.local/state/fnm_multishells/95621_1785974739287/bin/node
│  Yarn: 1.22.22 -
│  /Users/vivshaw/.local/state/fnm_multishells/95621_1785974739287/bin/yarn

title: [Bug]: Angular-Vite compodoc skip-check ignores -d, so a custom output dir regenerates on every build (and a stray root documentation.json silently suppresses regeneration)
body:
### Describe the bug

`@storybook/angular-vite` decides whether to run Compodoc by checking **only** if `<workspaceRoot>/documentation.json` exists, regardless of where `compodocArgs`' `-d` actually writes.

https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/d7645749a56bf2f1d2089e05d07f1ea58bdffef2/code/frameworks/angular-vite/src/preset.ts#L122-L132

The writer honours the users `-d` flag but the reader skips the actual cache. This has two consequences:

**1. A custom `-d` means Compodoc reruns on every single build.** The guard stats a path that will never exist, so it never fires. In a monorepo where you keep `documentation.json` next to the Storybook project rather than at the repo root, this is repeated cost. 

**2.a stray root `documentation.json` silently suppresses regeneration.** If anything ever writes `documentation.json` to the workspace root, the guard fires and Compodoc is skipped, leaving the project-level copy permanently stale. Compodoc still reports success and the build is green; the only symptom is `Component not found in compodoc JSON: '…'` warnings in the browser console.

---

But I am actually not sure if such a guard (file exists check) should actually exists. What happens if someone updated angular components, the guard then just skips updating the documentation.json???

In the code above there is such a comment, I actually don't understand what else would run compodoc then storybook (angular doesn't):
```
// Generate compodoc's documentation.json on cold start when no builder
  // path has produced it yet (e.g. addon-vitest child, ng run without the
  // Angular CLI builder). Skipped when the file already exists or when the
  // user opts out via framework.options.compodoc === false.
```

### Reproduction link

https://github.com/LeLunZ/storybook-compodoc-issue

### Reproduction steps

1. Angular workspace using `@storybook/angular-vite`.
2. In `.storybook/main.ts`, point Compodoc's output somewhere other than the workspace root:

```ts
framework: {
  name: '@storybook/angular-vite',
  options: {
    compodoc: true,
    compodocArgs: ['-e', 'json', '-d', 'libs/storybook-host/'],
  },
},
```

3. `rm -f documentation.json libs/storybook-host/documentation.json`
4. Run `build-storybook` twice.
   → Compodoc runs **both** times, even though `libs/storybook-host/documentation.json` exists after the first run.
5. Now `touch documentation.json` at the workspace root and run `build-storybook` again.
   → Compodoc is **skipped entirely**, even though the root file is empty and the real output lives elsewhere. Any subsequent component changes never reach `documentation.json`, and stories log `Component not found in compodoc JSON`.

title: [Bug] next/image static imports fail to resolve on Windows (virtual image path keeps backslashes in 3.3.0)
body:
## Describe the bug

On Windows, any story that renders a `next/image` with a **static import** fails the Vite build/dev with a Rollup resolve error, because the virtual-image path keeps OS-native backslashes and Rollup mangles them:

```
[vite]: Rollup failed to resolve import "C:\Users\me\git\voyages\src\assets\...\Foo.svg?ignore"
```

The backslashes get eaten downstream (`git\voyages` → `gitoyages`), so resolution fails and `storybook dev` / `storybook build` crash.

## Root cause (still present on `main`)

In `src/plugins/next-image/plugin.ts`, the image path round-trips through the virtual id **without separator normalization**:

- `resolveId` — [`plugin.ts:162`](https://github.com/storybookjs/vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs/blob/main/src/plugins/next-image/plugin.ts#L162): `return \`${virtualImagePrefix}${encodeBase64Url(imagePath)}\`` — `imagePath` is encoded **as-is**, so on Windows it carries `\`.
- `load` — [`plugin.ts:199`](https://github.com/storybookjs/vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs/blob/main/src/plugins/next-image/plugin.ts#L199): `const imagePath = decodeBase64Url(id.slice(virtualImagePrefix.length))` — decoded back to `\`, no normalization.
- That `imagePath` is then interpolated into a generated `import` at [`plugin.ts:206`/`L216`](https://github.com/storybookjs/vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs/blob/main/src/plugins/next-image/plugin.ts#L206) (`import image from "${imagePath}?ignore"`), and Rollup mangles the backslashes.

This is the same class of Windows path bug tracked historically in storybookjs/vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs#51 ("Patch for virtual image paths") and PR storybookjs/vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs#57 ("Transform Windows-style backslashes in image paths", closed unmerged). PR storybookjs/vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs#68 later rewrote this plugin to the current base64-id form but did not carry the normalization forward, so the bug persists in the latest release (3.3.0).

## Fix

Normalize `\` → `/` on either side of the round-trip. The one-line decode-side fix is enough (the only consumers of the decoded path are the generated `import` statements and `fs.readFile`, both of which accept forward slashes on Windows):

```diff
- const imagePath = decodeBase64Url(id.slice(virtualImagePrefix.length));
+ const imagePath = decodeBase64Url(id.slice(virtualImagePrefix.length)).replace(/\\/g, "/");
```

Normalizing at the encode side (`plugin.ts:162`, `encodeBase64Url(imagePath.replace(/\\/g, "/"))`) is an equivalent alternative and keeps `pathForFilter` consistent too. No-op on POSIX either way.

Happy to open a PR.

## To Reproduce

Any Storybook story on Windows that renders a `next/image` with a static import (e.g. an SVG), built via `@storybook/nextjs-vite`.

## System

- `vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs@3.3.0`, `@storybook/nextjs-vite@9.1.20`, Vite 7, Next 15.5, Windows 11.

title: [Bug]: A type-only export in an SFC drops the whole file's vue-component-meta docgen
body:
## Describe the bug

With `docgen: { plugin: 'vue-component-meta' }`, a component that exports a **type** alongside itself loses its entire prop table in autodocs. The component still renders, only its documentation silently disappears, in both `dev` and `build`.

`vue-component-meta@3.x`'s `getExportNames()` reports type-level exports (`export type` or `export interface` declared in an SFC's `<script>` block). `getComponentMeta()` throws for such a name. The plugin maps over every export name inside a single `try`, whose `catch` discards the result for the whole module:

```ts
// code/frameworks/vue3-vite/src/plugins/vue-component-meta.ts
try {
  const exportNames = checker.getExportNames(id);
  let componentsMeta = exportNames.map((name) => checker.getComponentMeta(id, name));
  // ...
} catch (e) {
  return undefined;   // one non-component export name discards every component in the file
}
```

So one throw costs the file all of its docgen, not just the export that threw.

Because an SFC cannot `export` from `<script setup>`, reaching this requires the two-block form. That is not a workaround: "Declare named exports" is one of the reasons the Vue docs give for adding a normal `<script>` alongside `<script setup>`, see [Usage alongside normal `<script>`](https://vuejs.org/api/sfc-script-setup.html#usage-alongside-normal-script). It is the supported way to publish a prop type next to the component that uses it:

```vue
<script lang="ts">
export type ButtonVariant = 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'ghost';
</script>
<script setup lang="ts">
defineProps<{ label: string; variant?: ButtonVariant }>();
</script>
```

This shape is more common than it might appear, since the pattern is not widely known. [Reka UI](https://github.com/unovue/reka-ui) uses it as house style so each component's prop interface stays co-located with the component, for example [`TabsIndicator.vue`](https://github.com/unovue/reka-ui/blob/main/packages/core/src/Tabs/TabsIndicator.vue):

```vue
<script lang="ts">
import type { PrimitiveProps } from '@/Primitive'
export interface TabsIndicatorProps extends PrimitiveProps {}
</script>

<script setup lang="ts">
const props = defineProps<TabsIndicatorProps>()
</script>
```

A GitHub code search for `repo:unovue/reka-ui "export interface" "script setup" language:vue` currently returns 376 files. Every one of them would lose its prop table under `docgen: 'vue-component-meta'`.

Value exports are unaffected. `getExportNames()` does not surface an `export const` the same way, so `getComponentMeta` is never called with that name. The trigger is specifically a **type-only** export. The reproduction includes a fixture for each so the two cases can be told apart.

This is not a regression in the plugin's own code. Lines 47-48 and the silent `catch` predate 10.5. What changed is the checker underneath: `@storybook/vue3-vite` moved from `vue-component-meta` `^2` to `^3`, and v2's export enumeration was value-only, so `getComponentMeta` was never handed a type name. On 10.4.6 (`vue-component-meta@2.2.12`) all fixtures keep their docgen.

## Reproduction link

https://github.com/seanogdev/sb-vue3-docgen-repro

## Reproduction steps

```sh
git clone https://github.com/seanogdev/sb-vue3-docgen-repro
cd sb-vue3-docgen-repro
npm install
node verify.mjs dev
```

`verify.mjs` asks the dev server for each fixture's transformed module over HTTP and reports whether `__docgenInfo` was attached, so there is nothing to inspect by hand:

```
storybook dev:
  CleanButton          docgen present
  TypeExportButton     DOCGEN MISSING     <-- this bug
  ConstExportButton    docgen present
```

`TypeExportButton.vue` differs from `CleanButton.vue` only by adding `export type TypeExportButtonVariant` in a plain `<script lang="ts">` block. `ConstExportButton.vue` adds an `export const` instead and is unaffected.

Expected: all three keep their prop tables, as they do on 10.4.6.

To see the 10.4.6 reference, set `storybook` and `@storybook/vue3-vite`

title: [Bug]: next/link mock ignores trailingSlash: true when rendering href
body:
### Describe the bug

The `next/link` mock in `@storybook/nextjs-vite` (`code/frameworks/nextjs-vite/src/export-mocks/link/index.tsx`, and its `@storybook/nextjs` twin) renders the `href` prop verbatim. The real `next/link` normalizes hrefs according to the `trailingSlash` setting in [next.config.ts](cci:7://file:///tmp/next-link-mock-trailing-slash-repro/next.config.ts:0:0-0:0) (via the `__NEXT_TRAILING_SLASH` define), so with `trailingSlash: true` a link to `/foo` renders as `href="/foo/"` in the app but as `href="/foo"` in Storybook.
 
This is a regression for `@storybook/nextjs-vite` users as of `vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs@3.3.0`, which added the `next/link` → mock alias (storybookjs/vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs#121, companion to #34736). Before that, the real `next/link` rendered in stories and hrefs matched production. Any story test that snapshots markup or asserts on rendered hrefs now fails after upgrading.
 
The env wiring is not the problem: `process.env.__NEXT_TRAILING_SLASH` still evaluates to `true` inside the story browser context under 3.3.0. The mock just never reads it. Pinning `vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs` to 3.2.5 (real `next/link`, everything else identical) restores the correct href:
 
| plugin version | `__NEXT_TRAILING_SLASH` at runtime | `<Link href="/foo">` renders |
|---|---|---|
| 3.2.5 (real `next/link`) | `true` | `/foo/` |
| 3.3.0 (mock) | `true` | `/foo` |
 
This also affects apps using next-intl's `Link`, which delegates href rendering to `next/link`.

### Reproduction link

https://github.com/dan-holmes-softwire/next-link-mock-trailing-slash-repro

### Reproduction steps

1. `npm install && npx playwright install chromium`
2. `npm test` (the repo has `trailingSlash: true` in [next.config.ts](cci:7://file:///tmp/next-link-mock-trailing-slash-repro/next.config.ts:0:0-0:0) and a story asserting `<Link href="/foo">` renders `href="/foo/"`)
3. The test fails with `expected '/foo' to be '/foo/'`
4. Add `"overrides": { "vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs": "3.2.5" }` to [package.json](cci:7://file:///tmp/next-link-mock-trailing-slash-repro/package.json:0:0-0:0), reinstall, rerun: the test passes
 

### System

```bash
storybook / @storybook/nextjs-vite: 10.4.6
vite-plugin-storybook-nextjs: 3.3.0
next: 16.2.10
vitest: 4.1.10 (browser mode, playwright/chromium)
npm 11 / pnpm 10, macOS
```

title: [Bug]: @storybook/vue3-vite doesn't request schema from vue-component-meta 3.x, causing enum props to degrade to strings
body:
### Describe the bug

After updating `@storybook/vue3-vite`, enum-like prop types generated by `vue-component-meta` are no longer available as structured schemas.

As a result, Storybook receives

```ts
schema: "Color | undefined"
```

instead of

```ts
schema: {
  kind: "enum",
  type: "Color | undefined",
  schema: [
    '"theme"',
    '"blue"',
    // ...
    "undefined",
  ],
}
```

This breaks consumers that rely on `__docgenInfo` to extract enum values for controls.

### Reproduction link

-

### Reproduction steps

### Reproduction

Component:

```ts
export const buttonColors = [
  'theme',
  'blue',
  'green',
  'orange',
  'red',
  'pink',
  'brand',
] as const;

export type Color = typeof buttonColors[number];

defineProps<{
  color?: Color;
}>();
```

### Investigation

`@storybook/vue3-vite` creates the checker like this:

```ts
const checkerOptions: MetaCheckerOptions = {
  forceUseTs: true,
  noDeclarations: true,
  printer: { newLine: 1 },
};
```

so `schema` is never provided.

`vue-component-meta` then passes

```ts
checkerOptions.schema ?? false
```

to `getComponentMeta()`.

After vuejs/language-tools#5891 ("skip schema resolution correctly when option is false"), `false` now correctly disables schema resolution.

Therefore unions are returned as plain strings instead of structured enum schemas.

### Expected behavior

Since Storybook consumes `schema`, it should explicitly request it:

```ts
const checkerOptions: MetaCheckerOptions = {
  schema: true,
  forceUseTs: true,
  noDeclarations: true,
  printer: { newLine: 1 },
};
```

With this change `component.__docgenInfo` again contains the full enum schema.

### Versions

Before:

- @storybook/vue3-vite 10.4.4
- vue-component-meta 2.2.12

After:

- @storybook/vue3-vite 10.5.2
- vue-component-meta 3.3.7

The regression appears after the vue-component-meta upgrade together with the behavior change introduced in https://github.com/vuejs/language-tools/pull/5891.

### System

```bash
Storybook Environment Info:

System:
  OS: Windows 11 10.0.26200
  CPU: (12) x64 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12450H

Binaries:
  Node: 24.12.0
  npm: 11.18.0

Browsers:
  Chrome: 150.0.7871.129
  Edge: Chromium 150.0.4078.83

title: [Bug]: build-storybook ~15-20x slower after 10.4.6 → 10.5.x with docgen: 'vue-component-meta'
body:
# [Bug]: `build-storybook` ~18× slower after upgrading 10.4.6 → 10.5.x with `docgen: 'vue-component-meta'`

### Describe the bug

After upgrading Storybook from **10.4.6 to 10.5.3**, `storybook build` went from **~6s to ~1m51s** for the same project, with no other changes. I bisected it to the framework option `docgen: 'vue-component-meta'` in `@storybook/vue3-vite`.

The Vite/Rolldown `PLUGIN_TIMINGS` report is misleading: it blames `unplugin-vue-i18n:resource` (~67%), but that plugin is unchanged between the two versions. Disabling **only** `docgen` (leaving i18n and everything else untouched) brings the build back to ~2–4s, which shows the whole transform pipeline is serializing behind the `vue-component-meta` checker.

**Bisect (Storybook 10.5.3, same repo, same machine):**

| Config | `Vite ✓ built in` |
| --- | --- |
| `docgen: 'vue-component-meta'` (my current setup) | **1m 51s** |
| `docgen: 'vue-component-meta'` + Chromatic addon removed | 1m 43s (unchanged → not Chromatic) |
| `docgen: false` | **~2.3s** |
| `docgen: false` + Chromatic addon removed | ~2.4s |

So `docgen: 'vue-component-meta'` alone accounts for the entire regression. On **10.4.6** the same `docgen: 'vue-component-meta'` setup built in ~6s.

### Root-cause analysis

Looking at `node_modules/@storybook/vue3-vite/dist/preset.js` in 10.5.3, the `storybook:vue-component-meta-plugin` transform:

```js
exclude = /\.stories\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx)$|^\0\/virtual:|^\/virtual:|\.storybook\/.*\.(ts|js)$/,
include = /\.(vue|ts|js|tsx|jsx)$/,
...
transform: {
  order: "post",
  filter: { id: { include, exclude } },
  async handler(src, id) {
    if (filter(id)) {
      let exportNames = checker.getExportNames(id);
      let componentsMeta = exportNames.map((name) => checker.getComponentMeta(id, name));
      ...
```

Two things combine to make this expensive at scale:

1. The transform runs on **every `.vue`, `.ts`, `.js`, `.tsx`, `.jsx` module** (it only excludes stories, virtuals and `.storybook/*`). In a component library that means it also runs `getComponentMeta()` against every non-component file — theme files, barrel `index.ts`, utils, composables — most of which return empty/`Unknown` meta but still pay the full `vue-component-meta` type-resolution cost.

2. The checker is created via:

```js
let checkerOptions = { forceUseTs: true, noDeclarations: true, printer: { newLine: 1 } };
let defaultChecker = createCheckerByJson(projectRoot, { include: ["**/*"] }, checkerOptions);
return await fileExists(projectTsConfigPath)
  ? (await getTsConfigReferences(projectTsConfigPath)).length > 0
    ? defaultChecker                                 // <-- project uses tsconfig references
    : createChecker(projectTsConfigPath, checkerOptions)
  : defaultChecker;
```

My root `tsconfig.json` uses **project references** (`tsconfig.app.json`, `tsconfig.node.json`, `tsconfig.vitest.json`), so the code takes the `defaultChecker` branch → `createCheckerByJson(projectRoot, { include: ["**/*"] })`, i.e. a single shared TS program spanning **all files in the project**. Every module then runs through this one program in a `post` transform, single-threaded.

This looks tied to the 10.5 docgen rework — my `build` log now shows a new **`Building open services..`** step that did not exist in 10.4.6. Candidate PRs from the 10.5.0 notes:

- "Vue: Ensure vue-component-meta runs in post" (#34976)
- "Docgen: Add mock open service" (#34954) / "Register service runtime, payload argTypes" (#35108)
- "Docgen: Run experimentalDocgenServer extraction in a worker thread" (#35324)
- "DocgenServer: Fix OOM by recycling the shared TS program" (#35305)

### To reproduce

My repo is private, so here is the exact shape that triggers it (a fairly standard Nuxt-UI-style Vue 3 + TS design system):

- **84 component folders** under `src/components/`, each following:
  ```
  src/components/MzButton/
  ├── index.ts            # exports Props/Slots/Emits interfaces + the component
  ├── MzButton.vue        # <scrip

title: [Bug]: 10.5.x breaks floating-ui-based overlay positioning — `defaultOpen` popovers (Ark UI / Zag.js) park off-screen permanently

## Describe the bug

Since Storybook **10.5.x** (10.4.6 is the last version we verified good), stories that render an Ark UI overlay (Menu, Select, Tooltip — anything positioned by Zag.js/floating-ui) with `defaultOpen` never get positioned. The positioner element stays frozen in Zag's pre-positioning placeholder state:

```
style="position: absolute; … pointer-events: none; top: 0px; left: 0px; transform: translate3d(0px, -100vh, 0px); …"
```

Visually the story shows only the trigger — the open overlay is parked at `-100vh` and never appears. It also never recovers: the parked state is still there seconds later, and dispatching a window `resize` does not trigger a repositioning.

Downstream effects:
- `@storybook/test-runner` play functions that interact with items inside the overlay fail with user-event's `Unable to perform pointer interaction as the element has pointer-events: none` (the parked positioner ancestor).
- Visual regression screenshots of these stories are empty where the overlay should be.

On 10.4.6, the identical stories position correctly (positioner gets its real transform and `pointer-events` clears within ~100ms of mount).

## What we ruled out

- **Not a hidden-canvas/timing issue on the story side.** We instrumented the preview iframe with a MutationObserver: at the exact moment the positioner is inserted into the DOM, the body classes are already past `sb-show-preparing-story`, there are **zero** hidden ancestors (`display`/`visibility`/`hidden`), and the trigger measures a real bounding rect (40×30). Wrapping stories in a decorator that defers mounting until the canvas is visible changes nothing.
- **Not the other packages in our upgrade.** Bisected on a lockfile that bumps 31 dev dependencies: with **only** `storybook` + `@storybook/react-vite` + `@storybook/addon-docs` + `@storybook/addon-a11y` reverted 10.5.3 → 10.4.6 (everything else kept, including `@testing-library/jest-dom` 7, vitest 4.1.10, playwright 1.61.1), all stories position and 244/244 test-runner tests pass. Re-bumping just the Storybook family to 10.5.3 reproduces the parked positioner.
- **Not test-tooling.** Reproduces in a plain browser page loading `iframe.html?id=<story>` from a static `storybook build` — no test-runner, no user-event involved.

Zag positions an overlay once when it opens (floating-ui `computePosition` + `autoUpdate`). Whatever changed in 10.5's story rendering causes that one attempt to fail with no retry path — the same component code, same React, same Vite works on 10.4.6.

## Reproduction

Minimal repro repo (ships broken on 10.5.3; README shows the 10.4.6 flip that fixes it): **https://github.com/KhYossi/storybook-ark-defaultopen-repro**
One-click: https://stackblitz.com/github/KhYossi/storybook-ark-defaultopen-repro

It is a stock `create vite` (react-ts) + stock `create storybook` scaffold with a single story:

1. React + Vite Storybook project (`@storybook/react-vite`), React 19, any `@ark-ui/react` 5.x overlay.
2. Story:

```tsx

        <Menu.Content>
          <Menu.Item value="a">Item A</Menu.Item>
        </Menu.Content>
      </Menu.Positioner>
    </Menu.Root>
  ),
};
```

3. On storybook 10.4.6: menu renders open below the trigger.
4. Upgrade `storybook`/`@storybook/react-vite` (+ addons) to 10.5.3: the menu is gone; inspect `[data-part="positioner"]` → parked inline style above, permanently.

Verified the repro is not project-specific: the linked repo is a pristine scaffold and reproduces identically to the component-library monorepo where we first hit this (every Ark overlay story — Menu, Select, Tooltip — affected the same way). On the repo, flipping the five storybook entries in `package.json` to an **exact** `10.4.6` (a `^` range still resolves to 10.5.3) and reinstalling makes the same story position correctly (

title: [Bug]: vue-component-meta docgen dropped in production build for <script setup lang="ts"> (works in dev)
body:
### Describe the bug

With framework.options.docgen: 'vue-component-meta', autodocs prop tables render descriptions/defaults/slots under storybook dev but lose all of them under storybook build. Only story-level markdown survives; per-prop metadata is gone. This persists on 10.5.0 (i.e. after [#34976](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/34976)).

Root cause

The vueComponentMeta plugin (@storybook/vue3-vite/dist/preset.js) only appends _sfc_main.__docgenInfo when parseLocalBindings(id, src) reports a local binding named _sfc_main:

```javascript
localBindings.has(name) && ( … s.append(`;${name}.__docgenInfo = …`) )
parseLocalBindings counts declarations, not import specifiers (verified: import _sfc_main from "x" → []; const _sfc_main = {} → ['_sfc_main']).
```

@vitejs/plugin-vue's canInlineMain() only inlines <script setup lang="ts"> as a local const _sfc_main when options.devServer is set (dev). In build, it emits import _sfc_main from "…?vue&type=script". So in build _sfc_main is an import → the guard is false → docgen is silently skipped. The vue-component-meta checker itself works fine in build (it extracts all props); only the append guard fails.

Reproduction: any .vue with <script setup lang="ts"> + docgen: 'vue-component-meta'; compare an autodocs page under storybook dev vs a served storybook build.

Suggested fix: append for a .vue default export even when _sfc_main is imported (mutating the imported component object is valid, identical to the dev path):

```javascript
(localBindings.has(name) || (id.endsWith(".vue") && isDefaultExport)) && ( … )
```

Environment: Storybook 10.5.0, @storybook/vue3-vite, @vitejs/plugin-vue 6.0.7, Vite 8, Vue 3.5.

n/a

title: [Bug]: Illegal invocation on HTMLElement.focus in setupGlobalFocusEvents on first Docs-page load
body:
### Describe the bug

Environment
storybook: 10.5.0
@storybook/addon-docs, @storybook/addon-a11y, @storybook/addon-themes, @storybook/addon-vitest: 10.5.0
@storybook/react-vite: 10.5.0
vite: 8.1.3
Framework: React 19, Vite builder
Browser: Chrome (reproduced via manual testing; not yet reproduced headlessly)
Describe the bug
Navigating to a Docs page (?path=/docs/<title>--docs) that embeds multiple story <Canvas> blocks throws an uncaught TypeError: Illegal invocation on first load. A manual page refresh resolves it and the Docs page renders correctly thereafter. It has recurred across multiple sessions and survives a full node_modules/.cache/storybook wipe (i.e. not a stale-cache artifact) and a clean dependency reinstall.

```
Stack trace
TypeError: Illegal invocation
    at HTMLElement.get [as focus] (.../sb-vite/deps/storybook_internal_preview_runtime.js:32143:18)
    at setupGlobalFocusEvents (.../sb-vite/deps/blocks-BbfHk4cu.js:12601:185)
    at <anonymous> (.../sb-vite/deps/blocks-BbfHk4cu.js:12614:51)
    at <anonymous> (.../sb-vite/deps/blocks-BbfHk4cu.js:12618:26)
Suspected cause
setupGlobalFocusEvents (in @storybook/blocks, appears react-aria-derived) monkey-patches HTMLElement.prototype.focus on a captured windowObject for a given element's realm:

function setupGlobalFocusEvents(element) {
  ...
  let windowObject = getWindow(element), documentObject = getDocument(element),
      focus = windowObject.HTMLElement.prototype.focus;
  windowObject.HTMLElement.prototype.focus = function() {
    hasEventBeforeFocus = true;
    focus.apply(this, arguments);
  };
  ...
}
```

A Docs page with multiple <Canvas> blocks embeds one iframe realm per story. If this patch is applied against one iframe's window, and the wrapped focus is later invoked with this bound to an element from a different iframe realm (plausible if a story iframe is torn down/recreated while Docs page iframes are still settling on first mount), the captured native focus (closed over from realm A) is called with a receiver from realm B — which native DOM methods reject with Illegal invocation due to per-realm brand checks.

This would explain why it's specific to first-load-of-a-Docs-page (iframes mounting/settling asynchronously) and self-resolves on refresh (iframes already stable).

Reproduction
Not yet reliably reproduced in an automated/headless environment (attempted with Playwright against the same dev server instance without success — likely a timing-sensitive race). Consistently reproducible manually: cold-navigate to a Docs page with 3+ `<Canvas>` blocks referencing separate stories, refresh to clear.

Expected behavior
No uncaught error on first navigation to a Docs page.

### Reproduction link

local repo only

### Reproduction steps

Building a components library on local. No public reproduction.

title: Storybook 10.5 focus instrumentation breaks Zag focus-visible in browser tests
body:
## Summary

Upgrading Storybook from 10.4.6 to 10.5.0 causes an unhandled `TypeError: Illegal invocation` when an Ark UI component initializes Zag's focus-visible manager in a Storybook browser test.

## Minimal reproduction

https://github.com/Guria/storybook-zag-focus-repro

The repository has two branches:

- [`working`](https://github.com/Guria/storybook-zag-focus-repro/tree/working): `npm ci && npm test` passes.
- [`broken`](https://github.com/Guria/storybook-zag-focus-repro/tree/broken): the same command fails.

The only dependency changes from `working` to `broken` are:

- `storybook`: 10.4.6 → 10.5.0
- `@storybook/addon-vitest`: 10.4.6 → 10.5.0
- `@storybook/react-vite`: 10.4.6 → 10.5.0

Ark UI stays at 5.37.2; Vitest stays at 4.1.9; Vite stays at 8.1.0; Playwright stays at 1.61.1. The repro includes a GitHub Actions workflow.

## Actual behavior

On `broken`, Vitest reports:

```text
TypeError: Illegal invocation
  HTMLElement.get [as focus] storybook/dist/csf/index.js
  setupGlobalFocusEvents @zag-js/focus-visible/dist/index.mjs
  trackFocusVisible @zag-js/switch/dist/switch.machine.mjs
```

The story also verifies that `HTMLElement.prototype.focus` is a native data property. That is true on 10.4.6, but on 10.5.0 it is an accessor, so the check fails and makes CI fail deterministically.

Zag reads `HTMLElement.prototype.focus` while installing its global focus handler. With the 10.5 accessor in place, that getter is invoked with `HTMLElement.prototype` as `this`; evaluating `this.ownerDocument` throws `Illegal invocation`.

## Expected behavior

Storybook browser tests should not emit an unhandled error when a library reads and wraps `HTMLElement.prototype.focus`. In particular, the interaction instrumentation should not make a native prototype method unsafe to read from the prototype.

I have a local preview-level mitigation that restores the native method before each story, but it is deliberately absent from the reproduction because it is not a suitable integration contract.

title: Error on invalid tag names
body:
### Describe the problem

As of #12821, we [error on invalid component names](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAE6tWSsvMSS1WsoquVspLzE1VslJyLChQ0lEqqSwAcYrLUnNKUoH84vzSomSQiI1zfm5Bfl5qXkm0YayCvh1QLjc_JTMtMzVFyaqkqDS1NrYWACD05ZdWAAAA). We don't have any similar validation for element names.

In Svelte 4, something like `<yes[no]>` [is a runtime error](https://svelte.dev/repl/aea07590a9ca42aabb4441106d5d4019?version=4.2.18), because you can't do this:

```js
document.createElement('yes[no]');
```

Because we use template cloning in Svelte 5, we don't hit that constraint — it just lets you create an obviously-incorrect element. We should have some validation here

### Describe the proposed solution

Either replace the 'invalid component name' error with a more generic 'invalid tag name' error, or have some way of determining whether a tag name is supposed to be a component or an element before we've been able to determine whether it's valid

### Importance

nice to have

title: Svelte 5: deprecate `<svelte:component>`
body:
### Describe the problem

See #12646 — we're now in a position to deprecate `<svelte:component>` if we want.

There are some places where _in theory_ it still makes sense to keep it:

```svelte
<script>
  import A from './A.svelte';
  import B from './B.svelte';

  let { condition } = $props();
</script>

<svelte:component this={condition ? A : B} />
```

```svelte
{#each things as thing}
  <svelte:component this={thing.component} />
{/each}
```

We could solve these with `$derived` or `@const` but maybe that's not as nice. The second one could be solved by treating `<thing.component>` as a component rather than as an (impossible) element, which is a change we could make separately or at the same time. (It would conflict with Svelte Native's [property elements](https://svelte-native.technology/docs#property-element), however.)

Both should be considered for 5.0

### Describe the proposed solution

see above

### Importance

nice to have

title: Svelte 5: decide on behaviour of `$state.frozen`
body:
### Describe the problem

The discussion in #12413 revealed some differences of opinion around `$state.frozen`. As of that PR, it will error if passed existing reactive state, which eliminates one source of confusion. But others remain:

- in dev, the input will be frozen with `Object.freeze`, but in prod it won't (for perf reasons). As such, the name is a bit of a misnomer
- `Object.freeze` is so-called for a reason — it freezes the object passed in; it has a side-effect. `frozen` implies that it returns a frozen object, rather than freezing its argument as a side-effect. Which _isn't_ to say that `$state.freeze` would be a better name, since that implies that it freezes existing state proxies
- It's shallow — it doesn't affect state inside the object, including in classes

### Describe the proposed solution

Together, these observations suggest (to me at least) we should change the name and the behaviour. Taking a cue from [MobX](https://mobx.js.org/api.html#observableref), perhaps `$state.ref` would be a better name. `$state.raw` is another option. Doubtless there are others.

This would have similar semantics to `$state.frozen` today — in other words only reassigning (not mutating) will cause updates (or in implementation terms: it creates a source but not a proxy) — but without the dev-time `Object.freeze`.

Of course, by doing this we lose the opportunity to tell people that they're incorrectly mutating an object. If we want to keep that but _also_ have consistency between dev and prod, then the alternative is to _always_ use `Object.freeze`, perf implications be damned.

### Importance

nice to have

{browser ? 'browser' : 'server'}
``` ...Svelte will update the text node upon hydration. It does _not_ update `{@html ...}` tags however: ```svelte
{@html browser ? 'browser' : 'server'}
``` This is deliberate — these often contain large chunks of HTML rendered from a CMS or a markdown file, and as such it's very rare that there's a discrepancy between server and client. It would be expensive to either a) check that everything matches or b) remove it and reinsert it. We make a similar trade-off in the case of things like `src` attributes, since we don't want to reload iframes or kick off additional network requests. But in those cases we warn about the discrepancy at dev time. It would be nice to do the same thing for `{@html ...}` tags. ### Describe the proposed solution At dev time, hash the content and put the hash in the opening hydration boundary comment. In the browser, repeat, and check that the hashes match. ### Importance nice to have
