title: Don't auto-open the browser when `storybook dev` runs under an AI agent (and flip the default in SB11)
body:
## Problem

When an AI agent starts `storybook dev` in an agentic dev environment (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, …), Storybook pops open the system browser (Chrome) instead of — or in addition to — the ADE's in-app preview browser. Reported by @shilman (Codex GPT-5.5 High in Astryx: opened system Chrome; in Claude it opened in **both** the preview browser and Chrome) and @yannbf (same with Codex in yamada-ui; agents also often start Storybook only to verify, so the Chrome tab is pure pollution). Internal Slack thread: https://chromaticqa.slack.com/archives/C0BDPP3LKTR/p1783478295532359

## Root cause

The open gate in `code/core/src/core-server/dev-server.ts` opens the browser unless `--ci`, `--smoke-test`, or `--no-open` is passed. The only agent-aware suppression today is `isClaudePreviewLaunch` (`code/core/src/shared/utils/agent-environment.ts`): `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION && !AI_AGENT`, i.e. only processes spawned by Claude's `preview_start` launcher. A `storybook dev` launched from an agent's shell (Claude Bash sets `AI_AGENT`/`CLAUDECODE`; Codex sets `CODEX_SANDBOX`/`CODEX_THREAD_ID`) is not suppressed and opens Chrome.

This also explains the mixed repro reports: flows that go through `preview_start` (or where the sandbox blocks spawning a browser, which fails silently via `.catch(() => {})`) don't show the bug; shell-launched `storybook dev` under an agent does.

Core already ships the right detector: `detectAgent()` (`code/core/src/telemetry/detect-agent.ts`, backed by `std-env` v4) recognizes claude, codex, cursor, gemini, opencode, devin, kiro, … plus the explicit `AI_AGENT` override — but it is only used for telemetry and onboarding-skip, not for the open gate.

## Plan (decided 2026-07-08, Kasper + discussion session)

### 1. Storybook 10.5 (this repo, non-breaking): silently suppress auto-open for detected agents

- When `detectAgent()` reports any agent, resolve `open: false` for `storybook dev`. **Silent** — no log line, no new CLI flag. Humans in non-agent shells are unaffected.
- Keep the existing `isClaudePreviewLaunch` logic intact (it also drives port precedence); agent detection is a superset for the open gate only.
- Because the plugin skills already require Storybook >= 10.5, this makes `--no-open` steering in skills and in the `storybook ai` intercept texts unnecessary — those stay unchanged.

### 2. storybookjs/mcp: Codex skill steers to the in-app preview browser (+ evals)

The Codex `stories` skill currently has **no** dev-server block at all (the Claude variant steers to `preview_start` + `.claude/launch.json`; the Codex variant omits the block entirely), and `expectPreviewBrowserStarted()` is a no-op for Codex cells (it only asserts for `claude-code` + `plugin`).

- Add a dev-server block to `packages/codex-plugin/plugins/storybook/skills/stories/SKILL.md`: start the dev server via the project's Storybook script, **leave it running** (onboarding DX — don't kill it after verification), and deliberately open the Storybook URL in Codex's in-app browser via the `control-in-app-browser` surface (`agent.browsers` API through the Node REPL `js` tool; mocked in `agent-eval/lib/mcp/codex-browser-*`).
- Extend the eval assertions so Codex cells actually verify this: assert the codex-browser mock saw the Storybook URL opened (goto) and that the dev server was left running, in the relevant 8xx evals (801, 802, 803, 804, 806, 808, 812, 813 as applicable).

### 3. Storybook 11 (breaking): flip the default to no-open

- `storybook dev` no longer auto-opens the browser in 11.0.
- Add an explicit `--open` flag as the opt-in (today only `--no-open` exists; commander provides no way to force-open).
- MIGRATION.md entry documenting the flip.

title: Improve storybook ai instance selection with agent-aware runtime records
body:
## Context

`storybook ai` runtime commands need to route to the same running Storybook instance that the agent/user is actually reviewing. This matters especially for `display-review`, because the review payload is pushed into the selected Storybook runtime and the returned review URL points at that runtime's origin. If the CLI routes to a different instance than the preview browser, the review state and browser state diverge.

Today the selector is based on exact normalized `cwd` plus optional `--port`. When no port is provided and multiple ready records match the same cwd, it falls back to the latest-started instance. That is useful, but Claude preview launches make the port hard to carry reliably: Claude can generate a port for the preview-launched Storybook process, but later `storybook ai ...` CLI commands should not assume that generated port is available in their environment.

The MCP proxy path is out of scope; this issue is for Storybook core / `storybook ai` instance selection.

## Known signals

- `detectAgent()` tells the current CLI process's agent name via `std-env` (`AI_AGENT` override, Claude/Codex/Cursor/etc. env detection).
- `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION` is injected into the Claude preview-launched Storybook process.
- When `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION` is set and `AI_AGENT` is not set, treat that Storybook runtime as a Claude preview-browser instance, not as a normal generic Claude CLI invocation.

## Proposed behavior

Add optional agent provenance to Storybook runtime instance records:

```ts
type StorybookInstanceRecord = {
  // existing fields...
  agent?: string;
};
```

When the Storybook dev server writes its runtime instance record:

1. If `process.env.CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION` is set and `process.env.AI_AGENT` is not set, write `agent: 'claude-preview'`.
2. Otherwise write `agent: detectAgent()?.name` when an agent is detected.
3. Keep records without `agent` valid for backward compatibility.

When `storybook ai` resolves a runtime instance without an explicit `--port`:

1. Continue matching by exact normalized cwd first.
2. Detect the current CLI agent with `detectAgent()?.name`.
3. If the current CLI agent is `claude`, prefer records with `agent === 'claude-preview'`, then records with `agent === 'claude'`.
4. For any other current CLI agent, prefer records with `agent === currentAgent`.
5. If no agent-specific bucket applies, fall back to the existing latest-started ready instance behavior.
6. Within a selected bucket, if multiple records compete, choose the latest-started ready instance.
7. Warnings about multiple matching instances should only show the records in the selected competing bucket, not every same-cwd record.
8. Explicit `--port` remains an exact cwd+port override and should take precedence over agent ranking.

## Acceptance criteria

- Runtime instance record types/schemas accept optional `agent` metadata while preserving old records.
- The dev-server record writer persists `agent: 'claude-preview'` for `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION && !AI_AGENT`.
- The dev-server record writer persists `agent: detectAgent()?.name` for other detected agents.
- Resolver tests cover:
  - explicit `--port` still wins;
  - Claude CLI prefers `claude-preview` records over generic `claude` records and over newer unrelated records;
  - non-Claude CLI agents prefer records with the same `agent` value;
  - multiple records in the same selected bucket choose the latest-started ready instance;
  - records without `agent` still fall back to latest-started behavior;
  - warnings only include the selected competing bucket.
- `storybook ai display-review` can route to the Claude preview-launched Storybook instance in the happy path without requiring the agent to manually pass `--port`.
- The implementation stays in Storybook core; no MCP proxy compatibility work is required.

## Verification

- Run formatting from `code/` with `yarn fmt:write`.
- Run targeted unit tests for runtime instance record writing and resolver beh

title: Make Storybook AI help and story instructions work without a running dev server
body:
## Summary

`storybook ai --help`, `storybook ai <command> --help`, and `storybook ai get-storybook-story-instructions` should not require a running Storybook dev server or a live MCP endpoint.

These surfaces should still be dynamic, but the dynamic data can be computed from the target project's Storybook config, loaded presets, addon options, feature flags, framework, refs, and import-resolved addon availability. The CLI should not need to call the dev-server MCP process just to render help or return Storybook story-writing instructions.

## Background

Today the AI CLI help path depends on a running Storybook instance because it resolves the runtime registry, calls the addon MCP server's `initialize` response for workflow instructions, then calls `tools/list` for command descriptors. That makes help text unavailable or stale when the dev server is not running, even though much of the information is generated from presets/config rather than live browser/runtime state.

We want the new model to be **dynamic but serverless**:

- Dynamic: derived from the actual project Storybook config and addon/preset state.
- Serverless: no HTTP/MCP call to the running dev-server process for help or local-only instructions.

The expected upgrade path is Storybook 10.5, where `@storybook/addon-mcp` is upgraded with the needed preset hook. We do not need a backwards-compatibility fallback that silently calls the live MCP server for older addon versions.

## Proposed two-PR shape

### PR 1: `storybookjs/mcp`

Expose a small preset-facing API from `@storybook/addon-mcp`, without rewriting the MCP server around a new broad abstraction.

Suggested shape:

- Add an addon preset hook, name TBD, such as `experimental_storybookAi`.
- The hook returns dynamic Storybook AI metadata:
  - workflow instructions
  - MCP-shaped tool descriptors for commands the addon would expose for this project/config
  - metadata for commands that can be executed locally by the CLI
- Keep the existing MCP registration flow in `mcp-handler.ts` mostly intact.
- Extract only the shared logic needed now:
  - a builder for Storybook AI metadata, using existing availability and instruction helpers
  - a shared `get-storybook-story-instructions` builder so the MCP tool and CLI local execution return the same output
  - descriptor helpers where needed to avoid duplicating command descriptions/schemas
- Reuse existing dynamic inputs where possible, especially `getToolAvailability(...)` and `buildServerInstructions(...)`.
- Use the same Valibot-to-JSON-schema conversion path as MCP uses for `tools/list` so CLI help receives MCP-shaped schemas.

### PR 2: `storybookjs/storybook`

Change the AI CLI to consume the new addon preset hook for serverless help and local story instructions.

Expected behavior:

- `storybook ai --help` loads the target project's Storybook presets and renders the preset-provided workflow instructions and command list.
- `storybook ai <command> --help` reads the same preset-provided command descriptors.
- `storybook ai get-storybook-story-instructions` runs locally through preset-provided logic and does not require a running Storybook dev server.
- CLI target-selection options are Commander-owned and should be passed before the AI command name. The command shape is `storybook ai [target options] <command> [command args]`, for example `storybook ai --cwd /repo --config-dir config/storybook --port 6007 preview-stories --storyIds '["button--primary"]'`. After the command name, remaining tokens are command/tool arguments, with `--help`/`-h` still supported for command help. title: Make storybook ai --help show MCP server instructions
body:
## Context

`storybook ai --help` currently lists the dynamic commands exposed by the running Storybook's MCP server via `tools/list`, but it does not show the server-level workflow instructions returned by the MCP `initialize` response.

That creates pressure for `@storybook/addon-mcp` to duplicate those workflow instructions into a callable tool so agents can discover them through CLI help. See storybookjs/mcp#291 for the motivating PR: it adds a `get-storybook-workflow` tool so `storybook ai --help` can surface the same guidance that already exists as MCP server instructions.

We should make the Storybook CLI consume the protocol-native source instead: read `initialize.result.instructions` from the MCP handshake and render it in top-level `storybook ai --help`.

This is a follow-up to the experimental CLI passthrough work from #35124. It should stay behind the existing `STORYBOOK_FEATURE_AI_CLI=1` gate.

## Desired behavior

When `STORYBOOK_FEATURE_AI_CLI=1` is enabled and a running Storybook MCP server returns non-empty `instructions` from `initialize`, top-level help should include a separate workflow section before the command list:

```text
Storybook workflow instructions:
<initialize.result.instructions>

Storybook commands (from the Storybook running at ...):
  ...
```

The dynamic command list should continue to come from `tools/list` exactly as it does today.

This issue only scopes top-level `storybook ai --help`. Per-command help (`storybook ai <command> --help`) should stay focused on that command's description and arguments unless a later issue finds a need to repeat session-level workflow guidance there.

## Implementation sketch

The CLI already sends an `initialize` request before `tools/list` / `tools/call` in `code/core/src/cli/ai/mcp/client.ts` to attach `clientInfo` for telemetry/session context.

Today that code drains the initialize response body and keeps only the session id. The implementation can parse the initialize JSON-RPC result, extract optional `result.instructions`, and thread that value into the help-building path in `code/core/src/cli/ai/mcp/run-tool.ts`.

Keep the exact function names flexible. The important contract is that the CLI reads the MCP server instructions from the initialize response rather than requiring addon-mcp to expose duplicated workflow guidance as a tool.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `STORYBOOK_FEATURE_AI_CLI=1`, `storybook ai --help` includes a `Storybook workflow instructions` section when the MCP `initialize` response includes non-empty `instructions`.
- [ ] The workflow instructions section appears before the dynamic `Storybook commands` list.
- [ ] The command list still comes from `tools/list` and keeps the current formatting/behavior.
- [ ] If `instructions` is absent or empty, help omits the workflow section and still lists commands.
- [ ] Existing unavailable/degraded help behavior stays intact when no Storybook is running, MCP is missing, MCP is still starting, or the command server cannot be reached.
- [ ] Without `STORYBOOK_FEATURE_AI_CLI=1`, `storybook ai` behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] Tests cover initialize instruction parsing, help rendering with and without instructions, and no behavior change when the feature flag is off.
- [ ] Manual QA verifies help output against a running Storybook with `@storybook/addon-mcp`.
- [ ] Run an independent `cursor-team-kit:thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review`; address or explicitly resolve actionable findings.
- [ ] Run a Claude CLI review using Claude Opus 4.8 Max, explicitly prompted to perform a thermo-nuclear code quality review; address or explicitly resolve actionable findings.

## Suggested verification

1. Start a Storybook project with `@storybook/addon-mcp` installed and the MCP endpoint ready.
2. Run `STORYBOOK_FEATURE_AI_CLI=1 storybook ai --help`.
3. Confirm the output includes the server instructions from `initialize.result.instructions` before the command list.
4. Confirm the command list still reflect

body:
## Context

The Storybook agent integration currently relies on a stdio MCP proxy (`@storybook/mcp-proxy` in [storybookjs/mcp](https://github.com/storybookjs/mcp)) whose main job is to manage the lifecycle of the HTTP MCP served by `@storybook/addon-mcp` inside `storybook dev` (registry lookup, version check, repair instructions). MCP's core benefits (auth, fine-grained permissions, SaaS access) don't apply to this local setup, and in practice we are fighting the protocol more than using it (lifecycle babysitting, skill-vs-tool discovery races, failures in cloud agent environments).

This issue is the first step of a POC for a **skill + CLI based approach**: expose the same capabilities as real CLI commands so agent skills can call them directly. Internal context: Notion pitch "Why Storybook plugin don't need a MCP, and can better be just skills reaching to CLI tooling" (2026-06-09).

**Scope of this issue: only the CLI commands in this monorepo.** Plugin (skill) changes and the eval comparison against the MCP-proxy plugin happen later in storybookjs/mcp.

## Design decisions

- **`npx storybook ai <tool-name>`** — generic passthrough: connect to the local Storybook MCP endpoint and forward the call via `tools/call`. No hand-written subcommand per tool; new addon tools work for free.
- **Feature flag**: the new subcommands are only registered when `STORYBOOK_FEATURE_AI_CLI=1` is set. Without it, `storybook ai` behaves exactly as today (`setup` only). This lets us merge to `next` and release immediately.
- **Discovery**: resolve the running Storybook the same way the mcp-proxy does — read `~/.storybook/instances/*.json`, match on cwd, check PID liveness, version-check (>= 10.5.0, canary `0.0.0-*` allowed), then call `url + mcp.endpoint` over streamable HTTP. **Copy the relevant registry/version-check/repair code from `@storybook/mcp-proxy` into the monorepo for now** (no cross-repo dependency; consolidate later if the approach wins).
- **`--cwd <path>`**: optional, defaults to `process.cwd()` — an ergonomic win over MCP where the agent must always pass `cwd`.
- **Tool arguments**: `--key value` flags become tool arguments; values are coerced by attempting `JSON.parse`, falling back to string. `--json '<args>'` as an escape hatch for raw argument objects.
- **`storybook ai list-tools`**: helper that prints the tools exposed by the running Storybook (via `tools/list`). Also used to produce a helpful error (list available tools) when a call fails with unknown-tool.
- **Output**: tool results print as markdown to stdout. Intercept conditions (no running instance, addon missing, version too old, mcp starting, etc.) print the same repair-instruction markdown the proxy returns today, and exit non-zero.
- **Telemetry**: deferred for now (explicitly out of scope).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `STORYBOOK_FEATURE_AI_CLI=1`, `npx storybook ai <tool>` works for all tools exposed by the running Storybook's MCP (e.g. `list-all-documentation`, `get-documentation`, `get-storybook-story-instructions`, `preview-stories`, `run-story-tests`, ...).
- [ ] Without the env var, `storybook ai` is unchanged (only `setup`; no new commands visible).
- [ ] `--cwd` optional, defaulting to `process.cwd()`; `--key value` arg mapping with JSON-parse coercion; `--json` escape hatch.
- [ ] Registry resolution, PID liveness, version check, and repair instructions match mcp-proxy behavior; intercepts exit non-zero with repair markdown.
- [ ] `storybook ai list-tools` works; unknown tool names produce an error listing available tools.

title: [Tracking]: Agentic Review
body:
## Problem

Storybook needs a faster, more focused way to review **agentic UI changes**. The current "changed stories" experience is useful but noisy: it often surfaces many stories that *might* be affected but actually aren't, still requiring the reviewer to hunt for what actually matters. This project introduces a **dedicated review page** that opens on an **agent-selected shortlist** of high-signal stories, with an easy "zoom out" path to the full changed set, aiming to reduce review fatigue and make agentic development more efficient.

### Clarifications

- **This project takes a hybrid approach between spiking and delivering a working feature** to aid in direction-finding around agentic development with Storybook. We should learn during the first half of the supercycle and then refine to something ship-worthy towards the end.
- We are mainly **targeting new users and vibe coders**, so we are optimizing for first impressions, not extensive integration with other tools or CI (e.g. Vitest, Chromatic).
- We'll test the before/after concept with users, but not actually ship it.
- We'll spend 2 weeks refining concepts and spiking solutions, and then validate these with end users. The final weeks of the project will be used to take the most promising spike and make it shippable.
- Spikes may be as simple as a story for a UI concept, or even just a Figma design.

## Proposed solution

Build a **focused Storybook review page** for agentic UI changes:

1. The agent reviews available signals (code diff, story index, changed-stories output).
2. The agent writes a **one-paragraph overview** of the change with headline statistics.
3. The agent groups stories into labelled **categories with rationales**.
4. Storybook opens a **review summary page** that displays the overview, stats, and categorized stories.
5. The review page includes a **“zoom out”** path to the set of changed (related) stories so the reviewer can expand scope when needed.

## Deliverables

- **Agent selection workflow** (prompt/skill/context) that reliably generates a useful categorized list of stories to review.
- A Storybook mechanism to open a **dynamically selected story set**.
- A **focused review page UI** that:
  - shows the agent-selected stories in one place
  - provides a clear **zoom-out** path to the broader changeset
  - renders well in an ADE (e.g. Claude Desktop) browser panel
- Documentation on what we've learned from the user interviews

## Milestones

### Agentic curation MVP (wk 1–2)
- [x] Storybook MCP update to group relevant stories into categories, with per-category and overall change descriptions
- [x] Storybook API for the agent to push curation info and receive back a review URL
- [x] Improve review link visibility in output (too subtle among preview URLs)
- [x] Telemetry for `display-review` tool

### Review page MVP (wk 1–2)
- [x] Review page with Summary and Details screens per Figma designs
- [x] Story before/after view on the Details screen (spike)
- [x] Preview iframe performance enhancements (e.g. freezing / DOM snapshot)
- [x] Verify story freezing also disables HMR
- [x] Show banner on stale state

### User interviews (wk 3–4)
- [x] Write the interview script and circulate for feedback (Vanessa)
- [x] Schedule 3–5 interviews (confirmed: Stephanie, Steven; +2–3 others)
- [x] Have ≥2 facilitators present for the first few sessions
- [x] Prepare the test branch/canary: frozen review page + before/after view + updated copy
- [x] Stand up a Chromatic deployment or static Storybook to serve as the before/after baseline
- [x] Run sessions, verify the spikes, consider alternatives, and re-scope based on feedback
- [ ] Document what we learned from the interviews

### Refinements (wk 4-5, flexible scope)
- [x] ~Baseline strategies: HEAD / last-push / session-start / merge-base~
- [x] Support viewports
- [x] ~Iframe zooming and resizing / grid layout enhancements~

title: [Review Changes]: T7 - Status-based filtering in TagsFilterPanel + statuses URL parameter
body:
### Problem statement

Add a general-purpose **"Statuses" filter group** to the existing `TagsFilterPanel` and a new `statuses` URL parameter. This group lets users filter stories by any `StatusValue` (e.g., `new`, `modified`, `error`, `warning`, `success`). It works with ANY status source — change detection, vitest, a11y — and is independent of the change detection engine.

**Depends on:** T3a (for the `StatusValue` type), T2 (for the URL infrastructure)

## Scope

### In scope

**Filter state management (in** file:code/core/src/manager-api/modules/stories.ts**):**

- Add new state fields: `includedStatusFilters: StatusValue[]` and `excludedStatusFilters: StatusValue[]`
- Add new APIs: `addStatusFilters(statuses, excluded?)`, `removeStatusFilters(statuses)`, `resetStatusFilters()`, `setAllStatusFilters(included, excluded)` — analogous to the existing tag filter APIs
- Register a new filter function via `experimental_setFilter` (or compose within `computeTagsFilterFn`) that checks whether a story has any StatusStore entry matching the included/excluded status values
- **OR within the Statuses group:** if both `new` and `modified` are included, stories matching either are shown
- **AND between groups:** a story must pass the status filter AND the tag filters to be shown

**TagsFilterPanel extension (in** file:code/core/src/manager/components/sidebar/TagsFilterPanel.tsx**):**

- Add a new "Statuses" section at the bottom of the filter panel, below built-in tags and user tags
- Derive status counts by iterating over all StatusStore entries and counting stories per `StatusValue`
- Show only status values with count > 0
- Order by `statusPriority` (highest criticality first): error, warning, modified, new, success, pending, unknown
- Each item supports include/exclude via the same toggle pattern as existing tag filters
- Checking/unchecking uses the new `addStatusFilters` / `removeStatusFilters` APIs

**URL parameter (`statuses`):**

- On startup, read the `statuses` URL parameter. Split on semicolons; entries prefixed with `!` go to `excludedStatusFilters`, all others to `includedStatusFilters`. Map short names to full `StatusValue` strings (e.g., `new` → `'status-value:new'`)
- When any status filter is toggled, serialize current state into a `statuses` URL parameter using short names separated by semicolons. Excluded values are prefixed with `!`
- Examples: `?statuses=new;modified`, `?statuses=!error;!warning`, `?tags=a11y&statuses=new;modified`
- No localStorage persistence — URL-only, consistent with T2's tag filter approach

### Out of scope

- Server-side change detection (T3)
- Sidebar rendering and animation (T5)
- MCP tool (T6)
- The `StatusValue` type infrastructure (T3a — already done)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A "Statuses" section appears at the bottom of the filter panel when at least one status value has count > 0
- Status items are ordered by priority: error, warning, modified, new, success, pending, unknown
- Checking `new` and `modified` shows only stories with those statuses in the sidebar
- Status filters compose with tag filters via AND (e.g., `?tags=a11y&statuses=new` shows only `a11y`-tagged stories with a `new` status)
- Exclude support works: `?statuses=!error` hides all stories with error statuses
- The `statuses` URL parameter is updated when any status filter is toggled
- Refreshing the page restores the status filter state from the URL

title: [Tracking]: SB Agentic Setup
body: ### Problem statement For most projects, Storybook is quite difficult to set up. Every project has different, unique needs such as providers, CSS frameworks, mocks, themes, etc. Without that context, components fail to render or misbehave. This is the "Storybook setup problem": users install Storybook, try to write stories, and then spend minutes or hours searching for a solution when things don't "just work." With the rise of AI agents and the fact that users are already using them to set up Storybook, we have an opportunity to create a self-healing agentic workflow that installs, sets up, tests, and fixes Storybook automatically. The goal of this project is to improve the experience for users who use AI (either fully through agents or using agents after manual installation): Get a functional Storybook, ready to render stories for most of the project's components, with a selection of stories to display that, out of the box, with zero additional intervention. ### Proposed workflow ### Current scope React only, Vite-based projects only. We will expand the scope as followup. ### Milestones ### M0: Eval system **Owner: `@kasperpeulen`** **Complete by:** We add an eval system to serve as the backbone for measuring the impact of this project's improvements and validating that we're actually fixing the Storybook setup problem. It will be based on the existing `storybookjs/mcp` eval suite, and use the Ghost Stories benchmark. - [x] Analyse the `storybookjs/mcp` eval suite and implement/move to/in the monorepo - [x] Define scenarios to cover e.g. with/without error hints, with/without custom vitest reporter, etc. - What is defined impacts what's built in upcoming milestones - [x] Define a way to evaluate ghost stories rate - [x] Define multiple model tiers (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, and lower-end models) - [x] Define structured output format for eval results, e.g.: - model used - changes made to `preview.js` - setup patterns - number of self-healing iterations - time spent on operations - context usage - cost - ghost stories rate before/after - quality (renders, doesn't error, has styles) ### M1.1: `storybook ai` CLI command **Owner: `@yannbf @Sidnioulz`** **Complete by:** We add a new CLI command `storybook ai` (name up for discussion) that outputs a post-init checklist and prompt to guide agents in setting up Storybook. This command will be invoked automatically after `storybook init` if an agent is detected, and will also be available for manual users to reference. - [x] Implement `storybook ai` in `lib/cli-storybook/src/` - AI prompts command with subcommands - Introduce `storybook ai init` command to output prompt including setup instructions (structured markdown checklist), useful CLI commands and versioned docs URL references - Should be a v0 prompt, can be rough! - [x] Project introspection: detect framework, renderer, installed addons, Storybook version - [x] Output versioned docs URL for reference (`https://storybook.js.org/docs/{major}.0/`) - There's a bug in the docs website where `/9` and `/9.0` works, however `/10` doesn't and `/10.0` does, so we stick to `{major}.0`. - [x] Detect monorepo and provide monorepo-specific instructions - [x] Include self-healing loop instructions, using Vitest when possible, and falling back to visiting the story in Storybook for verification - Depending on how this goes, we might need a CLI command to get Story URL based on file path + export name. It's [already implemented ](https://github.com/storybookjs/mcp/blob/9881af9c38cf4dfdeb620bac30e4640ceeaaf312/packages/addon-mcp/src/utils/find-story-ids.ts#L40)in the MCP addon - [x] Think about how this command can be expanded in the future for other use cases e.g. chromatic, upgrade, automigrate, doctor etc. - [ ] Think about whether this command should be added in the reference

title: [Review Changes]: T3 - Server-side change detection engine
body:
# T3: Server-side change detection engine

## Overview

Implement the server-side `ChangeDetectionService` and `GitDiffProvider` in `core-server`. This service consumes the builder's dependency map, runs git diff, traces affected stories using the three-category BFS algorithm (new/modified/affected), and publishes per-story change statuses to the `StatusStore`.

**Depends on:** T1, T3a, T3b

## Scope

### In scope

**GitDiffProvider (new):**

- Encapsulates git CLI calls via `child_process`
- Single fixed diff mode — all uncommitted changes:
  - `git diff --name-only HEAD` — modified/deleted tracked files
  - `git diff --name-only HEAD --diff-filter=A` — newly tracked (staged) files
  - `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` — untracked new files
- Returns `{ changedFiles: string[], newFiles: string[] }` or throws a typed error

**ChangeDetectionService (new):**

- Instantiated in `storybookDevServer()` **before** `previewBuilder.start()`
- Registers `builder.onModuleGraphChange(cb)` early — if undefined, change detection is unavailable
- Reads `features.changeDetection` (boolean). If `false`, skip instantiation and log "Change detection disabled."
- On each callback: runs git diff, traces changed files through the dependency map using **three-category BFS**:
  - `new` → story file is in the added-files set (untracked/newly tracked)
  - `modified` → story(ies) at the minimum reachable BFS distance from a changed file. Ties at the same level → all marked modified
  - `affected` → stories reachable at greater distances than the minimum level
- Publishes results to `StatusStore` using a **diff patch** strategy (set added/updated, unset removed)
- Debounces live-update rescans
- Exposes a **scan readiness signal** (promise) for addon-mcp

**StatusStore writes (uses types from T3a + T3b):**

- `typeId: 'storybook/change-detection'`
- `value: 'status-value:new'`, `'status-value:modified'`, or `'status-value:affected'`
- `data: { changedFiles: string[] }`
- `sidebarContextMenu: false`

### Out of scope

- `StatusValue` type extension (T3a, T3b)
- Manager-side consumption (T7)
- Any UI changes (T5)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Builder as builder-vite
    participant CDS as ChangeDetectionService
    participant Git as GitDiffProvider
    participant SIG as StoryIndexGenerator
    participant SS as StatusStore

    Builder->>CDS: onModuleGraphChange(dependencyMap)
    CDS->>Git: git diff HEAD + git ls-files --others
    Git-->>CDS: changedFiles + newFiles
    CDS->>SIG: match file paths to story specifiers
    CDS->>CDS: three-category BFS trace (new/modified/affected)
    CDS->>SS: diff patch (set new/modified/affected, unset removed)
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- Modifying a component marks nearest stories as `modified` and further stories as `affected`
- Changing `Button.module.css` marks `Button.stories.tsx` as `modified` but `Header.stories.tsx` as `affected` (greater import distance)
- If two stories are at the same minimum distance, both are `modified`
- Adding a new story file marks its stories as `new`
- Reverting a file removes its stories from the StatusStore (diff patch)
- If not in a git repo, no statuses written; startup message logged
- Setting `changeDetection: false` disables the feature; startup message logged
- All uncommitted changes (staged, unstaged, untracked) are detected
- Live file changes trigger debounced rescan
- Scan readiness signal exposed and resolves after first scan

title: [Review Changes]: T2 - URL-based tag filter encoding + filter-aware initial story selection
body:
## Overview

Replace localStorage persistence for tag filters with URL-based state. Tag filter state is encoded in a `tags` URL parameter; status filter state is encoded in a separate `statuses` URL parameter (implemented in T7). Fix the existing bug where initial story selection ignores active tag filters when navigating to Storybook without a story path.

## Scope

**URL encoding (bidirectional sync):**

- On startup, read the `tags` URL parameter from the current URL. Split on semicolons; entries prefixed with `!` go to `excludedTagFilters`, all others to `includedTagFilters`. Map only known built-in URL tags (`$docs`, `$play`, `$test`) to internal `_`-prefixed equivalents (e.g., `$docs` → `_docs`); leave all other `$...` tags untouched
- When any tag filter is toggled (via `addTagFilters`, `removeTagFilters`, `resetTagFilters`, `setAllTagFilters`), serialize the current filter state into a single `tags` URL parameter and update the URL. Tags are separated by semicolons. Built-in tags (internal `_` prefix) are serialized with `$` prefix (e.g., `_docs` → `$docs`). Excluded tags are prefixed with `!` (e.g., `?tags=$docs;a11y;!experimental`)
- Remove `{ persistence: 'permanent' }` from all tag filter mutations in file:code/core/src/manager-api/modules/stories.ts — filter state is URL-only, no localStorage
- Remove the startup code that reads `includedTagFilters` / `excludedTagFilters` from `persistedState` (localStorage); replace with URL-based initialization

**Filter-aware initial story selection (bug fix):**

- Fix `selectFirstStory()` in file:code/core/src/manager-api/modules/stories.ts to use `filteredIndex` when filters are active, falling back to `index` when no filters are active. If `filteredIndex` is empty, suppress navigation
- Fix the `STORY_SPECIFIED` handler: when `isCanvasRoute` is true and active filters exist, check whether the emitted `storyId` is present in `filteredIndex`. If not, navigate to the first story in `filteredIndex` instead. If `filteredIndex` is empty, suppress navigation entirely

### Out of scope

- The `statuses` URL parameter (T7)
- Status-based filtering in the TagsFilterPanel (T7)
- Any server-side changes (T1, T3)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Navigating to `?tags=play` shows only stories tagged `play` in the sidebar
- Navigating to `?tags=a11y;!experimental` shows stories tagged `a11y` but not `experimental`
- Unknown custom tags that start with `$` are preserved as-is (not rewritten to `_...`)
- Toggling a filter in the UI updates the URL immediately with semicolon-separated tags and `$` prefix for built-in tags
- Refreshing the page restores the same filter state from the URL
- No tag filter state is written to or read from localStorage
- Navigating to `http://localhost:6006/?tags=play` (no story path) selects the first story that passes the `play` filter, not the first story in the full index
- If `filteredIndex` is empty on load, no story is selected and no navigation occurs

title: Integrate addon-console into core
body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/discussions/31657

<div type='discussions-op-text'>

<sup>Originally posted by **Sidnioulz** June  3, 2025</sup>
### RFC Summary

#### Intro

The `storybook-addon-console` package depends on and extends the actions addon to print console statements into the actions panel, which is useful for debugging.

However, this means we have an addon depending on another. We're building and loading a whole addon building on functionality that's included elsewhere (and that is now part of core). It could make sense to remove the console addon and include its features in the actions code.

#### Consensus

* It makes sense to deprecate the console addon
* The functionality can easily be achieved by end users by spying on console with `@storybook/test`
* It still makes sense for Storybook to code support for this as the console addon was very popular (150k DL/week)

### Proposed implementation

1. Add config to the actions addon so end users can set a default behaviour for console spies (this also guarantees users can disable the feature if it interferes with their own console spies or monkey-patching)

```ts
addons.setConfig({
  console: {
    error: true,
    warn: true,
    log: false,
    debug: false,
    count: false, // useful to e.g. debug render loops?
  }
})
```

2. Add spies for console properties that the end user requested

```ts
spyOn(console, 'log').mockName('console.log');
```

3. Add a UI that lets end users edit what console content to show without having to restart Storybook; this would ensure feature parity with a DevTools console's filters
4. Add relevant stories / tests
5. Add relevant documentation
6. Archive the console repo and add a README and NPM deprecation notice

title: [Bug]: Storybook 9 - Improvements for Storybook upgrade and upgradeStorybookRelatedDependencies automigration
body:
### Describe the bug

Currently, the upgrade experience is great for `@latest` but not so much for `@next`.
When running upgrade for beta, for instance, the `upgradeStorybookRelatedDependencies` is never triggered (on purpose, for now) and therefore users still have broken Storybooks because some addons might depend on Storybook 8.


Here are the changes to improve the experience:
1. "Core satellite packages" should be upgraded directly, without prompt, on the upgrade command. By core satellite packages I mean addons maintained by the Storybook team which are outside of the monorepo: [addon-designs](https://github.com/storybookjs/addon-designs), [addon-coverage](https://github.com/storybookjs/addon-coverage), [test-runner](https://github.com/storybookjs/test-runner), [addon-svelte-csf](https://github.com/storybookjs/addon-svelte-csf), [addon-webpack5-compiler-babel](https://github.com/storybookjs/addon-webpack5-compiler-babel), [addon-webpack5-compiler-swc](https://github.com/storybookjs/addon-webpack5-compiler-swc), [@chromatic-com/storybook](https://github.com/chromaui/addon-visual-tests). On `@latest upgrade`, it fetches the latest version on npm, and on `@next upgrade`, it fetches the prerelease version on npm.

title: Add full support for Axe context parameter in a11y addon
body:
Currently, the a11y addon for Storybook supports the `element` parameter to define the root of accessibility checks, which corresponds to only **one of the six** possible shapes of Axe's [`context` parameter](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core/blob/develop/doc/API.md#context-parameter):

> 1. ✅ An element reference that represents the portion of the document that must be analyzed
> 2. ❌ A NodeList such as returned by document.querySelectorAll.
> 3. ❌ A [CSS selector](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core/blob/develop/doc/developer-guide.md#supported-css-selectors) that selects the portion(s) of the document that must be analyzed.
> 4. ❌ An object with exclude and/or include properties
> 5. ❌ An object with a fromFrames property
> 6. ❌ An object with a fromShadowDom property

This creates a gap between what Axe supports and what Storybook exposes, especially since we already support other Axe configurations like rule-level ignores and selectors.

**Proposal: Deprecate the element parameter and add support for the full context API from Axe:**

``` ts
parameters: {
  a11y: {
    context: ...,  // supports all Axe context shapes
    options: ...,
    config: ...,
  }
}
```
This would provide full parity with Axe and be simpler for users to reason about, especially since we could point them directly to Axe’s own documentation.

title: 🚀 Architecture Proposal: `pg_agent` (In-Database Autonomous Agents via WAL Integration)
body:
# 🚀 Architecture Proposal: `pg_agent` (In-Database Autonomous Agents via WAL Integration)

Hi Supabase Team,

Supabase has democratized Postgres for the modern web, but the current paradigm for AI applications is fundamentally inefficient. Right now, to build an AI agent with Supabase, a developer must:
1. Listen to a webhook / Edge Function.
2. Pull data out of Postgres.
3. Send it to OpenAI/Anthropic.
4. Push the result back into Postgres.

This creates latency, race conditions, and massive network overhead. 

I propose a groundbreaking architectural addition to the Supabase ecosystem: **`pg_agent` - A native PostgreSQL extension for autonomous AI**.

### The Vision: The Database IS the Agent
Instead of externalizing the AI, we embed the autonomous logic directly into the database engine using the Write-Ahead Log (WAL) and native Postgres background workers. 

When a row is inserted (e.g., `INSERT INTO support_tickets (issue) VALUES (...)`), the `pg_agent` extension intercepts the event at the WAL level. It queries a locally hosted SLM (or an API) *inside the database transaction lifecycle*.

```sql
-- Proposed Paradigm
CREATE EXTENSION pg_agent;

-- Attach an autonomous agent to a table
SELECT agent.attach(
    'support_tickets', 
    'model=gpt-4o, system_prompt="You are a support bot. Categorize and resolve the issue.", tools=[refund_user, escalate_to_human]'
);

-- When a user inserts data:
INSERT INTO support_tickets (issue) VALUES ('My app keeps crashing on launch');

-- The pg_agent intercepts, runs the LLM inference asynchronously in C, 
-- and executes the resulting tool call (e.g., UPDATE support_tickets SET category='bug', status='escalated') 
-- with ZERO network hops to an external application server.
```

### Why Supabase must own this:
Supabase already dominates `pgvector`. But vector storage is just memory. `pg_agent` is the **pre-frontal cortex**. 

By allowing developers to define autonomous agents using pure SQL that react to database mutations natively, Supabase would completely eliminate the need for LangChain, AutoGen, or external Node.js orchestration servers. The database becomes the entire AI backend.

### Next Steps
If the core architecture team is interested in this paradigm shift, my engineering team (`allornothingai`) specializes in C-level Postgres extensions and AI architecture. We are prepared to design, build, and PR the `pg_agent` extension for the Supabase ecosystem.

Let's make the database think for itself.

body:
# Bug report

- [x] I confirm this is a bug with Supabase, not with my own application. 
- [x] I confirm I have searched the [Docs](https://docs.supabase.com), GitHub [Discussions](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions), and [Discord](https://discord.supabase.com). 

## Describe the bug

Occasionally it's necessary to create a PROCEDURE instead of a FUNCTION. Specifically, PROCEDUREs invoked with CALL can do their own transaction management, while FUNCTIONs cannot.

It's possible to create, replace, and drop PROCEDUREs using the SQL editor, but they don't show up in the Functions view, which makes accessing and editing them very difficult.

## To Reproduce

1. Use the SQL editor to create a PROCEDURE, for example:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE public.myproc()
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $procedure$
declare
begin
  -- do something here
end;$procedure$
;
```

2. Open the Database / Functions view and select the specified schema (if necessary) to find it. It won't be there, and if search for it using the search box, it won't show up either.

## Expected behavior

PROCEDUREs should be shown in the Functions view together with actual FUNCTIONs. There should be some symbol or similar that allows to distinguish which is which.

Alternatively, there could be a separate Database / Procedures view just for them.

Ideally it should also be possible to create them using the GUI. Either by adding to the "Add a new function" view a checkbox "Create as procedure" (or something similar). Or, if there is a new Database / Procedures view, by adding a "Add a new procedure" button there.

title: Move Away from Using Environment Variables for Secrets
body:
# Chore

## Describe the chore

Currently, self-hosting supabase using docker is recommending environment variables for sensitive data (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/self-hosting/docker). This is generally discouraged, since exposing secrets as environment variables might be a security problem. Also a while back https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/6014, supabase began to make iterative changes to support *_FILE based environment to store paths to secrets. We should utilize this and start moving away from directly using environment variables for secrets.

(And of course, update the docs about this)

## Additional context

For more context, this is what I mean. Currently, we store `PGRST_JWT_SECRET=some_secret` in `.env` file, and we load using 
```
services:
 rest:
   image: postgrest/postgrest
   environment:
     PGRST_JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET}
```
A better way to go about this is:
```
services:
 rest:
   image: postgrest/postgrest
   environment:
     PGRST_JWT_SECRET_FILE: /run/secrets/jwt_secret
 secrets:
   - jwt_secret

secrets:
 jwt_secret:
   file: path/to/jwt_secret
```

Additional resources:
Docker' .env: https://docs.docker.com/compose/environment-variables/set-environment-variables/
Docker secrets: https://docs.docker.com/compose/use-secrets/
Supabase self-hosted: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/self-hosting/docker#configuring-services

title: Allow access to strict-mode JSON type coercions after JSON decode
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything
- [x] I have read and followed [the docs](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/get-started/) and still think this feature is missing

### Description

Context/Background:
Reported issue: https://github.com/psalvaggio/dynapydantic/issues/33
and the fix I came up with: https://github.com/psalvaggio/dynapydantic/pull/34

To distill the above context to a smaller reproducer:

```python
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic import BaseModel, TypeAdapter, ValidationError

class Model(BaseModel, strict=True):
    file_path: Path

adapter = TypeAdapter(Model)

decoded_json = {
    "file_path": "/tmp/example.txt",
}

# This is the value a field-level validator receives after
# model_validate_json() has decoded the JSON document.
try:
    adapter.validate_python(decoded_json, strict=True)
except ValidationError as exc:
    print("validate_python failed:")
    print(exc)

# Pydantic's JSON validation accepts the same string in strict mode
# and performs the JSON-specific Path coercion.
result = adapter.validate_json(
    '{"file_path": "/tmp/example.txt"}',
    strict=True,
)

print(result)
# Model(file_path=PosixPath('/tmp/example.txt'))
```

Given the constraints I have in my library, it would be desirable to be able to access the available type coercions in strict-mode JSON validation from the TypeAdapter. I could see this taking one of two forms:

1. Allow `strict` on `validate_python` to also take `"json_strict"` or something like that. This is appealing as a non-breaking API change.
2. Allow `validate_json` to take an already decoded object. This seems less desirable.

title: Allow arbitrary core schemas for serialization
body:
As per the TODO in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/13487:

There is currently no way to tell `pydantic-core` "serialize this value using this core schema". `Ser`Schema is:

```python
SerSchema = Union[
    SimpleSerSchema,
    PlainSerializerFunctionSerSchema,
    WrapSerializerFunctionSerSchema,
    FormatSerSchema,
    ToStringSerSchema,
    ModelSerSchema,
]
```

The only member that expresses "use this schema" is `SimpleSerSchema`, and it does not take a schema at all, only a name from a closed literal:

```python
ExpectedSerializationTypes = Literal[
    'none', 'int', 'bool', 'float', 'str', 'bytes', 'bytearray', 'list', 'tuple',
    'set', 'frozenset', 'generator', 'dict', 'datetime', 'date', 'time', 'timedelta',
    'url', 'multi-host-url', 'json', 'uuid', 'any',
]

class SimpleSerSchema(TypedDict, total=False):
    type: Required[ExpectedSerializationTypes]
```

So an arbitrary schema (a model, a dataclass, `list[int]`, a TypedDict, anything constructed by the schema generator) cannot be used directly. Every place in Pydantic that needs it works around the gap the same way: it wraps the schema in a wrap serializer whose function is the identity, purely so the schema can ride along in the `schema` argument.

From `ValidateAs.__get_pydantic_core_schema__()`:

https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/27f95c789b20aa23306e5ce559327db0e9a10a6e/pydantic/functional_validators.py#L911-L917

title: Add Prototype() in the metadata's Annotated of a function attribute for TypeAdapter to use
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything
- [x] I have read and followed [the docs](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/get-started/) and still think this feature is missing

### Description

Hi,

My use case is in Fastmcp where i want my tool (python function) to accept incomplete BaseModel (missing fields, no model validation). The idea is to use the filled information as a search query and return to the llm all BaseModel that match. 

Fastmcp uses TypeAdapter for calling the function tool (validate_python) and also for getting the JSON schema (json_schema) that will be sent to the llm.

Consider the following example:

```python
from typing import Annotated, List, Union
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, Prototype # new Prototype class

class Car(BaseModel):
    owner: Annotated[str, Field()]
    color: Annotated[str, Field()]

class Bus(BaseModel):
    company: Annotated[str, Field()]
    color: Annotated[str, Field()]

vehicules: List[Union[Car, Bus]] = []

def get_vehicules(
    vehicule: Annotated[Union[Car, Bus], Prototype()],
):
    results = [found for found in vehicules if found.__class__ == vehicule._class__]
    for field in vehicule.__class__.model_fields:
        if hasattr(vehicule, field):
            for result in results:
                if getattr(result, field) != getattr(vehicule, field):  # will need a correct __eq__ for BaseModel fields
                    results.remove(result)
    return results

# adapter that knows that the vehicule attribute is a prototype because of Protoype()
adapter = TypeAdapter(get_vehicules)
# send the JSON Schema of get_vehicules to the llm, saying that Car and Bus BaseModel have all their required model fields accepting null values if their current type does not already accept null.
# Then if a field is required in the model, it is still required in the JSON Schema but the llm can put the field to null (this is for pydantic to differentiate a bus from a car)
adapter.json_schema()
# get the blue cars
search_result = adapter.validate_python({"vehicule": {"owner": None, "color": "blue"}})  # None is null in JSON
# get the blue buses
search_result = adapter.validate_python({"vehicule": {"company": None, "color": "blue"}})
``` 

Note: you may need first to support dictionary (python/json) for fields of type BaseModel in model_construct. Today it only supports BaseModel instance. See issue 8084.

title: BaseModel-like API for top-level discriminated unions
body:
### Description

This is related to #10409, especially the later comments asking whether `TypeAdapter` can behave more like a `BaseModel`.

Using the docs example:

```py
from typing import Annotated, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, RootModel, TypeAdapter


class Cat(BaseModel):
    pet_type: Literal["cat"]
    meows: int


class Dog(BaseModel):
    pet_type: Literal["dog"]
    barks: float


class Lizard(BaseModel):
    pet_type: Literal["reptile", "lizard"]
    scales: bool


type Pet = Annotated[
    Cat | Dog | Lizard,
    Field(discriminator="pet_type"),
]
```

For a nested field, the documented pattern works well:

```py
class Model(BaseModel):
    pet: Pet
```

But for a flat top-level object, the available options all have tradeoffs:

```py
pet = TypeAdapter(Pet).validate_python({"pet_type": "cat", "meows": 3})
pet.pet_type  # works
pet.model_dump()  # works
```

But `TypeAdapter` itself is not model-like:

```py
TypeAdapter(Pet).model_validate(...)  # not available
```

`RootModel` gives a model-like API, but wraps the actual object under `.root`:

```py
class PetModel(RootModel[Pet]):
    pass

pet = PetModel.model_validate({"pet_type": "cat", "meows": 3})
pet.root.pet_type  # works
pet.pet_type       # does not
```

Is there, or should there be, a Pydantic-native way to define a top-level discriminated union that:

- preserves the flat input/output shape
- selects the correct concrete model using the discriminator
- is constructible/validatable like a `BaseModel`
- exposes the selected model's fields directly, without `.root`

In other words, something with the ergonomics of `TypeAdapter(Pet).validate_python(...)`, but with a first-class model-style API.

title: Add a global option to serialise/deserialise enums by name not value
body:
### Initial Checks

### Description

There's an existing [discussion](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/discussions/2980) about this which started off as a feature request but was changed to a discussion. I think that discussion has run its course so I'd like to make a feature request which can either be progressed, or closed if the project does not want to go that way.

This feature request is for a single, global flag added to the configuration:

- Add a boolean configuration option: "serialise_enum_by_name" or similar, default False.
- If it is False: no change to serialisation / schemas.
- If it is True: serialisation / de-serialisation uses the enum name, and generated schemas contain a list of enum names.

I think this needs to be part of the core library as there have been a few suggested workarounds over time in the linked discussion, but they all rely on specific internal behaviour at the time and eventually break with newer releases.

There is some discussion in the linked issue of a non-global requirement that could be applied to specific enum instances. I'd like to explicitly exclude those from this feature request: I think that is a sufficiently different use case that if people want that it should go in its own request.

title: Ability to pass context to __get_pydantic_core_schema__ and __get_pydantic_json_schema__
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything
- [x] I have read and followed [the docs](https://docs.pydantic.dev) and still think this feature is missing

### Description

I maintain the following library: https://github.com/psalvaggio/dynapydantic https://psalvaggio.github.io/dynapydantic/latest/

The general idea of the library is to offer polymorphic validation to mirror the polymorphic serialization that has been added to pydantic. Essentially, classes keep track of their children via `__pydantic_init_subclass__`, register them, the create unions to serve as field annotations.

Initially, I made this work with a custom annotation around the base class, but I have come up with a way to make the following syntax work:

```python
import dynapydantic
import pydantic

class Base(
    dynapydantic.SubclassTrackingModel,
    union_mode="smart",
    implicit_polymorphic=True,
):
    pass

class A(Base, extra="forbid"):
    a: int

class B(Base, extra="forbid"):
    other: Base

B(other={"other": {"other": {"a": 2}}}) # B(other=B(other=B(other=A(a=2))))
```

This requires overriding `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` and `__get_pydantic_json_schema__`, which works fine in the typical usage.

However, I'm running into issues with inheritance. Consider the following simple tree:

```python
Base <- Mid <- Leaf
```
If I put `Base` (let's pretend it is abstract) into my model, I'd want the field to accept `Mid` and `Leaf`, which are concrete. If I put `Mid` in there however, I'd want it to accept `Mid` or `Leaf`. Same thing if `Base` was not abstract and would be acceptable. This leads to two paths's to `__get_pydantic_core_schema__`:

1. If I use the type directly as a field annotation. Here I want to make the validator that validates the union.
2. If I am making a TypeAdapter from a base class's schema. Here I want the schema that would have been produced had I not overridden `__get_pydantic_core_schema__`.

However, I haven't been able to find a way to make this work. I've tried hacking around with patching the method away or using `contextvars`, but I think pydantic is caching the schema after the first call, which makes sense.

I think having a mechanism to pass context to `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` would allow me to make this all work, assuming the context itself was folded into the caching key.

Would this be a viable feature to add?

title: `model_copy(deep=True, update=...)` unnecessarily deepcopies fields that will be replaced by `update`
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything
- [x] I have read and followed [the docs](https://docs.pydantic.dev) and still think this feature is missing

### Description

When calling `model_copy(deep=True, update={...})`, the current implementation deepcopies the **entire** model first, then applies the `update` dict afterwards:

```python
# pydantic/main.py
def model_copy(self, *, update=None, deep=False):
    copied = self.__deepcopy__() if deep else self.__copy__()  # full deepcopy first
    if update:
        ...
        copied.__dict__.update(update)  # then overwrite
    return copied
```

This means fields specified in `update` are deepcopied and then immediately discarded. This causes two problems:

1. **Wasteful performance**: fields that will be replaced are deepcopied for nothing.
2. **Fails on non-copyable fields**: if a field contains an object that cannot be deepcopied (e.g., native C extensions, file handles, GPU tensors), `model_copy` raises an error — even though the caller explicitly intends to replace that field via `update`.

### Example Code

```python
import mujoco
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class PhysicsEngine:
    """Wraps a native MuJoCo simulation (not deepcopy-safe)."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.model = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string("<mujoco/>")
        self.data = mujoco.MjData(self.model)


class AppConfig(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)

    name: str = "default"
    engine: PhysicsEngine = None


config = AppConfig(engine=PhysicsEngine())

# This FAILS even though we are replacing `engine`:
copy = config.model_copy(
    deep=True,
    update={"engine": None},  # explicitly replacing the non-copyable field
)
# ValueError: negative dimensions are not allowed
# (from deepcopy trying to copy the MuJoCo native structs)
```

### Proposed Solution

**Option A (minimal):** Add a parameter (e.g., `update_before_copy: bool = False`) to control the order of operations:

```python
def model_copy(self, *, update=None, deep=False, update_before_copy=False):
    if update_before_copy and update:
        # Apply update on a shallow copy first, then deepcopy
        shallow = self.__copy__()
        # apply update to shallow copy
        ...
        copied = shallow.__deepcopy__() if deep else shallow
    else:
        # Current behavior (backward compatible)
        copied = self.__deepcopy__() if deep else self.__copy__()
        if update:
            ...
    return copied
```

**Option B (better default):** When `deep=True` and `update` is provided, skip deepcopy for fields present in `update`. This is both more efficient and avoids the unnecessary failure:

```python
def model_copy(self, *, update=None, deep=False):
    if deep and update:
        # Shallow copy first, apply update, then deepcopy only the remaining fields
        copied = self.__copy__()
        copied.__dict__.update(update)
        for key, value in copied.__dict__.items():
            if key not in update:
                copied.__dict__[key] = deepcopy(value)
    elif deep:
        copied = self.__deepcopy__()
    else:
        copied = self.__copy__()
        if update:
            copied.__dict__.update(update)
    return copied
```

title: Support for x-enum-varnames (Enum member names) in JSON Schema Generator
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything
- [x] I have read and followed [the docs](https://docs.pydantic.dev) and still think this feature is missing

### Description

Hi! Thanks for the great library!

I need support for the `x-enum-varnames` OpenAPI 3 extension field in the JSON Schema Generator and was curious to see whether there is interests in adding support directly to pydantic, rather than simply creating a custom generator.
I have implemented a [PR](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/13004), and would love to commit it if there is interest.

### Context

`x-enum-varnames` maintains the key(name) of any enum value that defines it in the form `name = 'value'`.
  The default behavior is to use the value as both the key and value.
  This is a frequently supported extension field in OpenAPI 3 and is used by many code generators to allow generating bot Python and Typescript enums in the following form:

```python
class Fruit(Enum):
    apple = 'Apple'
    grape = 'Grape'
``` 
```typescript
export enum Fruit {
    apple = "Apple",
    grape = "Grape"
}
``` 

Without this extension we lose this extra information, and a 1:1 recreation of the original code is impossible:
```python
class Fruit(Enum):
    Apple = 'Apple'
    Grape = 'Grape'
``` 

### Proof Of Concept
In my PR I have added a new option 

**`use_x_enum_varnames`**: `bool`
Default: `False`
```
Whether the generated json-schema/OpenAPI 3 enums should have the `x-enum-varnames` extension populated.
This maintains the key of any enum value that defines it in the form `key = 'value'`.
The default behavior is to use the value as both the key and value.
This is a frequently supported extension field in OpenAPI 3.
```

### Example

```python
from enum import Enum

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

class SomeEnum(Enum):
    FOO = 'foo'
    BAR = 'bar'
    BAZ = 'baz'

class DefaultModel(BaseModel):
    value: SomeEnum

DefaultModel.model_json_schema()['$defs']['SomeEnum']
# "SomeEnum": {
#     "enum": ["foo", "bar", "baz"],
#     "title": "SomeEnum",
#     "type": "string"
# }

class VarnamesModel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(use_x_enum_varnames=True)
    value: SomeEnum

VarnamesModel.model_json_schema()['$defs']['SomeEnum']
# {
#     'enum': ['foo', 'bar', 'baz'],
#     'title': 'SomeEnum',
#     'type': 'string',
#     'x-enum-varnames': ['FOO', 'BAR', 'BAZ'],
# }
```

title: `BaseModel.model_zip()` - construct a list of models from column-oriented data
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything
- [x] I have read and followed [the docs](https://docs.pydantic.dev) and still think this feature is missing

### Description

A common pattern when working with Pydantic models is constructing a list of instances from parallel sequences - essentially a column-to-row transpose:

```python
orders = [
    Order(customer=c, product=p, quantity=q)
    for c, p, q in zip(customers, products, quantities, strict=True)
]
```

This comes up frequently in data processing pipelines, ETL code, and API layers where intermediate results are naturally columnar (one list per field) but the final output is a list of validated models.

**Proposed API**

A classmethod on `BaseModel`:

```python
orders = Order.model_zip(customer=customers, product=products, quantity=quantities)
```

Equivalent to the comprehension above, but:

- Validates that all sequences have the same length (raises on mismatch)
- Each row is validated through the normal model constructor

Of course, the name doesn't have to be `model_zip` :)

**Why this belongs in Pydantic**

`model_zip` would be a natural batched counterpart to normal model construction. Pydantic already provides field-aware tooling around model instantiation, including mypy plugin support and editor support in  e.g., VS Code. A built-in `BaseModel.model_zip(...)` would extend that experience to the common case where data is organized by field rather than by row.

Pydantic is also the right layer for this because it already owns the model’s field definitions and runtime validation semantics. While users can validate `list[MyModel]`, they still need to manually transpose columnar inputs first. `model_zip` would fill that gap with a small, explicit API for a common pattern.

**Alternatives considered**

- **Keep the comprehension**: Works, is type-safe (the IDE sees the constructor call), but verbose and repetitive when the pattern recurs across many call sites. This repetition is what brought me to write this request.
- **`TypeAdapter`**: Validates data against a type but has no columnar construction API.
- **`Unpack[TypedDict]`** (PEP 692): Could type specific kwargs, but AFAIK requires a separate TypedDict per model -- defeats the purpose of a generic utility. Unless I'm missing something?

title: Add `exclude_extra` option to `model_dump` and `model_dump_json`
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything

### Description

If a pydantic base model allows extra fields, they get included in `model_dump` by default, e.g.
```python
class A(BaseModel, extra="allow"):
    a: int

a = A(a=1, b="test")
print(a)  # A(a=1, b='test')
print(a.model_dump())  # {'a': 1, 'b': 'test'}
```
There are cases where we might want to exclude the extra fields from being dumped. The requested feature being something like
```python
print(a.model_dump(exclude_extra=True))  # {'a': 1}
```
`exclude_extra` would be `False` by default preserving the current behaviour.

Technically, this can be done today by doing something like
```python
a_dict = a.model_dump()
for k in a.model_extra:
    a_dict.pop(k)
```
But this is cumbersome, especially if doing `model_dump_json` since you have to deserialize, remove extra fields and then reserialize the dict, which defeats the point of calling `model_dump_json`. Having the option to exclude the extra fields to begin with would be nice.

title: Stdlib dataclass custom docstrings suppressed from JSON schema description
body:
source https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/pull/4138#discussion_r2818450381

### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Pydantic suppresses `__doc__` from stdlib dataclasses in JSON schema generation to avoid auto-generated signature docstrings (e.g. `'Foo(x: int = 1)'`) leaking as `description`. However, the suppression doesn't distinguish between auto-generated and custom docstrings — explicit docstrings are also dropped.

This is inconsistent with Pydantic dataclasses, which DO get their custom docstrings included.

The suppression is in `GenerateJsonSchema.dataclass_schema` (`pydantic/json_schema.py`):

```python
if is_stdlib_dataclass(cls):
    # vanilla dataclass; don't use cls.__doc__ as it will contain the class signature by default
    description = None
```

And similarly in `_update_class_schema`:

```python
docstring = None if cls is BaseModel or dataclasses.is_dataclass(cls) else cls.__doc__
```

Python makes it straightforward to distinguish auto-generated from custom docstrings — the auto-generated ones start with `f'{cls.__name__}('`.

This became more visible after #11822 fixed `is_stdlib_dataclass` (previously `is_builtin_dataclass`), which had a bug where dataclasses with `KW_ONLY` sentinel annotations were not recognized as stdlib dataclasses and accidentally got their docstrings preserved.

### Example Code

```python
# /// script
# requires-python = '>=3.10'
# dependencies = [
#     'pydantic>=2.12',
# ]
# ///
import dataclasses

import pydantic
import pydantic.dataclasses
from pydantic import TypeAdapter


@dataclasses.dataclass
class StdlibNoDoc:
    x: int = 1


@dataclasses.dataclass
class StdlibWithDoc:
    """A custom docstring that should appear as 'description' in JSON schema."""

    x: int = 1


@pydantic.dataclasses.dataclass
class PydanticWithDoc:
    """A custom docstring that should appear as 'description' in JSON schema."""

    x: int = 1


print(f'pydantic=={pydantic.__version__}')
print()

for cls in [StdlibNoDoc, StdlibWithDoc, PydanticWithDoc]:
    schema = TypeAdapter(cls).json_schema()
    desc = schema.get('description')
    print(f'{cls.__name__}:')
    print(f'  __doc__     = {cls.__doc__!r}')
    print(f'  description = {desc!r}')
    print()
```

### Output

```
pydantic==2.12.5

StdlibNoDoc:
  __doc__     = 'StdlibNoDoc(x: int = 1)'
  description = None

StdlibWithDoc:
  __doc__     = "A custom docstring that should appear as 'description' in JSON schema."
  description = None

PydanticWithDoc:
  __doc__     = "A custom docstring that should appear as 'description' in JSON schema."
  description = "A custom docstring that should appear as 'description' in JSON schema."
```

**Expected**: `StdlibWithDoc` should also have `description` set since it has an explicit custom docstring.

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

```
pydantic version: 2.12.5
python version: 3.13.3
platform: macOS
```

title: Extract type arguments used to specialize generic models at run-time
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything
- [x] I have read and followed [the docs](https://docs.pydantic.dev) and still think this feature is missing

### Description

I've been working on porting a Pydantic V1 [application](https://salsa.debian.org/freexian-team/debusine) to V2, and in the process found myself needing to import from `pydantic._internal._generics`.  Neither my reviewer nor I can think of a better way to do things at the moment, but we agreed it would make sense to file an issue upstream.

A number of parts of our database schema are structured with a category field and some JSON data fields; the category field selects the schema used to parse the JSON data fields.  For example, we have several different kinds of "artifact", each of which has its own schema for "artifact data".  The code to handle each artifact of course wants to work with a validated Pydantic model instance rather than the raw JSON data, but we wanted to keep things reasonably DRY by not repeating the code needed to construct the model in lots of different places.

I invented a pattern that we've found to work well across our application.  When ported to Pydantic V2, it looks something like this (reduced):

```python
import abc
import enum
from types import GenericAlias
from typing import Any, ClassVar, Generic, TypeVar, cast

import pydantic
from pydantic._internal._generics import get_args, get_origin


# The return type is really typing._GenericAlias, but that's private.
def _get_specialization(cls: type, base: type) -> Any:
    """
    Inspect a class for its specialization of a generic base class.

    A class may specialize a generic base class in various ways: for
    example, it might supply specific values for some of the relevant type
    variables, or it might itself be generic and rely on being specialized
    by its own subclasses, or both.  To help us introspect such classes,
    this returns the specialization of `base` by `cls` in the form of a
    :py:class:`typing._GenericAlias`.

    :raises AssertionError: if `cls` specializes `base` in different ways by
      means of multiple inheritance.
    """
    specializations: set[GenericAlias] = set()
    if hasattr(cls, "__pydantic_generic_metadata__"):
        orig_bases = [get_origin(cls)[get_args(cls)]]
    else:
        orig_bases = getattr(cls, "__orig_bases__", [])
    for cls_base in orig_bases:
        origin = get_origin(cls_base)
        if origin == base:
            specializations.add(cls_base)
        elif origin is not None and issubclass(origin, base):
            specializations.add(
                _get_specialization(origin, base)[get_args(cls_base)]
            )
    if len(specializations) != 1:
        raise AssertionError(
            f"{cls.__qualname__} must specialize {base.__qualname__} with "
            f"exactly one consistent list of type arguments "
            f"(got {specializations})"
        )
    [specialization] = specializations
    return specialization


def extract_generic_type_arguments(
    cls: type, expected_origin: type
) -> tuple[type, ...]:
    """
    Extract type arguments from a generic class.

    This is expected to be called from __init_subclass__ in a generic class
    (i.e. one that has Generic[...] as a base class), and allows extracting
    the specializing type arguments so that they can be used as factories.
    """
    args = get_args(_get_specialization(cls, expected_origin))
    assert isinstance(args, tuple)
    return args


class ArtifactCategory(enum.StrEnum):
    SOURCE_PACKAGE = "debian:source-package"


class ArtifactData(pydantic.BaseModel):
    model_config = pydantic.ConfigDict(validate_assignment=True, extra="forbid")


class DebianSourcePackage(ArtifactData):
    name: str
    version: str
    dsc_fields: dict[str, Any]


AD = TypeVar("AD", bound=ArtifactData)


class LocalArtifact(pydantic.BaseModel, Generic[AD], abc.ABC):

title: Improve logic around `ImportString` validation when the `ImportError` originates from another source
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

When something else (and not the `ImportString` import path) produces an `ImportError`, `ImportString`'s error handling catches the exception and assumes it has been produced by the user-provided import path. 

This results in a misleading and confusing exception message. 

### Example Code

#### repro.py

```py

from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from pydantic.types import ImportString

adapter: TypeAdapter[type] = TypeAdapter(ImportString)

# This import path points to a valid module, but that module has its own ImportError
import_path = "my_module.MyClass"

print("Attempting to validate import path:", import_path)
print()

# What Pydantic reports:
print("=== Pydantic ImportString error ===")
try:
    adapter.validate_python(import_path)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")

print()

# What the actual error is:
print("=== Actual ImportError ===")
try:
    import my_module
except ImportError as e:
    print(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

#### my_module.py

```py
import torch  # do not install torch!

class MyClass:
    pass
```

```
› python repro.py
Attempting to validate import path: my_module.MyClass

=== Pydantic ImportString error ===
ValidationError: 1 validation error for function-plain[import_string()]
  Invalid python path: No module named 'my_module.MyClass' [type=import_error, input_value='my_module.MyClass', input_type=str]

=== Actual ImportError ===
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch'
```

title: Add `Port` as a network type
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything
- [x] I have read and followed [the docs](https://docs.pydantic.dev) and still think this feature is missing

### Description

I would like to propose adding a built in `Port` type, similar in spirit to existing network types.

When handling configuration, network ports can be very common. It would be ideal if, when parsing such configuration, ports could be represented in a type safe and semantically meaningful way.

Ports have a clear meaning, and while it can be argued that ports are simply integers with a defined range, this semantic information is currently lost in most model definitions.

Currently, a way to solve the issue with having a typesafe `Port` could be the following:

```python
Port = Annotated[int, Field(ge=0, le=65535)]

class SomeConfig(BaseModel):
    port: Port
```

While the above example works, it leads to each project needing to define its own type. I believe implementing `Port` can provide a more centralized and reusable definition. It could also raise the intuition that a port also needs to be validated and not simply be taken as is, and applications would be able to fail at an earlier stage.

title: Support `exclude_if` for computed fields
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

The new `exclude_if` annotation in `Field` is ignored on `computed_fields`.

I am not sure if this is similar to or completely different from the other issue (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12387).  It seems like it's different enough I decided to open a new issue.

### Example Code

```Python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Annotated

IntExcludeZero = Annotated[int, Field(exclude_if=lambda v: v == 0)]

class Model(BaseModel):
    @computed_field
    def a_computed_field(self) -> IntExcludeZero:
        return 0

obj = Model()
print(obj.model_dump())  # {"a_computed_field": 0 }
```

The expected behavior for the code above  is for `a_computed_field` to not be in the result due to the `exclude_if` directive.
