title: Premature warning about Python 3.14 in pydantic.v1
body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

When a module is imported `from pydantic.v1` and a user is running Python 3.14, they'll get a warning: "Core Pydantic V1 functionality isn't compatible with Python 3.14 or greater."

On the surface, the logic here is sound: if the user is importing something from `pydantic.v1` they must be about to use that thing, so let's warn them that it's not going to work.

But there are packages that import classes from V1 just to _check_ if the end user is using V1. For example, [LangChain in this file](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/libs/core/langchain_core/utils/pydantic.py).

In these cases, the warning is confusing and sends developers down a rabbit hole of trying to work out "who's trying to use Pydantic V1?" and if they don't know Python intimately, they might think that different packages are using different versions of Pydantic at the same time and they're clashing, all rather unpleasant, considering that nothing's actually wrong!

I see three possible futures:
1. Python 3.14 users in this situation get warnings, they can ignore them (warning fatigue, not great)
2. All packages that do this "import from `pydantic.v1` to check usage" pattern fix their code to check in some way that doesn't involve importing from `pydantic.v1` (probably not going to happen)
3. Pydantic refines the logic to only show this warning when it looks like something is actually going to break (e.g. triggered in the constructors of classes)

The current logic is going to be helpful to a shrinking number of users, and rather annoying for a growing number of users.

Relevant PR: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/12263

### What is the documentation issue?

https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/middleware#convention

### Is there any context that might help us understand?

The documentation contains the following statement:

> Note: While only one middleware.ts file is supported per project, you can still organize your middleware logic modularly. Break out middleware functionalities into separate .ts or .js files and import them into your main middleware.ts file. This allows for cleaner management of route-specific middleware, aggregated in the middleware.ts for centralized control. By enforcing a single middleware file, it simplifies configuration, prevents potential conflicts, and optimizes performance by avoiding multiple middleware layers.

The docs seem to imply that the mere act of importing multiple files exporting a `middleware` and `config` object is enough to use multiple middleware. But I imagine there is actually a composition step missing. Obviously middleware can be composed with function composition, but what isn't clear is how to combine multiple `config` objects and matchers, that is, to ensure that each middleware is associated with a given matcher.

title: Docs: default image loader ignores image cache on new deployment, leading to higher usage costs
body:
### What is the documentation issue?

The documentation about Image Optimization with Vercel states that the [cache is not invalidated for remote images for a new deployment](https://vercel.com/docs/image-optimization#remote-images).
While this may be true and the image remains on the Vercel Edge Network, the default image loader in Next.js [appends the deployment id to the query url to the image optimization](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/44cb7dddfe386a6ddc307adf7c8b4ab3e9a00335/packages/next/src/shared/lib/image-loader.ts#L79-L83):
```ts
  return `${config.path}?url=${encodeURIComponent(src)}&w=${width}&q=${
    quality || 75
  }${
    process.env.NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID
      ? `&dpl=${process.env.NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID}`
      : ''
  }`
```
The result is that after every new deployment, a user's browser will see this as new image and will not use it's local cache.

This may be a documentation issue, where the actual implementation is not fully documented, or it may be a bug or feature request, to allow the author to opt out of using the deployment id in the default loader.

A workaround for this is to write a [custom loader](https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/api-reference/components/image#loader) that does the same as the Next.js default loader, with the exception of adding the deployment id.

### Is there any context that might help us understand?

Vercel bills projects for (amongst others) number of edge requests, number of image optimizations and transferred data. If every deployment will cause all visitors to download images again _even if they have not been changed_, this will create unnecessary charges.

### Does the docs page already exist? Please link to it.

https://vercel.com/docs/image-optimization#remote-images

title: type transformed by `$state.snapshot`
Improve warning for reassigning states used by context
body:
### Describe the problem

Regarding [using context with state](https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/context#Using-context-with-state) docs, the compiler does give a warning, but it is not intuitive:

> note that if you _reassign_ `counter` instead of updating it, you will 'break the link

> Svelte will warn you if you get it wrong.

```svelte
<script>
  import Child from './Child.svelte';
  import { setCounter } from './context.ts';

  let counter = $state({ count: 0 });

  // This reference only captures the initial value of `counter`. Did you mean to reference it inside a closure instead?
  // https://svelte.dev/e/state_referenced_locally
  setCounter(counter);
</script>

<button onclick={() => (counter = { count: (counter.count += 1) })}>
  increment
</button>

<Child />
```

I learned this the hard way by checking that `$state.raw` and `$derived` do not work with the context API.

### Describe the proposed solution

If possible, provide a better warning message.

### Importance

nice to have

title: docs: clarify `$derived` `await` examples, dependency tracking
body:
### Describe the problem

## 1

> An exception is that independent `$derived` expressions will update independently, even though they will run sequentially when they are first created:

```js
// these will run sequentially the first time,
// but will update independently
let a = $derived(await one());
let b = $derived(await two());
```

### 1-1

'run sequentially' is confusing.

For example, the promises can be created sequentially, but `b` can resolve first. The truth is:

> ...the second `$derived` will not be created until the first one has resolved.

Why not be specific like the quote in [`await_waterfall` docs](https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/runtime-warnings#Client-warnings-await_waterfall)?

Clarification is needed because `$derived` isn't vanilla JavaScript.

```js
// this is intuitive. `two` is called after `one` is resolved.
await one();
await two();

// this is not intuitive
$derived(await one());
$derived(await two());
```

### 1-2

'update independently' is confusing.

Can `one` and `two` rerun? They don't have any dependencies.

```js
$derived(await one());
$derived(await two());
```

Example from query remote function seems better:

```js
let a = $derived(await one());
const post = $derived(await getPost(params.slug)); // params.slug is the dependency
```

## 2

> Anything read synchronously inside the `$derived` expression (or `$derived.by` function body) is considered a _dependency_ of the derived state.

Claude is complaining that `params.slug` is not read synchronously, thus not a dependency.

```js
$derived(await getPost(params.slug));
```

What are considered dependencies in async Svelte and `$derived`?

## Note

I believe I've used `await` inside `$derived.by` as an alternative to `untrack`. Maybe this should be warned on Svelte 5 to 6 migration? I didn't see it in the breaking changes section.

### Describe the proposed solution

See above

### Importance

nice to have

title: Explain why `$bindable` shouldn't be often used
body:
https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/$bindable tells:

> Ordinarily, props go one way, from parent to child. This makes it easy to understand how data flows around your app.
>
> In Svelte, component props can be bound, which means that data can also flow up from child to parent. This isn’t something you should do often, but it can simplify your code if used sparingly and carefully.

I think it misses an explanation why it could be done but shouldn't be done often. Or just don't tell anything ?

Actually I see it as a big topic, because I feel that bidirectional binding allows local source of truth and component responsibility, which is the state of art of OOP / SASS / API. I've yet to be convinced why suddenly with UI it's different and the flow should only go one way, because it equals to global variables, which is known to be the enemy of scalability and responsibility.

title: Add much shorter cheatsheets to Docs for LLMs
body:
### Describe the problem

One pain point that many Svelte users experience today (I imagine) is the fact that current llm models have a limited ability to produce accurate Svelte 5 code. This is of course expected to get better over time but it remains a problem for the near/medium term.

One suggested and implemented solution for this is the [docs for llms](https://svelte.dev/docs/llms).

However, even the [small size](https://svelte.dev/llms-small.txt) is actually quite big, too big to be of any practical use for me at least. Perhaps it works for youtubers to show-off cool demos, but how would you use THAT embedded in your system prompt without seeing your token usage go through the roof?

It also contains a lot of information that the llm probably already has captured in its training data, for example what Svelte is and how Svelte relates to Sveltekit.

I would like something **much shorter** and **focused** that I can use in my daily work.

### Describe the proposed solution

I propose a new llm txt file that is more of a Svelte 5 cheatsheet than anything. It should only contain the bits that are expected to present problems for llms due to being newly added.

It should laser focused and be clean of any redundant statements like `Components are the building blocks of Svelte applications.` (taken from the current llm small docs)

I suppose there already are these cheatsheets (and I can of course create one myself) but it would be nice to have a official and up-to-date source for this.

One alternative intepretation of this request (perhaps better now that I think of it) is to create a kind of `llm-recent-changes.txt` that is a cheatsheet variant of a release log, not only specific to Svelte 5. The same thought model could be used for handling recent changes in Sveltekit also (it is also evolving!).

### Importance

would make my life easier

docs: copy buttons on vite.dev have no accessible name (WCAG 4.1.2, axe button-name, critical)
body:
### Documentation is

- [x] Not sure? (this is a site defect rather than page content, and blank issues are disabled, so the docs template seemed the closest fit)

### Explain in Detail

The code-block copy buttons on vite.dev have no accessible name, so a screen reader announces them only as "button". There is no way to tell what any of them does, or which code block each belongs to.

The markup is empty, in the served HTML and after hydration:

```html
<button class="copy" data-v-b9927c34=""></button>
```

No `title`, no `aria-label`, no text content, and no `aria-labelledby`. It does not gain one after being clicked either, so this is not a transient hydration state.

axe-core on https://vite.dev/:

```
rule    : button-name
impact  : critical
tags    : wcag2a, wcag412
target  : .active > .copy
```

WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A). axe reports 1 node on the homepage because the others sit in inactive tabs; the raw HTML contains 5 of these buttons.

Worth noting where this is *not* coming from, since it took some digging: VitePress core is fine. `src/node/markdown/plugins/preWrapper.ts` renders `<button title="${tooltipText}" ...>`, and that `title` has been there since 2024. The `data-v-*` attribute means these buttons come from a Vue SFC instead, which points at `@voidzero-dev/vitepress-theme` (`^5.0.4` in `docs/package.json`). That package declares no public repository, so I could not open a PR against it directly, which is why this is an issue rather than a patch.

### Your Suggestion for Changes

Give the button a name in the theme. Either is enough on its own:

```html
<button class="copy" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"></button>
```

VitePress core already carries a translatable string for exactly this (`codeCopyButton.tooltipText`), so the theme can reuse it rather than hardcoding English.

If the "copied" state is conveyed only by a CSS class today, an `aria-live` announcement or toggling the accessible name to "Copied" would also make the result perceptible, but that is a separate improvement and not required for 4.1.2.

### Reproduction

https://vite.dev/

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open https://vite.dev/
2. Inspect any `button.copy`, or run axe-core with the `button-name` rule
3. Observe there is no accessible name

Alternatively, tab to the button with a screen reader on: it is announced as "button" with no further information.

---

Found with an accessibility checker I maintain. I am not selling anything here, and everything above is reproducible from the two commands in the steps.

title: docs: inline code appears visually smaller than body text
body:
### Description

Inline code in the Vite documentation uses KH Teka Mono at `0.875em`. Its perceived x-height and stroke weight do not align well with the surrounding KH Teka body text, which is especially noticeable in examples such as `vite.new/{template}` on the Getting Started page.

### Expected behavior

Inline code should retain the compact code size while having an x-height that is visually balanced with adjacent body text. Code blocks and code in headings should remain unchanged.

### Proposed approach

Apply a narrowly scoped `font-size-adjust` value to inline code. This uses the fonts' x-height rather than changing the declared `font-size`, and can be limited to non-heading inline code.

title: CSS side-effect imports become unreferenced when multiple entry points import the same CSS file
body:
### Describe the bug

When two or more entry points independently import the same CSS file as a side effect (`import './style.css'`), the CSS asset is emitted but no output chunk references it. The CSS is completely disconnected from the module graph — no chunk has it in `viteMetadata.importedCss`, and no JS file in the build output contains any reference to it.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/jimmy-sc/vite-css-orphan-repro

```sh
git clone https://github.com/jimmy-sc/vite-css-orphan-repro
cd vite-css-orphan-repro
pnpm install
npx vite build
```

The setup:
- `src/search.js` — imports `search.css`, exports `SearchView`
- `src/settings-search.js` — independently imports `search.css`, exports its own view
- `src/mail-search.js` (+ calendar, contacts, tasks, files) — imports `SearchView` from `search.js`
- `preserveEntrySignatures: 'strict'` with `entryFileNames: '[name].js'`

### Steps to reproduce

Run `npx vite build`. The debug plugin in `vite.config.js` logs chunk metadata:

```
search.js:              css=[], imports=[assets/search-xxx.js]
settings-search.js:     css=[], imports=[assets/search-xxx.js]
assets/search-xxx.js:   css=[assets/search-yyy.css], codeLen=0, imports=[]

CSS asset "assets/search-yyy.css": referenced by NOTHING (bug!)
```

The orphaned chunk `assets/search-xxx.js` has the CSS reference but has empty code and is not written to disk. `grep -r "search-yyy" src/dist/` returns nothing — zero references to the CSS file anywhere in the output.

### Expected behavior

Each entry chunk that imports `search.css` should have the CSS file in its `viteMetadata.importedCss`, or the CSS should be on a chunk that is reachable through the entry's import chain and written to disk.

### Root cause

This appears to be caused by Rolldown's side-effect deduplication (rolldown#8804). When multiple entries import the same CSS file, Rolldown deduplicates the CSS import into a single empty chunk. That chunk exists in the `generateBundle` bundle object but is not written to disk, and no written chunk imports it.

### Real-world impact

In our application (~600 entry points), this affects 48 modules. CSS loads in the main app because a bundle plugin walks the full import graph and collects CSS from all chunks. But when modules are loaded individually (e.g. in child browser windows), the CSS is missing because the entry chunk's import chain never reaches the CSS reference.

### System Info

```
System:
  OS: macOS 26.4
  CPU: (14) arm64 Apple M4 Pro
  Memory: 134.08 MB / 48.00 GB
  Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh
Binaries:
  Node: 25.9.0 - /opt/homebrew/bin/node
  npm: 11.12.1 - /opt/homebrew/bin/npm
  pnpm: 10.33.0 - /opt/homebrew/bin/pnpm
Browsers:
  Chrome: 146.0.7680.178
  Safari: 26.4
```

Broken: vite 8.0.3+ (rolldown 1.0.0-rc.12+) through vite 8.0.8 (rolldown 1.0.0-rc.15)
Works: vite 8.0.0 (rolldown 1.0.0-rc.9)

title: Improve clarity around VITE_* exposure to client
body:
### Documentation is

- [x] Missing
- [ ] Outdated
- [x] Confusing
- [ ] Not sure?

### Explain in Detail

Documentation around the exposure risk when using `VITE_*` is disjointed and obscured behind inconsistent terminology, especially  considering the potential impact of incorrect 

Further, the problem is made worse by the newly included Scrimba tutorial, which briefly reinforces the idea of freely using secrets with `VITE_*` (1:15 mark in the video), and does not cover the precautions or steps necessary to protect secrets in production.

### Your Suggestion for Changes

Docs should be more explicit regarding the impact of using env variables incorrectly. Additionally, rather than having mentions of client bundle risk sprinkled through the document, a dedicated sub-section to solidify the concept could be helpful. I believe the below text should all be grouped together.

**Suggested Revisions**
>To prevent accidentally leaking env variables to the client, only variables prefixed with `VITE_` are exposed to your Vite-processed code. e.g. for the following env variables:

This reads as though `VITE_` is the solution against the preceding scenario. In other words, it's as though `VITE_` will prevent env variables appearing on the client. Of course, the exact opposite is true and there should be no confusion in the language about this. Also, I wasn't entirely clear on what 'Vite-processed code' means here. I didn't find this phrase anywhere else:
>_Only variables prefixed with `VITE_` will be exposed in Vite-processed, client-side code. To prevent accidentally leaking env variables to the client, avoid using this identifier. As an example, for the following env variables:_
---
> Only `VITE_SOME_KEY` will be exposed as `import.meta.env.VITE_SOME_KEY` to your client source code, but `DB_PASSWORD` will not.

This can read as the variable `VITE_SOME_KEY` itself is what's being exposed, not it's value. I'd consider this to be clearer:
> _In this example, the parsed value of `VITE_SOME_KEY` – '123' – will be exposed to your source code, but the value of `DB_PASSWORD` will not._
---
>SECURITY NOTES
- `.env.*.local` files are local-only and can contain sensitive variables. You should add `*.local` to your `.gitignore` to avoid them being checked into git.
- Since any variables exposed to your Vite source code will end up in your client bundle, `VITE_*` variables should not contain any sensitive information.

I believe the second bullet obfuscates the point being made, again with an otherwise unused term like 'vite source code'. It should plainly relay that static replacement during Vite processing will expose variable **values** on the client. Additionally, a reasonable recommendation on how to proceed would be helpful and further the idea that an additional solution will be necessary if working with critical secrets.
>SECURITY NOTES
- `.env.*.local` files are local-only and can contain sensitive variables. You should add `*.local` to your `.gitignore` to avoid them being checked into git.
- _`VITE_*` variables should not contain any sensitive information such as API keys or secrets. 
The values of these variables are exposed to the client during build time. Consider a backend server, serverless functions, or backend as a service to properly protect secrets instead._

title: Docs: explain how to do node polyfills
body: ### Documentation is - [x] Missing - [ ] Outdated - [ ] Confusing - [ ] Not sure? ### Explain in Detail Hi! Can we please have some docs on *how* to do node polyfills in modern (Rolldown) vite? I understand the project's decision not to do this automatically (since frontend packages should not be relying on node functions). But in reality, not all mainstream NPM packages have caught up, and node polyfills are still sometimes needed. I think many in the community are relying on the [vite-plugin-node-polyfills](https://www.npmjs.com/package/vite-plugin-node-polyfills) NPM package, but my impression is it's not being actively maintained or upgraded for `rolldown-vite` and `Vite 8` (e.g. see recent bug tickets on security, `optimizeDeps.esbuildOptions` warnings, runtime error regression). I've also seen projects using: - [rollup-plugin-node-polyfills](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rollup-plugin-node-polyfills) (presumably only relevant for production builds in older pre-rolldown versions of Vite) - [@esbuild-plugins/node-modules-polyfill](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@esbuild-plugins/node-modules-polyfill) and [@esbuild-plugins/node-globals-polyfill](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@esbuild-plugins/node-globals-polyfill), via `optimizeDeps.esbuildOptions.plugins` (presumably only relevant for dev server builds in older pre-rolldown versions of Vite) And recently found - [rolldown-plugin-node-polyfills](https://github.com/rolldown/rolldown-plugin-node-polyfills), but it wasn't immediately clear to me if that's directly usable in Vite, or if it applies to both PROD and DEV builds. Currently all I can find in the Vite docs is this statement, but no tips on how. ### Your Suggestion for Changes Could we please have an example / recommendation in the docs on how to add a polyfill for a node dependency (e.g. `Buffer`). That would really help me unblock two projects if `vite-plugin-node-polyfills` doesn't get some maintenance for Vite 8 support. Thank you! ### Reproduction https://vite.dev/guide/troubleshooting#module-externalized-for-browser-compatibility ### Steps to reproduce N/A (docs update request)

title: Possible discrepancy in Deno CLI default for `--allow-import`: `user.githubusercontent.com` vs. documented `gist.githubusercontent.com`
body:
Version: Deno v2.5.3

When examining the default allowed hosts for the `--allow-import` permission, I've found a discrepancy between the Deno ~~v2.4.0~~v2.0.0 through v2.5.3 documentation and the output of the `deno run --help` command.

Permission options:
Docs: https://docs.deno.com/go/permissions

The documentation currently states:
> By default Deno allows importing sources from following hosts:
> deno.land
> esm.sh
> jsr.io
> cdn.jsdelivr.net
> raw.githubusercontent.com
> gist.githubusercontent.com

However, the output of `deno run --help` for `--allow-import` shows:
```
  -I, --allow-import[=<IP_OR_HOSTNAME>...] Allow importing from remote hosts. Optionally specify allowed IP addresses and host names, with ports as necessary.
                                            Default value: deno.land:443,jsr.io:443,esm.sh:443,cdn.jsdelivr.net:443,raw.githubusercontent.com:443,user.githubusercontent.com:443
                                             --allow-import  |  --allow-import="example.com,github.com"
```

The key difference is that the documentation lists `gist.githubusercontent.com`, while `deno run --help` lists `user.githubusercontent.com`.

**Question:**

Which host is the correct default for `--allow-import` permissions: `user.githubusercontent.com:443` or `gist.githubusercontent.com:443`?

**Context:**

This discrepancy was observed in Deno ~~v2.4.0~~v2.0.0 (and later versions, including 2.5.3). I noticed this when comparing the Deno documentation with the actual help output.

Looking at the codebase for Deno v2.5.3, the `flags.rs` file includes `user.githubusercontent.com`:
* [https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.5.3/cli/args/flags.rs#L4326](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/v2.5.3/cli/args/flags.rs#L4326) (across 2 lines)

And the `_commands_reference.json` file also includes `user.githubusercontent.com`:
* [https://github.com/denoland/docs/blob/3006b6ed924a04ed57dfdbfd750d4fd3a4955337/runtime/reference/cli/_commands_reference.json#L1955](https://github.com/denoland/docs/blob/3006b6ed924a04ed57dfdbfd750d4fd3a4955337/runtime/reference/cli/_commands_reference.json#L1955) (across 6 lines)

This suggests an inconsistency between the implemented default and the documented default. Clarification is needed on which is the intended and currently active default for `--allow-import`.

title: Feature Request: REPL Command to Print Documentation Comments
body:
# Feature Request: REPL Command to Print Documentation Comments

## Summary

Provide a dedicated REPL command or helper function that displays TypeScript/JSDoc comments for any object, class, method, or function. This makes it easy to inspect API documentation and type information without leaving the REPL.

---

## Motivation

Deno’s REPL is ideal for interactive exploration but currently doesn’t expose in-source doc comments. Developers switch to an editor or external docs to see parameter details, return descriptions, or the originating type of an instance. A REPL helper would streamline discovery and minimize context switching.

---

## Proposal

Introduce one of the following in the Deno REPL:

- A dot-command:
  ```shell
  > .doc Array.prototype.map
  ```
- A global helper function:
  ```js
  > doc(Array.prototype.map)
  ```

Behavior:

- Locate and render the JSDoc/TypeScript comment for the target symbol.
- For instances, show the constructor’s documentation and the instance’s type.
- Preserve tags like `@param` and `@returns`, with optional terminal-friendly formatting.
- Cache parsed comments for subsequent calls.

---

## Usage Examples

```shell
> doc(Deno.stdin.read)
/**
 * Reads up to `p.length` bytes from stdin. Blocks until data is available.
 *
 * @param p Buffer to read into
 * @returns Number of bytes read, or `null` on EOF
 */

> doc(new URL("https://deno.land"))
Type: URL

/**
 * Represents an object providing static methods used for creating object URLs.
 *
 * @param input A string representing an absolute or relative URL.
 */
```

```js
> const arr = [1, 2, 3];

> doc(arr)
Type: Array<number>

/**
 * Array is a global object used in the construction of arrays; which are high-level,
 * list-like objects whose prototype has methods to perform traversal and mutation operations.
 */

> doc(arr.map)
/**
 * Creates a new array populated with the results of calling a provided function
 * on every element in the calling array.
 *
 * @param callback Function that produces an element of the new Array, taking three arguments:
 *                 currentValue, index, array
 * @returns A new array with each element being the result of the callback function.
 */
```

title: Must wait for `Deno.Listener.accept` to reject after calling `Deno.Listener.close`
body:
I've just discovered that after a call to `Deno.Listener.close`, if I attempt to call `Deno.listen` on the same port, I get `AddrInUse` error, and the best way I found to avoid this is to wait for any `Deno.Listener.accept` calls (or `Deno.Listener[Symbol.asyncIterator]`).

<details>
<summary>Example server code</summary>

```typescript
const server = Deno.listen({ port: 10000 });
server.accept().catch(() => {});
server.close();
Deno.listen({ port: 10000 }); //< AddrInUse
```
</details>

The only information I managed to find was on `Deno.Listener.close` which said 
>Any pending accept promises will be rejected with errors.

With the lack of documentation on the functions in question, I'm not able to determine if this is desired behaviour or not, so I've assumed it is. 

Is it possible to either:
* Change `Deno.Listener.close` to actually close the socket
* Change `Deno.listen` to wait for sockets that have been requested to close before opening
* Add/change documentation to explain this requirement, on one or more of these functions

title: Add ARCHITECTURE.md
body:
https://matklad.github.io/2021/02/06/ARCHITECTURE.md.html

Deno is very fast moving and it's hard to keep up with internal changes if you are not closely involved. An architecture is an up-to-date overview of the inner workings of the system, stuff like:

- General overview, eg:
  - Event loop details and tokio integration
  - How ops works.
  - How `deno compile` works under the hood

- Perf characteristics that get lost in lengthy discussions over time, eg:
  - How does startup snapshots work?
  - Documenting known perf attempts that were not applied because of drawbacks. Eg: #22711 
  - HTTP slab optimizations

- Inner workings of extensions, eg:
  - How does Node-API work?
  - FFI turbocall
  - WebCrypto key material storage formats

title: doc command + examples
body:
I'm fond of the documentation approach taken in [the denobyexample repo](https://github.com/denoland/denobyexample): generate documentation from well-commented examples, potentially with a bit of module-level jsdocs. Library developers stand to benefit greatly from a streamlined version of this approach:

As demonstrated by denobyexample, examples can be compiled into markdown / elegant documentation websites. This makes sense for a few reasons:

1. Examples can double as tests (especially if one uses assertions within the examples)
2. Upon making changes to library code, examples may become invalid, which is immediately reflected upon their checking + execution. This is easier to observe and maintain when housed within the library itself.
3. Examples are one of the best on-ramp for new users of a given library.

Given the numerous benefits of examples as part of the development workflow, I believe it makes sense to add example-related behavior to the `deno doc` subcommand. Here is *roughly* what I imagine:

**Input**:

`examples/first.ts`

```ts
/**
 * @title My Example
 *
 * Some description of the example.
 */

// Bring imports into scope.
import { myFn } from "my-lib";

// Some description of `myFn`.
const x = myFn()
```

**Command**:

```sh
deno doc --example examples/first.ts
```

**Output**:

````md
# My Example

Some description of the example

Bring imports into scope.

```ts
import { myFn } from "my-lib";
```

Some description of `myFn`.

```ts
const x = myFn()
```
````

title: Consider moving manual/docs to a separate repo
body:
https://deno.land/manual is the "source for truth" and main documentation for Deno. 

These docs are generated from files in [`docs/`](https://github.com/denoland/deno/tree/main/docs) directory.

I don't have a data to back it up, but it is my impression that going through full Deno CI is discouraging contributions to manual; after all there are several pages on how to contribute to the repo and setting up dev environment is non-trivial. Additionally CI can take anywhere from 20 to 40 minutes.

Hereby I propose to move `docs/` directory to a separate repository (`deno_manual`) with its own CI. 

Here are pros and cons for this proposal.

Pros:
- contributing will be significantly easier as the only requirement would be to have `deno` installed on your system (to run `deno fmt`)
- CI will take less than 1 minute (quick development loop)
- we could even enable auto-formatting in CI, so the PRs that are opened via "Edit" button in Github wouldn't fails more often than not

Cons:
- another repo to maintain (would need to tag and release in unison with Deno release); although the maintenance cost should be marginal

All in all, I believe moving documentation to a separate repo will have a positive effect on the state of the manual as it would be trivial to contribute to it, which hasn't been the case lately in main repo.

Kinda off-topic but https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/11170 would immensely help to keep manual up to date by type-checking examples in codeblock (we already have this functionality for JSDocs, the issue is about adding ability to typecheck codeblock in markdown files).

title: ffi: napi_env can only be the last argument of the foreign function being called
body:
### What is the type of issue?

Documentation is missing

### What is the issue?

CITATION NEEDED: The napi_env can only be the last argument of the foreign function being called, because Bun FFI will always append it to the end of the arglist and then pass it to the foreign function, no matter where the `FFIType.napi_env` or `"napi_env"` being placed in FFIFunction.args. Both [FFI doc](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/ffi) and [C Compiler doc](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/c-compiler) have not mentioned it, and there seems no existing document about it across the internet. AI gives false response as well.

### Where did you find it?

I found it during writing [a FFI binding of libclang](https://github.com/calsys456/bun-libclang) with Bun FFI. You can find out how I use the napi_env in index.ts

title: [Documentation]: Clarify downsides of current TanStack Query integration
body:
### Describe the problem

I recently saw the new TanStack Query integration and it reminds about short comings that I encountered in the past.

Right now we mock network requests in Storybook with axios-mock-adapter and have one axios instance per story. That makes it very easy and safe to embed multiple stories that all make the same request, but show different results on the same docs page.

In the old (?) [MSW RFC](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/discussions/30267#discussioncomment-11920638) I tried to explain the same behaviour. Back then it was said "_Rendering multiple stories on the same page breaks that isolation as there's no identifier to distinguish the same request between stories._"

It sounds like the new TanStack Query integration works the same. The docs say:
> The recommended approach is to create a single [QueryClient](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/reference/QueryClient) in your preview file, clear it between stories via [beforeEach](https://storybook.js.org/docs/writing-tests/interaction-testing#beforeeach), and share the same instance through both parameters.tanstack.router.context and a QueryClientProvider decorator. ...  Clear the cache between stories so each story starts fresh

I'd like to learn why this is the recommended approach and what downsides it would have to use a client per story. 

In the bigger picture I wonder if we fight windmills and that Storybook rather sees it as an edge case to document multiple stories next to each other (e.g. via `<Canvas/>` in `.mdx` pages)? Because recommending to alter global state per Story seems to be against this pattern.

Thank you!

title: [Documentation]: main-config-docs is probably outdated
desktop: how to properly type a binding?
No way to opt out of global Node.js types (since 2.8.0)
body:
## Summary

Since v2.8.0, Deno includes the Node.js type lib globally by default, and there doesn't seem to be a way to opt out.

## Reproduction

```ts
const _timeout: number = setTimeout(() => {});
```

On Deno 2.8.0 or higher (currently 2.9.1), this fails with:

```
Type 'Timeout' is not assignable to type 'number'.
```

On 2.7.14 and earlier, it type-checks fine. `setTimeout` returning `number` matches the browser behavior.

## Background

I originally started writing this as a bug report. I assumed some package was importing the Node.js types and Deno was failing to exclude them. While isolating the issue, I realized the change was intentional:

> feat: include node lib by default and use NodeJS.Timeout for timers (#33823)

The node lib is pulled in via a `/// <reference lib="node" />` directive inside `lib.deno.shared_globals.d.ts`, so every Deno lib includes it. Setting `compilerOptions.lib` doesn't help, since you can't get Deno's globals without the Node.js types coming along.

I just realized this today after upgrading the Deno version of an old project, seeing Node.js type errors inside Deno truly feels like a bug. I was surprised how such an obvious bug could live until 2.9.1.

Turns out it was intentional. I have no idea why while there is `@types/node`.

## Why this matters

One of Deno's core promises (selling point) has always been browser API compatibility: web-standard APIs behaving the way they do in the browser. In the browser, `setTimeout` returns a `number`, and code written against web standards expects that. With this change, web-compatible code now type-errors under Deno, while Node-specific patterns are the ones that type-check.

Node.js compat is valuable, and I understand wanting `NodeJS.Timeout` patterns to work for people porting legacy code. But making the Node.js types global for everyone inverts the default: projects that don't touch `node:` at all (some on purpose) still get Node's type environment. Those who need it could opt in (as they already can with `@types/node`), rather than everyone else having no way to opt out.

## Expected

Either make the node lib opt-in, or at minimum provide a way to exclude it while keeping the Deno globals, so web-standard code can keep type-checking as it does in the browser.

If there will be a Node.js compat layer, that should be hidden from the user and should only apply to external packages until its not needed anymore.

title: Why does `deno run` use the network without the `--allow-net` flag (or including the --deny-net flag)
body:
I'm in the process of switching away from Node as much as possible, and came across a change to not use npx in favour of Deno.

```
deno run npm:wrangler pages blah blah
```

Per the docs: https://docs.deno.com/runtime/fundamentals/node/

```
# deno run allows remote execution of a package from various locations,
# and can scoped to npm via the `npm:` specifier.
$ deno run -A npm:create-next-app@latest
```

This is the error after blocking the network connection:

```
error: Failed loading https://registry.npmjs.org/wrangler for package "wrangler"

Caused by:
    error sending request for url (https://registry.npmjs.org/wrangler): client error (Connect): tcp connect error: Bad file descriptor (os error 9)
```

npmjs isn't on the list of allowed URLS: https://docs.deno.com/runtime/fundamentals/security/#network-access


Now, I think the nuance here is that the docs specifically state "executing code"?
```
executing code can not make network requests, open network listeners or perform DNS resolution. This includes making HTTP requests, opening TCP/UDP sockets, and listening for incoming connections on TCP or UDP.
```

So, I'm guessing that the intention is that Deno itself can have all permissions, but just the thing that Deno is running can't? I have to admit, I was a bit surprised to see my network blocker pop up when running that command.

title: deno compile ignores -o <name> when compilation is run from outside the project root (input file is not in the cwd)
body:
Version: Deno 2.3.6

### Reproduction Steps

1. Create a directory and initialize a Deno project:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/work/foo
cd ~/work/foo
deno init
cd ..
```

2. From outside the project root (`~/work`), run:

```bash
deno compile foo/main.ts -o out.bin
```

---

### Observed Behavior

```bash
~/work ❯ deno compile foo/main.ts -o out.bin
Check file:///home/user/work/foo/main.ts
Compile file:///home/user/work/foo/main.ts to foo
error: Could not compile to file 'foo' because a directory exists with the same name. You can use the `--output <file-path>` flag to provide an alternative name.
```

Despite explicitly using the `-o out.bin` argument, Deno:

- Logs that it's compiling "to foo"
- Attempts to emit the binary as `foo` rather than `out.bin`
- Fails if a `foo/` directory exists which should be irrelevant unless the `-o` was set to the same name

Additionally, if the compile command is run from any directory other than the project's direct parent like:

```bash
cd /tmp
deno compile ~/work/foo/main.ts -o out.bin
```

Deno still ignores the `-o` flag and instead emits a binary named `foo` directly into the current directory (i.e. `/tmp/foo`), not `out.bin`.

---

### Expected Behavior

- The compiler must respect the `--output` flag without referencing the source path or its parent directory.
- The output path specified via `-o` should always be used literally and without fallback logic.
- Compilation should succeed regardless of the current working directory or source location, as long as the `-o` path is valid and doesn't match any existing path.

---

### Additional Context

This appears to be a long-standing issue. A similar issue was previously raised in [#12759](https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/12759) but closed without being resolved, it only suggests using `--output` which appears to be broken as I stated above.

This bug creates serious friction in CI scripts, project automation, and build tools that rely on predictable output behavior.

    at file:///[...]/src/core/error.test.ts:152:25
    at assertRejects (https://jsr.io/@std/assert/1.0.5/rejects.ts:87:29)
    at Object.<anonymous> (file:///[...]/src/core/error.test.ts:151:5)

    at Function.runTest (https://jsr.io/@std/testing/1.0.2/_test_suite.ts:372:33)

```

Also, the error suggests that it must be an unawaited call to async FS API, which is not the case.

The error report is consistent across failures, meaning the same file/module, the same `const [...] = await Deno.readTextFile([...])` call.

Also should note that this failure is the only failure in the step that runs deno and there's no other test failures.

These started when we added tests for some functions that use temp files as buffers. We can't tell from which version of Deno this could have started, but the first time we got them we were already on version 2.0.x.

Also, these started without the `--trace-leaks` param, and the behavior has not changed since introducing `--trace-leaks`.

Have never been able to repro it on macos, though.

title: How to scale OTEL instrumentation in Deno without opinionated defaults?
body: Hi everyone, especially @lucacasonato I'm currently integrating OpenTelemetry (OTEL) in Deno and have a question regarding the current approach. From my perspective, I’m struggling to understand how this implementation is meant to scale in the long run. It seems that there are no opinionated defaults, leaving it entirely up to the developer to define and manage everything manually. When a trace is started, I can modify the name and add values globally on the middleware level. However, when Deno makes sub-requests within that trace, these do not automatically inherit meaningful names or status information—they remain undefined unless explicitly set by the developer. This makes me wonder how one is supposed to scale instrumentation properly—would I need to manually update every single sub-request span myself? Or is this actually the intended way to use OTEL in Deno? Personally, I think it would make sense to provide at least some opinionated defaults, such as setting the span name to something like METHOD /pathname. Since Deno already tracks sub-requests, why not also set the status and a reasonable default name automatically? These pieces of information should already be available, so it feels like an unnecessary burden to require developers to handle them manually. Since I’m a newbie when it comes to OTEL, I’d really appreciate some clarification. Thanks in advance! 😊

title: [feat] Make backend js ecosystem future better
body:
### Feature Request

Make backend js ecosystem future better.

### What changed?

Program language like `rust` and `zig`, leads to new backend js/ts runtime like `deno` and `bun`.

### What is the problem?

`npm` is awesome.

To use awesome `npm` package for **backend**, usually need `Node.js` core module.

But, currently, because three runtime not able to share same `Node.js` core module, when use `deno` or `bun` with `npm` packages, there are compatibility issues.

Because `Node.js` `deno` `bun` does not able to share same `Node.js` core module and spec and test, `deno` `bun` reinvent the not-fully-compact wheel individually, and not reinvent-once-use-forever.

### What maybe the solution?

`Node.js` `deno` `bun` all support `napi`.

- `deno` napi since [pull/13633](https://github.com/denoland/deno/pull/13633), stable at [v1.31](https://deno.com/blog/v1.31#stabilization-of-node-api)

- `bun` is also [implementing](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/158) napi

<details>
  <summary markdown="span">Extra</summary>

I don't know if override core module is needed for solution. 

If it does, I guess `Node.js` loader and `deno` importmap should works.

</details>

### What is the feature request?

- Rewrite `Node.js` core module using `napi`

- Rewrite `Node.js` core module test using `javascript`, so `Node.js` `deno` `bun` `browserify-XXX` can share **SAME** test

- Publish `napi` version of `Node.js` core module to `npm`

- Maybe publish to `npm` under a new organization `@backend-javascript-core-module-standard-committee/http`

### Related

- https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/50195

body:
### Describe the feature

Hello there, I am a NixOS (https://nixos.org/) developer and we package sometimes software that uses Nuxt as a server runtime, unfortunately, because we enforce scoping and many things, we cannot guarantee that `.nuxt` is in the same current working directory, it is often locked in a immutable folder.

title: Run function for Vuex store on app start for default settings
body:
<!-- 💚 Thanks for your time to make Nuxt better with your feedbacks 💚 -->

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I'm using Nuxt JS to build a hybrid app that uses Capacitor JS. I'm using the Vuex store in my project to create some default, initial settings for my app if a user hasn't previously changed a setting in the app. Once a user changes a setting in the app, I dispatch a function to the Vuex store to then update the appropriate setting, it then works just fine whilst navigating the app but when the app is forcefully closed and re-opened, I need to run `setDefaultSettings` to populate the `app_settings` before the view loads.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I'd like to be able to simply specify a function, say, at the bottom of my Vuex store file which runs `setDefaultSettings` when the website/app loads

### Describe alternatives you've considered

My current Vuex store file, `storage.js` looks like this:

```javascript
export const state = () => ({
  app_settings: {
    theme: 'system',
    refreshButtonPlacement: 'right',
    fetchTimeout: 120
  }
})

async function getData (storage, key) {
  const { value } = await storage.get({ key: key })
  return value
}


export const mutations = {

  /*
   * Set default settings on app launch
   */
  async setDefaultSettings (state) {
    const theme = await getData(this.$CapacitorStorage, 'theme')
    const refreshButtonPlacement = await getData(this.$CapacitorStorage, 'refreshButtonPlacement')
    const fetchTimeout = await getData(this.$CapacitorStorage, 'fetchTimeout')

    if (theme) {
      state.app_settings.theme = theme ? theme : 'system'
    }
    if (refreshButtonPlacement) {
      state.app_settings.refreshButtonPlacement = refreshButtonPlacement ? refreshButtonPlacement : 'right'
    }
    if (fetchTimeout != null) {
      state.app_settings.fetchTimeout = fetchTimeout != null ? fetchTimeout : 120
    }
  },

  /*
   * Update app setting
   */
  async updateSetting (state, data) {
    state.app_settings[data.key] = data.value

    await this.$CapacitorStorage.set({
      key: data.key,
      value: data.value
    })
  }

}
```

Right now, as a hacky workaround I'm using my app's `index.vue` file, which is a blank file to effectively run `this.$store.commit('storage/setDefaultSettings')` from within my `created` hook, which then redirects the user to the appropriate pages in the app, and since the user can't change URLs easily, this works fine, but I really need to be able to simply run `setDefaultSettings` whenever the app is started and the file is loaded.

### Additional context

Maybe there's already an approach I can take?

Nuxt 2.14 cache option & webmaster empowerment though async configuration
body:
> Disclaimer: this is something between a bug report, a feature request, and discussion about something out of scope for Nuxt 2, tried to provide as much information as possible to discuss about it. Hey, I'd like to talk about a pattern I like to use which allows configuration of the website settings through the CMS directly, helping it feel a bit more like WordPress (or others, in a good way), therefore empowering its final webmaster with great power (aKa not having your client / the marketing team reaching out to you two months later because they want to change the website's Google Analytics account, example) ## Problem Description Let's consider the following example with Google Analytics again (because I think that's the most obvious one): ```javascript /* nuxt.config.js */ module.exports = async () => { const settings = await getSettingsFromCMS(); console.log(settings); return { /* ... */ buildModules: [ ["@nuxtjs/google-analytics", { id: settings.analytics_id }] ], /* ... */ }; }; ``` The above works like a charm with Nuxt as this is (part of?) what asynchronous Nuxt configuration was meant for, although Nuxt 2.14 introduced [a new caching feature](https://nuxtjs.org/blog/nuxt-static-improvements#faster-static-deployments), allowing to skip the Webpack build of the website, so what's happening with this new feature on (default behavior)? 1. `$ nuxt generate` ran for a first time, generating everything as expected _(although the console log appears twice on the Webpack build part (?))_ and caching the Webpack build. 2. Settings are changed in the CMS (`analytics_id` is changed) 3. `$ nuxt generate` ran for a second time, taking advantage of the previously cached Webpack build, therefore skipping it because no code change occurred, build succeed but the new `analytics_id` value is not applied _everywhere (see below)_ because cache was used. Indeed, the Google Analytics module injects its internal Nuxt plugin at Webpack build time and "hard-code" the `id` value [here](https://github.com/nuxt-community/analytics-module/blob/master/lib/plugin.js#L6), so this value is part of the cached build now. On another hand if you forward our `settings` to Vue with `publicRuntimeConfig` and display it in a page you'll have the updated value each time as this part is injected on route generation (after Webpack build). > I know the Google Analytics module also makes use of the [`publicRuntimeConfig`](https://github.com/nuxt-community/analytics-module/blob/master/lib/plugin.js#L5) which is a suitable workaround here, but this module is just taken as example here as we can think of other settings giving the webmaster even more control over the website like choosing between Google Analytics & Google Tag Manager, enabling Sentry or not, changing the meta title template... possibilities look endless to me... I think you got the picture, if you want to fiddle with it, understand better what I talk about, you can download here a minimal reproduction:

✨ Reproduction Download Link ✨

## Current Workarounds ### Disabling cache (`nuxt.generate.cache = false`) **Pro:** Fixes the whole problem **Con:** Cache is never leveraged ### Telling the webmaster to clear cache on settings change **Pro:** Works, theoretically **Con:** It's obscure, error-prone, and we all know how this will end up: _"Heh I changed my settings but they aren't taken into account, any idea?"_ ### Setting cache programmatically **Pro:** Sounds like a nice idea, we can think of something like that: ```javascript /* nuxt.config.js */ module.exports = async () => { const settings = await getSettingsFromCMS(); // Just think of something telling you if T setting

title: Supabase Authentication Token Cross-Instance Validation Issue
body:
# Bug report

<!-- 

⚠️ We receive a lot of bug reports which have already been solved or discussed. If you are looking for help, please try these first:

- Docs: https://docs.supabase.com
- Discussions: https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions
- Discord: https://discord.supabase.com

Before opening a bug report, please verify the following: 

-->

- [x ] I confirm this is a bug with Supabase, not with my own application. 
- [x ] I confirm I have searched the [Docs](https://docs.supabase.com), GitHub [Discussions](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions), and [Discord](https://discord.supabase.com). 



When a user has a valid Supabase authentication token from Instance A (e.g., Web App X), this token is being incorrectly accepted as valid by Instance B (a separate Web App with SUpabase Auth) without proper validation.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Log into Instance A
2. Access a separate Supabase application Instance B
3. The application accepts the authentication token from Instance A as valid, despite it being from a completely different Supabase instance

**Expected behavior:**
- Each Supabase instance should only accept tokens that were issued by that specific instance
- Tokens from other Supabase instances should be rejected as invalid
- The `auth.getUser()` and `auth.getSession()` methods should validate the token against the current instance

**Actual behavior:**
- Tokens from any Supabase instance are being accepted as valid
- `auth.getUser()` and `auth.getSession()` return successful responses with tokens from different instances
- This allows users to potentially authenticate into applications using tokens from completely unrelated Supabase instances

**Security Implications:**
- Cross-instance token acceptance could lead to unauthorized access
- Applications cannot reliably verify that a token was issued by their specific Supabase instance
- Potential for session hijacking if users have active sessions on multiple Supabase instances

**Library:**
-Supabase JS (Client SDK, not SSR)

title: Nested Validation Errors in Pydantic Models Do Not Propagate Properly
body:
### Initial Checks

- [X] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

When creating nested Pydantic models, validation errors from an inner model are not fully propagated to the outer model in certain scenarios, especially when exceptions are re-raised or wrapped during outer model validation. This behavior makes it difficult to debug issues in complex model hierarchies.

In the example below, an InnerModel fails validation because a field does not meet its constraints. However, when this failure occurs during the validation of an OuterModel, the error message only reflects the outer validation failure, potentially obscuring the root cause.



### Example Code

```Python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError, validator

class InnerModel(BaseModel):
    age: int

    @validator("age")
    def check_age_must_be_positive(cls, value):
        if value <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Age must be positive")
        return value

class OuterModel(BaseModel):
    name: str

    @validator("name")
    def create_inner_model(cls, value):
        # Attempt to create the InnerModel with invalid data
        # Intentionally use a negative age to trigger an error
        InnerModel(age=-1)
        return value

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        OuterModel(name="Testing")
    except ValidationError as e:
        print("----- Python Exception Output -----")
        print(e)            # Human-readable error
        print("----- JSON Error Output -----")
        print(e.json())     # JSON-formatted error
```

title: PostgresDsn required host - should be optional
body:
### Initial Checks

- [X] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

There is assumption in the code that host is required parameter in PostgresDsn. 

I do think there a number of cases where you won't submit `host` as a parameter as it's not required in many PG drivers. In Google Cloud you can connect in Cloud Run and other environment via unix socket file never going via host network. Example: https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/python-docs-samples/blob/main/cloud-sql/postgres/sqlalchemy/connect_unix.py#L36-L37 
```python
        # postgresql+pg8000://<db_user>:<db_pass>@/<db_name>
        #                         ?unix_sock=<INSTANCE_UNIX_SOCKET>/.s.PGSQL.5432
        # Note: Some drivers require the `unix_sock` query parameter to use a different key.
        # For example, 'psycopg2' uses the path set to `host` in order to connect successfully.
        sqlalchemy.engine.url.URL.create(
            drivername="postgresql+pg8000",
            username=db_user,
            password=db_pass,
            database=db_name,
            query={"unix_sock": f"{unix_socket_path}/.s.PGSQL.5432"},
        ),
```
The URI part `postgresql+pg8000://<db_user>:<db_pass>@/<db_name>?unix_sock=<INSTANCE_UNIX_SOCKET>/.s.PGSQL.5432` doesn't have at all host and that is ok for a lot of drivers.

title: 'Url' type casts left around when serializing model to a dictionary
body:
### Initial Checks

- [X] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

When serializing a model using URLs back to a dictionary, provided the URLs are properly represented, and validated using any of the network URL types, `Url/AnyUrl/HttpUrl` are explicitly formatted as type casts to the serialized dictionary  (depending on the exact pydantic v2 release)  which makes it hard to deterministically compare data as plain dictionaries in unit tests.
I used the word "deterministically" because prior pydantic  2.10.2 it seems like all URL types where formatted as `Url(<url>)`, but after **2.10.2** where there were adjustments to the URL validation constraints the actual types are honored in the serialized dictionary.
I don't think the type casts should be dumped to a serialized dictionary once a model has been successfully validated, making it completely transparent to the user what the model does/did in the background.

[1] https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/serialization/#modelmodel_dump

### Example Code

```Python
from typing import Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, AnyUrl
from pprint import pprint


class SubModel(BaseModel):
    bar: AnyUrl
    baz: int = 1


class MainModel(BaseModel):
    foo: Optional[str] = None
    submodels: list[SubModel] = []


m = {
    "foo": "foo",
    "submodels":
        [
            {"bar": "https://example.com"},
            {"bar": "http://www.example.com/path", "baz": 2}
        ],
}

pprint(MainModel.model_validate(m).model_dump())


>>> python3 test.py
{'foo': 'foo',
 'submodels': [{'bar': AnyUrl('https://example.com/'), 'baz': 1},
               {'bar': AnyUrl('http://www.example.com/path'), 'baz': 2}]}
```

title: Avoid Models Field Caching
body:
The TestModel does not refresh the `ModelStack` instance whenever the `current_model` changes. As a result, the `TestModel` fails to validate input data correctly when `current_model` is dynamically updated. Specifically, updating `current_model` from `Model` to `Model2` should allow the `TestModel` to use `Model2` for validation, but it continues to reference `Model1`.

**Code to reproduce:**
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Model1(BaseModel):
    name: str

class Model2(BaseModel):
    numbers: list[int]

current_model = Model1

class ModelStack:
    def __getattr__(self, item):
        return getattr(current_model, item)

class TestModel(BaseModel):
    submodel: ModelStack()

print(TestModel.model_validate({"submodel": {"name": "John Doe"}}))  # Expected: submodel=Model1(name='John Doe')

current_model = Model2
print(TestModel.model_validate({"submodel": {"numbers": [1, 2, 3]}}))  # Expected: submodel=Model2(numbers=[1, 2, 3])
# Actual output:
# 
# pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for TestModel
# submodel.name
#   Field required [type=missing, input_value={'numbers': [1, 2, 3]}, input_type=dict]
#     For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.9/v/missing
```

**Expected Behavior:** The `TestModel` should refresh its `ModelStack` submodel whenever `current_model` is updated. Therefore, after updating `current_model` to `Model2`, `TestModel` should recognize it and validate `{"submodel": {"numbers": [1, 2, 3]}}` correctly.

**Actual Behavior:** The `TestModel` does not refresh the submodel and continues to expect the fields defined in `Model1`, resulting in a validation error.

Pydantic: 2.9.2

title: `model_dump` dict stays attached to the model's references for custom classes
body:
### Initial Checks

- [X] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

It appears that `model_dump` creates a 'shallow' dump of the model: if one of the model attributes is a custom class containing mutable data, then changing the data in a dump of the model will also change it in the original model.

This feels unexpected as one would expect a 'dump' to be a record (e.g. [core dump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Core_dump), or [database dump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database_dump)) of the model at the time of the dump, and changing that record should not change the original model. I think that either `model_dump` should do 'deep' dumps by default to actually create a dictionary record (and `vars(model)` can be used for `shallow` dumps) or `model_dump` should have an optional `deep` parameter.

A current workaround for this is if you use `model.model_copy(deep=True).model_dump()`, then it works as expected.

### Example Code

```Python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class MyClass:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = data

class Model(BaseModel, arbitrary_types_allowed=True):
    var: MyClass

m = Model(var=MyClass([1, 2, 3]))
md = m.model_dump()
md['var'].data.pop()

# will give a result of [1, 2], so 3 has been popped from the model as well
print(m.var.data)
```

title: Allow customizing `loc` for model validators
body:
### Initial Checks

- [X] I have searched Google & GitHub for similar requests and couldn't find anything
  - (I have actually searched GH for similar requests and found #8092 and #9686, which touch upon this.) 
- [X] I have read and followed [the docs](https://docs.pydantic.dev) and still think this feature is missing

### Description

Given something like

```python
from typing import Literal, Self

import pydantic


class ServiceConfiguration(pydantic.BaseModel):
    access_key: str | None = None
    endpoint_url: pydantic.HttpUrl | Literal[""] | None = None

    @pydantic.model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_access_key_format(self) -> Self:
        if self.endpoint_url:  # Customized endpoint, do not check format.
            return self
        if self.access_key and not self.access_key.islower():
            raise ValueError(
                "Access key must be lower case. The default service does not tolerate shouting and loud noises.")
        return self


ServiceConfiguration.model_validate({"access_key": "VERYVERYLOUD"})
```

I would like to be able to customize the `loc` for the resulting error to be `'access_key'`, since the error is actually an error in that field, so I can eventually format the `pydantic.ValidationError` to neatly nested JSON with a reference to the actual field that had the issue. 

Some ideas for implementing this:

* Allow setting `field_name` for `model_validator()`s too, and use it for `loc`. Not very dynamic, maybe overloads the `field_name` name too much?
* Read a `loc` or `_pydantic_loc` or similar field off the exception user code raises, use it if available. Simple enough, but also relies on the implicit magic that this is a thing, and creating such an exception is not idiomatic (and may not be possible, if the exception class has e.g. slots):
  ```python
  exc = ValueError("No shouting!")
  exc.loc = ("access_key",)
  raise exc
  ```
* A Pydantic-specific extra error info wrapper exception type?
  ```python
  raise pydantic.ErrorWithContext(ValueError("No shouting!"), loc=("access_key", ))
  ```
  Feels pretty elegant, should be easy to peel off and process in the Rust core code?
* Add `loc` to [`PydanticCustomError`](https://docs.pydantic.dev/dev/api/pydantic_core/#pydantic_core.PydanticCustomError)?

body:
### Initial Checks

### Description

When using `HttpUrl` for field validation it should I genenrate the URL type when doing `model_dump()`?

When I have schema the accept HttpUrl for one of the field and when I pass the data to sqlalchemy via `model_dump()`, sqlalchemy throws error that it can't accept `pydantic_core._pydantic_core.Url` type instead of string.

SImple solution can be using `.model_dump('json')` but this will convert datetime like objects to string which is wrong according to schema and sqlalchemy.

So, what should be best approach for this?

from pydantic import BaseModel, HttpUrl

title: Field parsing order is not taken into account for Decimal | str
body:
### Initial Checks

- [X] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

First of all thanks for the amazing library 👏 

I have observed a change in behavior confirmed in 2.9.0 and 2.9.1 compared to 2.8.2.

The type order for Decimal and string in not taken into account. I haven't checked for other types that could behave the same.

# How it used to behave
Having a field annotated `Decimal | str` used to first try to parse to `Decimal` in `2.8.2` then to `str` if the string was not a valid Decimal (e.g. `"5%"`) .

# How it now behaves
In 2.9.0 and 2.9.1, it does not try to parse to Decimal, or at least it always parses to str if the input is a string.

# Changelog
I checked the changelog for 2.9.0 and didn't see anything directly mentioning this change but may have missed something 😕 

There is a tiny change mentionning `Decimal` but it does not look related.
> Move decimal.Decimal validation to _generate_schema.py by @sydney-runkle in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/9977


With a little guidance, I'm up to try and fix this 🙂 

### Example Code

```Python
from decimal import Decimal

from pydantic import BaseModel

class Cover(BaseModel):
  deductible: Decimal | str

cover = Cover.model_validate({"deductible": "0"})

assert isinstance(cover.deductible, Decimal) # evaluates to "False"

title: Potential Issue with model_dump_json in Pydantic: Inconsistent Output Compared to json.dumps
body:
### Initial Checks

- [X] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Hello,

I have encountered a potential issue with the model_dump_json function in Pydantic. Specifically, the JSON string returned by model_dump_json may differ from the output of Python's built-in json.dumps in subtle ways, such as the presence or absence of spaces after colons. This inconsistency can lead to failures in processes that rely on exact string matches, such as MD5 hash-based encryption verification.

Problem Description:

When serializing a Pydantic model to JSON using the model_dump_json method, the resulting JSON string may include or omit spaces after colons differently compared to the json.dumps method. In scenarios where JSON strings must match exactly (e.g., for generating MD5 hashes for encryption verification), these differences can cause validation to fail.

Steps to Reproduce:

Create a Pydantic model.
Serialize the model to JSON using both model_dump_json and json.dumps with specific formatting options.
Compare the resulting JSON strings.


Expected Behavior:

The JSON output from model_dump_json should be consistent with the output from json.dumps(example.dict(), separators=(',', ':')), ensuring no spaces appear after colons, or providing options to control the formatting. This consistency is crucial for processes that depend on exact string matches.

Actual Behavior:

In some cases, the JSON outputs are not identical, particularly regarding spaces after colons. This discrepancy can cause failures in MD5 hash generation and other validation processes that require exact JSON string matches.

Impact:

This inconsistency can cause issues in systems relying on JSON-based encryption or signature verification, where the serialized JSON string must precisely match the string used at the time of signing or encrypting.

### Example Code

```Python
from pydantic import BaseModel
import json

class ExampleModel(BaseModel):
    key1: str
    key2: int

example = ExampleModel(key1="value1", key2=123)

pydantic_json = example.model_dump_json()
standard_json = json.dumps(example.model_dump())

print("Pydantic JSON:", pydantic_json)
print("Standard JSON:", standard_json)

Thanks for the best framework in Python and generally ❤️ Basically, passing a background task to a custom response overwrites any other tasks added to the injected `BackgroundTasks`. I'm not sure this is considered a bug, but I think it's confusing and can at least be clarified in the [Return a Response Directly](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/response-directly/) docs, for example. Other solutions can be actually changing this behavior (I guess that's a breaking change), or printing a warning/throwing [throwing is also a breaking change] if both mechanisms are used at once. But I can't imagine a user desiring this behavior. To be clear, this tripped us up when we couldn't figure out why some of our tasks were being swallowed. I'd be happy to work on either solution, obviously adding a docs pr would be the easiest first step. ### Operating System macOS ### Operating System Details _No response_ ### FastAPI Version 0.97.0 ### Pydantic Version 1.10.7 ### Python Version 3.9 ### Additional Context _No response_

Pydantic provides `RootModel` (instead of `BaseModel`) precisely to implement types with rich validation based on native types like `list` or `str` (instead of the more typical object/dict). Types built with `RootModel` do not seem to work as query params, *even if it is functionally equivalent* to a simple type like `str`. Furthermore, we cannot force them to work as query params with `Query()` annotations either. **NOTE:** the example is overly simplified, my RootModel-derived types do much more in terms of validation. ### Operating System macOS ### Operating System Details _No response_ ### FastAPI Version 0.108.0 ### Pydantic Version 2.5.3 ### Python Version Python 3.11.4 ### Additional Context I am not sure this is possible, but I would like for FastAPI to understand RootModel derived types, if the root type is one of the types that can be used as query param, then it should work as such. The workaround in my case is to use `str` parameters in my FastAPI calls then manually convert to the rich Pydantic type that does validation. Which kind of defeats the purpose of FastAPI rich type annotations.

DependedValue: TypeAlias = Annotated[int, Depends(some_value)] # This won't work. # type DependedValue = Annotated[int, Depends(some_value)] @app.get('/') async def get_with_dep(value: DependedValue) -> str: print(f'{type(value) = !r}') print(f'{value = !r}') assert isinstance(value, int), '`value` should be an integer.' assert value == 123, '`value` should be 123.' return f'value: {value}' ``` ### Description When using the method in line 15: ```python DependedValue: TypeAlias = Annotated[int, Depends(some_value)] ``` to declare a type alias, FastAPI correctly interprets it and fills the `value` with `123` for `get_with_dep`. class OAuth2PasswordRequestForm:
    """
    This is a dependency class, use it like:
        @app.post("/login")
        def login(form_data: OAuth2PasswordRequestForm = Depends()):
            data = form_data.parse()
            print(data.username)
            print(data.password)
            for scope in data.scopes:
                print(scope)
            if data.client_id:
                print(data.client_id)
            if data.client_secret:
                print(data.client_secret)
            return data
    It creates the following Form request parameters in your endpoint:
    grant_type: the OAuth2 spec says it is required and MUST be the fixed string "password".
        Nevertheless, this dependency class is permissive and allows not passing it. If you want to enforce it,
        use instead the OAuth2PasswordRequestFormStrict dependency.
    username: username string. The OAuth2 spec requires the exact field name "username".
    password: password string. The OAuth2 spec requires the exact field name "password".
    scope: Optional string. Several scopes (each one a string) separated by spaces. E.g.
        "items:read items:write users:read profile openid"
    client_id: optional string. OAuth2 recommends sending the client_id and client_secret (if any)
        using HTTP Basic auth, as: client_id:client_secret
    client_secret: optional string. OAuth2 recommends sending the client_id and client_secret (if any)
        using HTTP Basic auth, as: client_id:client_secret
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        grant_type: str = Form(default=None, regex="password"),
        username: str = Form(),
        password: str = Form(default=None), # THE ONLY CHANGE
        scope: str = Form(default=""),
        client_id: Optional[str] = Form(default=None),
        client_secret: Optional[str] = Form(default=None),

### Description

First of all, huge fan, big thanks for this awesome library ❤️ 

* I am comparing FastAPI vs Flask "under load" using [Apache Jmeter](https://jmeter.apache.org/). Jmeter allows me to issue 100 parallel requests to the `/load` endpoint of the above FastAPI app. It does so by generating 100 threads within 0.01 seconds that then issue the GET request.
* Jmeter times the roundtrip latency from each thread and generates a report
* The Jmeter report for both the FastAPI and the Flask app can be seen below:
      FastAPI took on average `3727.85ms` per request
      Flask took on average `2072.45ms` per request
* Somehow I expected FastAPI to be... well "faster". Please see the Github repo [here](https://github.com/MaxHoefl/demo-api-perf) to reproduce the findings

### Example Code

```python
def valid_token(                                                                        
    scopes: SecurityScopes,                                                             
    access_token: str = Depends(access_token_scheme),                                   
) -> Token:
    ...
    return Token(...)

@router.patch("/users/{username}")                                                                                   
async def some_endpoint(                                                          
    data: Data,                                                     
    token = Security(valid_token, scopes=["some-scope"]),                         
    username: str = Path(title="User username"),                                        
):                                                                                      
    if username == token.TYPO_HERE.username:    
        raise HTTPException(403, detail="Not allowed to change own user")
```


### Description

`mypy` is completely happy with this code, which, as far as I understand is because the return type of `valid_token` is not propagated through the `Security` wrapper.


### Wanted Solution

Some clever type hints for `Security` so that the callable return type is visible to `mypy`.

### Wanted Code

```python
pass
```


### Alternatives

The alternative is to manually type every endpoint that uses `Security`, which, as I discovered today is error prone:

```py
def valid_token(...) -> SystemToken: ...

@router.patch("/users/{username}")                                                                                   
async def some_endpoint(                                                          
    data: Data,                                                     
    token: UserToken = Security(valid_token, scopes=["some-scope"]),                         
    username: str = Path(title="User username"),                                        
):                                                                                      
    # Oops! token is actually SystemToken, not UserToken
    if username == token.username:    
        raise HTTPException(403, detail="Not allowed to change own user")
```

title: `explicit-f-string-type-conversion (RUF010)` incorrectly suggested when string type is supplied
body:
### Summary

When an f-string specifies the string type, `str()` is sometimes required if the variable is not already a string, else the expression errors:

```python
x = 3
f"{str(x):10s}"  # Ruff warning: Use explicit conversion flag
f"{x:10s}"       # ValueError: Unknown format code 's' for object of type 'int'
```

Ruff should not make the suggestion when `x` is not a string and the string type is specified via `:*s` in the f-string type specifier.

title: The Ruff VS Code extension uses the wrong `ruff.toml` file
body:
### Summary

I have a bunch of projects that do not follow the PEP8 formatting rules (longer lines and non-standard indentation). For these I have made custom `ruff.toml` file that is referred to in the respective `pyproject.toml` files like this:
```
[tool.ruff]
extend = "~/projects/notpep8/ruff.toml"
```

The file structure is like this:
```
~/projects --- notpep8 -+- ruff.toml
                        |
                        +- proj -+- pyproject.toml
                        |        |
                        |        +- src --- example.py
```

This works perfectly when running `ruff check` from the command line in the respective project directories. 

However when running ruff in VS Code using that Astral ruff extension, this seems to be ignored and instead the global PEP8 compliant `ruff.toml` file is used. This of course produces loads of errors.

I have tried several different things:

- Made an intentional error in pyproject.toml. This is detected so ruff does look at the file.
- Added `"ruff.configuration": "~/projects/notpep8/ruff.toml"` lines to the various `settings.json` files. That does not change anything.

As far as I can see from the attached log file ruff does seem to load the local `ruff.toml` file - and then it loads the global one immediately afterwards.

title: Option to use `code:name` for rules and output
body:
I currently keep a rather lengthy list of rules, which I order as:

```toml
lint.ignore = [
	# ...
    # PLR: Pylint - Refactor
    "PLR0402", # manual-from-import: some helpful comment or motivation for rule
    "PLR5501", # collapsible-else-if
    # PT: flake8-pytest-style
    "PT001", # pytest-fixture-incorrect-parentheses-style
    "PT023", # pytest-incorrect-mark-parentheses-style
    "PT026", # pytest-use-fixtures-without-parameters
	# ...
]
```

Which means when I add rules I would like to have both the code and the name. I find the logical ordering that comes with the codes to be helpful in arranging the configuration file, but also want the name as a hint to what the rule is about.

Currently when a rule is violated, the LSP defaults to showing only the name of the rule, not the code. This can be changed with the [`output-prefer-rule-codes` setting](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/settings/#output-prefer-rule-codes), but this means I don't get hints as to what the rule is about.

I think it would be helpful if rules to be specified as any of:
- `code`, i.e. `COM821`
- `name`, i.e. `missing-trailing-comma`
- `code:name`, i.e. `COM821:missing-trailing-comma`

I realise that having many equivalent ways of specifying a rule is perhaps not desirable, but I would argue that the benefits outweigh the negatives here, with the benefits of the `code:name` option being:
- Easy to identify both category of rule (via code) and nature of rule (via name)
- Neater configuration files for those that prefer to have both code and name listed
- Would make transitioning rule names easier (https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/27011)
  - If `COM821` changed name from `missing-trailing-comma` to `disallow-missing-trailing-comma` (perhaps a bad example), the user would immediately know the new rule `code:name` since the code would not have changed.

This would likely also mean changing the `output-prefer-rule-codes` setting into something like `output-preferred-rule-format`, which would then take one of `code`, `name`, `code:name`, or similar.

The configuration above would then be:
```
lint.ignore = [
	# ...
    # PLR: Pylint - Refactor
    "PLR0402:manual-from-import", # some helpful comment or motivation for rule
    "PLR5501:collapsible-else-if",
    # PT: flake8-pytest-style
    "PT001:pytest-fixture-incorrect-parentheses-style", 
    "PT023:pytest-incorrect-mark-parentheses-style",
    "PT026:pytest-use-fixtures-without-parameters",
	# ...
]
```

quote-style = "double"
